questions.question: In the process of charging of a capacitor, the current produced between the plates of the capacitor is (where symbols have their usual meanings): (A) $\mu_{0}\frac{d\phi_{E}}{dt}$ (B) $\frac{1}{\mu_{0}}\frac{d\phi_{E}}{dt}$ (C) $\varepsilon_{0}\frac{d\phi_{E}}{dt}$ (D) $\frac{1}{\varepsilon_{0}}\frac{d\phi_{E}}{dt}$
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
The displacement current is $I_{d}=\varepsilon_{0}\frac{d\phi_{E}}{dt}$, which equals the conduction current between the plates.

questions.question: $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ represent the electric and the magnetic field of an electromagnetic wave respectively. The direction of propagation of the wave is along (A) $\vec{B}$ (B) $\vec{E}$ (C) $\vec{E} \times\vec{B}$ (D) $\vec{B} \times\vec{E}$
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
The wave propagates along $\vec{E}\times\vec{B}$, since $\vec{E}$, $\vec{B}$ and the direction of propagation form a right-handed mutually perpendicular set.

questions.question: The ratio of the magnitudes of the electric field and magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave is (A) $1$ (B) $\frac{1}{c}$ (C) $c$ (D) $c^{2}$
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
For an electromagnetic wave, $\frac{E}{B}=c$, the speed of light.

questions.question: An electromagnetic wave is produced by a charge (A) moving with a constant velocity (B) moving with a constant speed parallel to a magnetic field (C) moving with an acceleration (D) at rest
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
Only an accelerated charge produces a time-varying electric and magnetic field that radiates as an electromagnetic wave.

questions.question: The electromagnetic radiations used to kill germs in water purifiers are called: (A) Infrared waves (B) X-rays (C) Gamma rays (D) Ultraviolet rays
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
Ultraviolet rays have germicidal properties and are used to kill bacteria in water purifiers.

questions.question: Electromagnetic waves of wavelength of the order of a few meters were first produced and detected in the laboratory by: (A) J.C. Maxwell (B) J.C. Bose (C) H.R. Hertz (D) G. Marconi
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
H.R. Hertz first produced and detected electromagnetic waves of wavelength of a few metres in the laboratory, confirming Maxwell's theory.

questions.question: A capacitor is charged by a battery. Between the plates, during process of charging: (A) only displacement current exists. (B) only conduction current exists. (C) both displacement current and conduction current exist. (D) no current exists.
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
Conduction current flows in the connecting wires while displacement current, due to the changing electric flux, flows between the plates; together they form a continuous current.

questions.question: The electromagnetic waves used in radar systems are: (A) Infrared waves (B) Ultraviolet rays (C) Microwaves (D) X-rays
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
Microwaves are used in radar systems because their short wavelength allows accurate detection of the direction and range of objects like aircraft and ships.

questions.question: Name the electromagnetic waves also known as ’heat waves’. (A) Radio waves (B) Microwaves (C) X-rays (D) Infrared waves
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
Infrared waves are called heat waves because they are readily absorbed by water and other substances, producing a heating effect.

questions.question: Which one of the following electromagnetic radiation has the least wavelength? (A) Gamma rays (B) Microwaves (C) Visible light (D) X-rays
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Gamma rays have the highest frequency and hence the least wavelength among the given electromagnetic radiations.

questions.question: Choose the correct option related to wavelengths $(\lambda)$ of different parts of electromagnetic spectrum. (A) $\lambda_{X}$-rays $< \lambda^{micro waves} < \lambda^{visible}$ (B) $\lambda_{visible} > \lambda_{X}$-rays $> \lambda^{radio waves}$ (C) $\lambda_{radio waves} > \lambda_{visible} > \lambda_{X}$-rays (D) $\lambda_{visible} < \lambda_{micro waves} < \lambda_{radio waves} < \lambda_{X}$-rays
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
In the electromagnetic spectrum, wavelength increases from X-rays to visible light to radio waves, i.e., $\lambda_{radio} > \lambda_{visible} > \lambda_{X-rays}$.

questions.question: What oscillates in an electromagnetic wave of frequency $10$ MHz?
questions.answer:
Option: Electric and magnetic fields oscillate.
In an electromagnetic wave, mutually perpendicular electric field $\vec{E}$ and magnetic field $\vec{B}$ oscillate sinusoidally in time and space, perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation.

questions.question: Name the electromagnetic radiation used for killing germs in water purifiers.
questions.answer: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation is used for killing germs in water purifiers.

questions.question: Write the mathematical form of Ampere-Maxwell circuital law.
questions.answer: The Ampere-Maxwell circuital law is $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 I_c + \mu_0\varepsilon_0 \dfrac{d\phi_E}{dt}$, where $I_c$ is the conduction current and $\mu_0\varepsilon_0 \dfrac{d\phi_E}{dt}$ is the displacement current.

questions.question: How is displacement current produced between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor during charging?
questions.answer: As the capacitor charges, the electric field $E$ between the plates changes with time, and this time-varying electric flux $\phi_E$ gives rise to a displacement current $I_d = \varepsilon_0 \dfrac{d\phi_E}{dt}$, which is equal in magnitude to the conduction current in the connecting wires.

questions.question: Differentiate between conduction current and displacement current.
questions.answer:
Conduction current: it arises due to actual flow of electrons/charges in a conductor, given by $I_c = \dfrac{dq}{dt}$, and exists only where a conductor is present.
Displacement current: it arises due to a time-varying electric field (flux) even in vacuum or between capacitor plates, given by $I_d = \varepsilon_0 \dfrac{d\phi_E}{dt}$.
Both together maintain continuity of current in circuits containing capacitors and are equal in magnitude during steady charging/discharging.

questions.question: Displacement current exists only when (A) electric field is changing. (B) magnetic field is changing. (C) electric field is not changing. (D) magnetic field is not changing.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Displacement current $I_d = \varepsilon_0 \dfrac{d\phi_E}{dt}$ exists only when the electric flux, i.e., the electric field, is changing with time.

questions.question: Electromagnetic waves used as a diagnostic tool in medicine are (A) X-rays. (B) ultraviolet rays. (C) infrared radiation. (D) ultrasonic waves.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
X-rays have high penetrating power and are used to image bones and internal body structures for diagnosis.

questions.question: A welder wears special glasses to protect his eyes mostly from the harmful effect of (A) very intense visible light. (B) infrared radiation. (C) ultraviolet rays. (D) microwaves.
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
Welding arcs emit intense ultraviolet rays, which can damage the eyes, so special UV-protective glasses are worn.

questions.question: In a travelling plane electromagnetic wave, which of the following have zero average value? (A) Magnetic energy and electric energy (B) Magnetic field and electric field (C) Magnetic energy and magnetic field (D) Electric energy and electric field
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
The electric field $\vec{E}$ and magnetic field $\vec{B}$ vary sinusoidally in time, so their average value over a complete cycle is zero, whereas the associated energy densities (proportional to $E^2$ and $B^2$) have non-zero average values.

questions.question: Mention the contribution of Indian physicist J.C. Bose in the production of electromagnetic waves.
questions.answer: J.C. Bose generated and studied electromagnetic waves of millimetre wavelength, demonstrating their production and detection well before their practical use in wireless communication.

questions.question: Write one use of the electromagnetic waves of frequency range from $10^{16}$ Hz to $10^{20}$ Hz.
questions.answer: X-rays (frequency range $10^{16}$ Hz to $10^{20}$ Hz) are used for medical diagnosis, such as imaging bones and detecting fractures.

questions.question: Which physical quantity associated with an electromagnetic wave does not change when it propagates from one medium into another medium?
questions.answer: The frequency of an electromagnetic wave does not change when it passes from one medium to another; only its speed and wavelength change.

questions.question: Name the electromagnetic radiations which may cause sunburn. Write their wavelength range.
questions.answer: Ultraviolet radiations cause sunburn, with wavelength range about $400$ nm to $1$ nm.

questions.question: An A.C. source with variable frequency is connected to a parallel plate capacitor. How will the displacement current be affected with the decrease in frequency of the source?
questions.answer:
The displacement current $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$ depends on the rate of change of electric flux, which decreases as frequency decreases.
So the displacement current decreases as the frequency of the source is decreased.

questions.question: Depict the fields diagram of an electromagnetic wave propagating along positive $X$-axis with its electric field along $Y$ -axis.
questions.answer:
Since the wave propagates along the $X$-axis with $\vec{E}$ along $Y$-axis, the magnetic field $\vec{B}$ must be along the $Z$-axis, as $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$ gives the direction of propagation.
The diagram shows sinusoidal $E_y$ and $B_z$ curves, in phase, varying along $X$, mutually perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation.

questions.question: Which part of the electromagnetic spectrum is used in RADAR? Give its frequency range. OR How are electromagnetic waves produced by accelerating charges?
questions.answer: Microwaves are used in RADAR, with frequency range from about $10^9$ Hz to $10^{12}$ Hz.

questions.question: The small ozone layer on top of the stratosphere is crucial for human survival. Why? OR Illustrate by giving suitable examples, how you can show that electromagnetic waves carry both energy and momentum.
questions.answer: The ozone layer absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun, preventing it from reaching the Earth's surface and damaging living tissue and DNA.

questions.question: Name the electromagnetic radiations used for (a) water purification, and (b) eye surgery.
questions.answer:
(a) Ultraviolet radiation is used for water purification.
(b) Ultraviolet (excimer laser) radiation is used for eye surgery (e.g., LASIK).

questions.question: How is the speed of em-waves in vacuum determined by the electric and magnetic fields?
questions.answer: The speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum is given by $c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \epsilon_0}}$, determined by the permeability $\mu_0$ and permittivity $\epsilon_0$ of free space.

questions.question: Write the expression for speed of electromagnetic waves in a medium of electrical permittivity $\varepsilon$ and magnetic permeability $\mu$.
questions.answer: $v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu \varepsilon}}$

questions.question: Do electromagnetic waves carry energy and momentum?
questions.answer: Yes, electromagnetic waves carry both energy and momentum, and can exert pressure (radiation pressure) on a surface they strike.

questions.question: Write the relation for the speed of electromagnetic waves in terms of the amplitudes of electric and magnetic fields.
questions.answer: $c = \dfrac{E_0}{B_0}$, the ratio of the amplitudes of the electric and magnetic fields equals the speed of light.

questions.question: In which directions do the electric and magnetic field vectors oscillate in an electromagnetic wave propagating along the x-axis?
questions.answer: The electric field vector oscillates along the y-axis and the magnetic field vector oscillates along the z-axis, both perpendicular to the direction of propagation (x-axis) and to each other.

questions.question: In which situation is there a displacement current but no conduction current?
questions.answer: Inside the gap between the plates of a charging or discharging capacitor, where no charge actually flows but the electric flux is changing.

questions.question: To which part of the electromagnetic spectrum does a wave of frequency $5 \times 10^{19}$ Hz belong?
questions.answer: Gamma rays, since frequencies of the order $10^{18}$-$10^{22}$ Hz correspond to this highest-energy part of the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.question: A capacitor has been charged by a dc source. What are the magnitudes of conduction and displacement currents, when it is fully charged?
questions.answer: Both the conduction current and the displacement current are zero, since no charge flows and the electric field between the plates is no longer changing.

questions.question: Name the part of electromagnetic spectrum whose wavelength lies in the range of $10^{-10}$ m. Give its one use.
questions.answer: X-rays; they are used in medical diagnosis to detect fractures and abnormalities in bones.

questions.question: What are the directions of electric and magnetic field vectors relative to each other and relative to the direction of propagation of electromagnetic waves?
questions.answer: The electric field vector, the magnetic field vector, and the direction of propagation are mutually perpendicular to one another.

questions.question: Name the physical quantity which remains same for microwaves of wavelength $1$ mm and $^{\circ}$ UV radiations of $1600$ A in vacuum.
questions.answer: Speed (equal to the speed of light $c$ in vacuum), since all electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in vacuum regardless of wavelength.

questions.question: Name the electromagnetic waves, which (i) maintain the Earth’s warmth and (ii) are used in aircraft navigation.
questions.answer:
(i) Infrared rays maintain the Earth's warmth (greenhouse effect).
(ii) Microwaves are used in aircraft navigation (radar).

questions.question: A plane electromagnetic wave travels in vacuum along $z$-direction. What can you say about the direction of electric and magnetic field vectors?
questions.answer: The electric field vector $\vec{E}$ and magnetic field vector $\vec{B}$ are mutually perpendicular to each other and both are perpendicular to the direction of propagation ($z$-axis), i.e., they lie in the $xy$-plane.

questions.question: Which part of electromagnetic spectrum has largest penetrating power?
questions.answer: Gamma rays have the largest penetrating power due to their highest frequency and hence highest photon energy among electromagnetic waves.

questions.question: Write the following radiations in ascending order in respect of their frequencies: X-rays, microwaves, UV rays and radio waves.
questions.answer: Ascending order of frequency: radio waves $<$ microwaves $<$ UV rays $<$ X-rays.

questions.question: Name the EM waves used for studying crystal structure of solids. What is its frequency range?
questions.answer:
X-rays are used for studying the crystal structure of solids, since their wavelength is comparable to interatomic spacing.
Their frequency range is about $3 \times 10^{16}$ Hz to $3 \times 10^{19}$ Hz.

questions.question: Name the part of the electromagnetic spectrum of wavelength $10^{-2}$ m and mention its one application.
questions.answer:
A wavelength of $10^{-2}$ m corresponds to microwaves.
Application: used in radar systems for aircraft navigation and in microwave ovens for cooking.

questions.question: Identify the part of the electromagnetic spectrum to which the following wavelengths belong: (i) $1 mm$ (ii) $10^{-11} m$.
questions.answer:
(i) $1$ mm wavelength belongs to the microwave region.
(ii) $10^{-11}$ m wavelength belongs to the X-ray region.

questions.question: What is the name given to that part of electromagnetic spectrum which is used for taking photographs of earth under foggy conditions from great heights?
questions.answer: Infrared rays are used for taking photographs of the Earth under foggy conditions from great heights, since they are scattered less by fog and smoke than visible light.

questions.question: Consider an induced magnetic field due to changing electric field and an induced electric field due to changing magnetic field. Which one is more easily observed? Justify your answer.
questions.answer:
The induced electric field due to a changing magnetic field is more easily observed.
This is because the induced electric field forms closed loops and can drive a detectable current in a coil, as in electromagnetic induction (Faraday's law), $\oint \vec{E}\cdot d\vec{l} = -\dfrac{d\phi_B}{dt}$.
The induced magnetic field due to a changing electric field is extremely weak in ordinary laboratory situations, since it depends on $\epsilon_0$, which is very small, so it is difficult to detect directly.

questions.question: A plane electromagnetic wave propagates in vacuum along $x$-axis. (a) Give the direction of electric field and magnetic field vectors. (b) $E_{0}$ and $B_{0}$ are the magnitudes of electric and magnetic fields respectively in a plane electromagnetic wave. Find the ratio of energy densities of electric field and magnetic field.
questions.answer:
(a) The electric field vector $\vec{E}$ oscillates along the $y$-axis and the magnetic field vector $\vec{B}$ oscillates along the $z$-axis, both perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation (the $x$-axis).
(b) The energy density of the electric field is $u_E = \dfrac{1}{2}\epsilon_0 E_0^2$ and that of the magnetic field is $u_B = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{B_0^2}{\mu_0}$.
Since $E_0 = c B_0$ and $c^2 = \dfrac{1}{\mu_0 \epsilon_0}$, these two energy densities are equal, so $\dfrac{u_E}{u_B} = 1$.

questions.question: Identify the part of electromagnetic spectrum which is: (a) next to the lowest frequency end of the visible part of electromagnetic spectrum, and (b) produced by bombarding a metal target by high energy electrons. Give one use of each of them.
questions.answer:
(a) Ultraviolet rays are next to the lowest frequency (violet) end of the visible spectrum.
Use: sterilizing surgical instruments and killing germs.
(b) X-rays are produced by bombarding a metal target with high energy electrons.
Use: medical diagnosis (imaging bones/fractures).

questions.question: How are infrared waves produced? Why are these waves referred to as heat waves? Give any two uses of infrared waves.
questions.answer:
Infrared waves are produced by hot bodies and molecules due to vibrational and rotational motion of atoms.
They are called heat waves because they are readily absorbed by water molecules present in most materials, raising their thermal motion and heating them.
Uses: (i) In remote controls of TV, AC etc. (ii) For treatment of muscular strain and in physiotherapy.

questions.question: How are X-rays produced? Give any two uses of these.
questions.answer:
X-rays are produced when high energy electrons, accelerated through a large potential difference, strike a heavy metal target and are suddenly decelerated.
Uses: (i) In medical diagnosis to detect fractures and diseases. (ii) In engineering to study crystal structure and detect defects in materials.

questions.question: What is meant by the term ’displacement current’? Briefly explain how this current is different from a conduction current.
questions.answer:
Displacement current is the current that arises due to a time-varying electric field between the plates of a capacitor, given by $I_{d} = \varepsilon_{0}\dfrac{d\phi_{E}}{dt}$.
Unlike conduction current, which is due to actual flow of electrons in a conductor, displacement current does not involve motion of charges and exists even in vacuum, yet both produce the same magnetic effect and together maintain continuity of current in an ac circuit.

questions.question: (a) What is a displacement current? How is it different from a conduction current? OR (b) Write any two characteristics of an electromagnetic wave. Why are microwaves used in radar systems?
questions.answer:
(a) Displacement current is the current arising from a time-varying electric field, given by $I_{d} = \varepsilon_{0}\dfrac{d\phi_{E}}{dt}$.
Conduction current is due to actual flow of charges in a conductor, whereas displacement current involves no motion of charge and can exist even in vacuum; both together satisfy the continuity of current and produce magnetic fields.
OR
(b) (i) Electromagnetic waves are transverse in nature, with $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ mutually perpendicular and perpendicular to the direction of propagation.
(ii) They travel through vacuum with the speed of light, $c = 1/\sqrt{\mu_{0}\varepsilon_{0}}$.
Microwaves are used in radar because their short wavelength allows sharp beams and easy detection of reflected signals from targets, useful in tracking aircraft and ships.

questions.question: Identify the electromagnetic wave whose wavelengths range is from about (a) $10^{-12}$ m to about $10^{-8}$ m. (b) $10^{-3}$ m to about $10^{-1}$ m. Write one use of each.
questions.answer:
(a) Wavelength range $10^{-12}$ m to $10^{-8}$ m corresponds to X-rays.
Use: medical diagnosis of fractures and diseases.
(b) Wavelength range $10^{-3}$ m to $10^{-1}$ m corresponds to microwaves.
Use: in radar systems and for cooking (microwave ovens).

questions.question: Identify the electromagnetic radiation and write its wavelength range, which is used to kill germs in water purifier. Name the two sources of these radiations.
questions.answer:
Ultraviolet radiation, having wavelength range about $4 \times 10^{-7}$ m to $6 \times 10^{-10}$ m, is used to kill germs in water purifiers.
Sources: the Sun, and mercury vapour lamps (or special UV lamps).

questions.question: How are electromagnetic waves produced? Write their two characteristics.
questions.answer:
Electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerated (oscillating) charges, which create a time-varying electric field that in turn produces a time-varying magnetic field, and so on, the two regenerating each other.
Characteristics: (i) They are transverse waves in which $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ are mutually perpendicular and both perpendicular to the direction of propagation. (ii) They travel through vacuum with the speed of light, $c = 1/\sqrt{\mu_{0}\varepsilon_{0}}$.

questions.question: (a) The electric field of an electromagnetic wave is represented as $E_{x} = E_{0} \sin(\omega t + kz)$. (i) In which direction is the wave propagating? (ii) In which direction does the magnetic field oscillate? (b) Write two characteristics of electromagnetic waves.
questions.answer:
(a) (i) Since $E_x = E_0\sin(\omega t + kz)$ is a function of $(\omega t + kz)$, the wave propagates along the negative $z$-direction.
(ii) Since $\vec{E}$, $\vec{B}$ and the direction of propagation are mutually perpendicular, with $E_x$ along $x$ and propagation along $-z$, the magnetic field oscillates along the $y$-direction.
(b) (i) Electromagnetic waves are transverse, with $\vec{E} \perp \vec{B} \perp$ direction of propagation.
(ii) They travel through vacuum with speed $c = 1/\sqrt{\mu_{0}\varepsilon_{0}} = 3 \times 10^{8}$ m/s, and carry energy and momentum.

questions.question: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has (a) minimum wavelength, and (b) minimum frequency? Write one use of each of these two waves. Infrared waves, Microwaves, $\gamma$-rays and X-rays
questions.answer:
(a) $\gamma$-rays have the minimum wavelength.
Use: in medical science to destroy cancer cells (radiotherapy).
(b) Infrared waves have the minimum frequency (among the four listed).
Use: in remote controls and for physiotherapy treatment of muscular strain.

questions.question: How does an oscillating charge radiate an electromagnetic wave? Give the relation between the frequency of radiated wave and the frequency of oscillating charge. OR (a) Explain briefly the fact that electromagnetic waves carry energy. (b) Why do we not feel the pressure due to sunshine?
questions.answer:
An oscillating charge produces an oscillating electric field, which in turn produces an oscillating magnetic field; these mutually perpendicular, time-varying fields regenerate each other and propagate through space as an electromagnetic wave, even in vacuum.
The frequency of the radiated electromagnetic wave is equal to the frequency of oscillation of the charge.
OR
(a) Electromagnetic waves consist of oscillating electric and magnetic fields which carry energy, momentum and information as they travel through space, similar to a mechanical wave carrying energy; this energy is manifested as electromagnetic energy density $u = \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_0 E^2 + \frac{1}{2\mu_0}B^2$.
(b) We do not feel the pressure due to sunshine because the radiation pressure exerted by sunlight is extremely small compared to the forces we normally experience, so its effect is imperceptible to our senses.

questions.question: Gamma rays and radio waves travel with the same velocity in free space. Distinguish between them in terms of their origin and the main application.
questions.answer:
Gamma rays are produced by nuclear transitions/radioactive decay of atomic nuclei, whereas radio waves are produced by oscillating electric circuits (accelerating charges in conductors, e.g., antennas).
Gamma rays are used in the treatment of cancer and sterilization of medical equipment, while radio waves are used in radio and television broadcasting/communication.

questions.question: A capacitor made of two parallel plates, each of area ’ $A$’ and separation ’ $d$’ is charged by an external dc source. Show that during charging, the displacement current inside the capacitor is the same as the current charging the capacitor.
questions.answer:
The conduction current charging the capacitor is $I_c = \frac{dQ}{dt}$, where $Q = \epsilon_0 A E$ is the charge on the plates and $E$ is the electric field between them.
The displacement current is $I_d = \epsilon_0 \frac{d\Phi_E}{dt} = \epsilon_0 A \frac{dE}{dt} = \frac{d(\epsilon_0 A E)}{dt} = \frac{dQ}{dt}$.
Since $I_d = I_c$, the displacement current inside the capacitor equals the conduction current charging it, ensuring continuity of current in the circuit.

questions.question: How is the equation for Ampere’s circuital law modified in the presence of displacement current? Explain.
questions.answer:
Maxwell modified Ampere's circuital law by adding a displacement current term to account for the changing electric flux between capacitor plates, giving $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 (I_c + I_d)$, where $I_d = \epsilon_0 \frac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$.
This modification was needed because a changing electric field also produces a magnetic field, just as conduction current does, making the law consistent even in regions with no conduction current (like between capacitor plates) and ensuring charge continuity.

questions.question: How are electromagnetic waves produced by oscillating charges? What is the source of the energy associated with the em waves?
questions.answer:
An oscillating (accelerating) charge produces a time-varying electric field, which in turn generates a time-varying magnetic field; these mutually perpendicular oscillating fields regenerate each other and propagate through space as an electromagnetic wave.
The energy associated with the electromagnetic wave comes from the energy of the source that causes the charge to oscillate (i.e., the energy supplied to accelerate the charge).

questions.question: A parallel plate capacitor of plate area $A$ each and separation $d$, is being charged by an ac source. Show that the displacement current inside the capacitor is the same as the current charging the capacitor.
questions.answer:
The conduction current charging the capacitor is $I_c = \frac{dQ}{dt}$, where $Q = \epsilon_0 A E$, $E$ being the electric field between the plates.
The displacement current is $I_d = \epsilon_0 \frac{d\Phi_E}{dt} = \epsilon_0 A \frac{dE}{dt} = \frac{d(\epsilon_0 A E)}{dt} = \frac{dQ}{dt}$.
Thus $I_d = I_c$, showing the displacement current inside the capacitor equals the current charging it, maintaining continuity of current in the ac circuit.

questions.question: (a) Why are infra-red waves often called heat waves? Explain. (b) What do you understand by the statement, "Electromagnetic waves transport momentum"?
questions.answer:
(a) Infra-red waves are often called heat waves because they are readily absorbed by water molecules and other substances in most materials, increasing their internal (thermal) energy, and they are emitted by hot bodies due to the vibration of atoms and molecules.
(b) "Electromagnetic waves transport momentum" means that when an em wave is incident on a surface, it exerts a force (radiation pressure) on that surface and can impart momentum to it, as observed when light causes the tail of a comet to point away from the sun.

questions.question: How does Ampere-Maxwell law explain the flow of current through a capacitor when it is being charged by a battery? Write the expression for the displacement current in terms of the rate of change of electric flux.
questions.answer:
According to the Ampere-Maxwell law, $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 (I_c + I_d)$, so even though no conduction current flows through the gap between the capacitor plates, the changing electric field between the plates gives rise to a displacement current $I_d$, which maintains continuity of current in the circuit.
The displacement current is given by $I_d = \epsilon_0 \frac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$, where $\Phi_E$ is the electric flux between the plates.

questions.question: Identify the electromagnetic waves whose wavelengths vary as (a) $10^{-12}$ m $< \lambda < 10^{-8}$ m (b) $10^{-3}$ m $< \lambda < 10^{-1}$ m Write one use for each.
questions.answer:
(a) $10^{-12}$ m $< \lambda < 10^{-8}$ m corresponds to X-rays, used in medical diagnosis (imaging bone fractures) and in the study of crystal structure.
(b) $10^{-3}$ m $< \lambda < 10^{-1}$ m corresponds to microwaves, used in radar systems and in microwave ovens for cooking.

questions.question: (i) How are infrared waves produced? Write their one important use. (ii) The thin Ozone layer on top of the stratosphere is crucial for human survival. Why?
questions.answer:
(i) Infrared waves are produced by hot bodies and molecules due to vibrational and rotational motion of atoms; they are used in remote controls for household electronic devices such as TVs and ACs.
(ii) The ozone layer absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun, preventing it from reaching the Earth's surface, where it would otherwise cause damage to living tissues such as skin cancer and mutation of cells.

questions.question: State two properties of electromagnetic waves. How can we show that em waves carry momentum?
questions.answer:
Electromagnetic waves are transverse in nature and $\vec{E}$, $\vec{B}$ oscillate in phase, perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation.
They travel through vacuum with speed $c = 1/\sqrt{\mu_0 \epsilon_0}$ and do not require a material medium.
That em waves carry momentum is shown by the fact that when an em wave falls on a surface, it exerts a force (radiation pressure) on it, which is observed experimentally, e.g., in the tail of comets pointing away from the sun.

questions.question: Considering the case of a parallel plate capacitor being charged, show how one is required to generalize Ampere’s circuital law to include the term due to displacement current.
questions.answer:
While charging a parallel plate capacitor, conduction current $I$ flows in the connecting wires but no charge actually crosses the gap between the plates, so Ampere's circuital law $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 I$ fails for a surface drawn through the gap.
Maxwell showed that the changing electric field between the plates gives rise to a displacement current $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\phi_E}{dt}$, equal to the conduction current, so that the generalized law becomes $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0(I + I_d)$, making the current continuous across the gap.

questions.question: (a) An em wave is travelling in a medium with a velocity $\vec{v} = v\hat{i}$. Draw a sketch showing the propagation of the em wave, indicating the direction of the oscillating electric and magnetic fields. (b) How are the magnitudes of the electric and magnetic fields related to the velocity of the em wave?
questions.answer:
(a) The wave travels along $x$, with $\vec{E}$ oscillating along $y$ and $\vec{B}$ oscillating along $z$, both varying sinusoidally and in phase; a sketch would show sine curves for $E_y$ and $B_z$ plotted against $x$, mutually perpendicular and perpendicular to $\hat{i}$.
(b) The magnitudes are related by $v = E/B$, and in free space this equals $c = 1/\sqrt{\mu_0\epsilon_0}$.

questions.question: Draw a sketch of a plane electromagnetic wave propagating along the $z$-direction. Depict clearly the directions of electric and magnetic fields varying sinusoidally with $z$.
questions.answer:
For a plane em wave travelling along the $z$-direction, the electric field $\vec{E}$ oscillates sinusoidally along the $x$-axis and the magnetic field $\vec{B}$ oscillates sinusoidally along the $y$-axis, both in phase with each other.
A sketch shows $E_x = E_0 \sin(kz - \omega t)$ and $B_y = B_0 \sin(kz - \omega t)$ as two sine curves perpendicular to each other, both perpendicular to the direction of propagation $\hat{z}$, confirming the wave is transverse with $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$ along $\hat{z}$.

questions.question: A capacitor of capacitance ’ $C$’ is being charged by connecting it across a dc source along with an ammeter. Will the ammeter show a momentary deflection during the process of charging? If so, how would you explain this momentary deflection and the resulting continuity of current in the circuit? Write the expression for the current inside the capacitor.
questions.answer:
Yes, the ammeter shows a momentary deflection during charging.
This is because while the conduction current flows in the connecting wires, a time-varying electric field between the plates produces a displacement current $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\phi_E}{dt}$, which is equal in magnitude to the conduction current, so that current appears continuous through the circuit including the capacitor gap.
The current inside the capacitor is $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\phi_E}{dt} = C\dfrac{dV}{dt}$.

questions.question: When an ideal capacitor is charged by a dc battery, no current flows. However, when an ac source is used, the current flows continuously. How does one explain this, based on the concept of displacement current?
questions.answer:
With a dc battery, once the capacitor is fully charged the electric field between the plates becomes constant, so $\dfrac{d\phi_E}{dt} = 0$ and the displacement current $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\phi_E}{dt}$ vanishes, hence no current flows.
With an ac source, the voltage and hence the electric field between the plates keeps changing continuously, so $\phi_E$ keeps varying with time, producing a continuous displacement current that maintains current flow in the circuit.

questions.question: Explain briefly how electromagnetic waves are produced by an oscillating charge. How is the frequency of the em waves produced related to that of the oscillating charge?
questions.answer:
An oscillating charge produces an oscillating electric field, which in turn produces an oscillating magnetic field; these mutually perpendicular, time-varying $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ fields regenerate each other and propagate through space as an electromagnetic wave, away from the charge.
The frequency of the em wave produced is equal to the frequency of oscillation of the charge.

questions.question: What is sky wave communication? Why is this mode of propagation restricted to the frequencies only upto few MHz?
questions.answer:
Sky wave communication is the mode of propagation in which radio waves transmitted from a ground antenna are reflected back to earth by the ionosphere, enabling long-distance communication.
This mode is restricted to frequencies up to a few MHz because the ionosphere can reflect waves only up to a certain critical frequency; waves of higher frequency penetrate the ionosphere and escape into space instead of being reflected back.

questions.question: A parallel plate capacitor is being charged by a time varying current. Explain briefly how Ampere’s circuital law is generalized to incorporate the effect due to the displacement current.
questions.answer:
While a capacitor is being charged, a conduction current $I$ flows in the wires but no charge crosses the gap between the plates, so Ampere's circuital law $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 I$ gives inconsistent results depending on the surface chosen.
Maxwell resolved this by proposing that the changing electric flux between the plates constitutes a displacement current $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\phi_E}{dt}$, and generalized the law to $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0(I + I_d)$, making it valid for any surface.

questions.question: How are infrared waves produced? Why are these referred to as heat waves? Write their one important use.
questions.answer:
Infrared waves are produced by hot bodies and molecules due to vibrational and rotational motion of atoms, and are also emitted by the sun.
They are called heat waves because they are readily absorbed by water molecules present in most materials, increasing their thermal motion and thus heating them.
One important use is in remote controls for electronic devices such as TVs; they are also used in night-vision devices and for treating muscular strain.

questions.question: Show how the equation for Ampere’s circuital law, viz. $HB$ · $d\vec{l} = \mu_{0}I$ is modified in the presence of displacement current.
questions.answer:
Ampere's circuital law, $\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 I$, holds only for steady currents.
For time-varying fields, Maxwell added a displacement current term $I_d = \epsilon_0 \frac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$, arising from a changing electric flux, to make the law consistent with charge conservation.
The modified (Ampere-Maxwell) law is $\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 (I_c + I_d) = \mu_0 I_c + \mu_0 \epsilon_0 \frac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$, where $I_c$ is the conduction current.

questions.question: Arrange the following electromagnetic radiations in ascending order of their frequencies: (i) Microwave (ii) Radio wave (iii) X-rays (iv) Gamma rays Write two uses of any one of these.
questions.answer:
Ascending order of frequency: Radio wave $<$ Microwave $<$ X-rays $<$ Gamma rays.
Uses of X-rays: (1) detection of fractures and diagnosis of bone-related diseases in medicine, (2) detection of flaws/cracks in metal structures and security check at airports.

questions.question: How does a charge $q$ oscillating at certain frequency produce electromagnetic waves? Sketch a schematic diagram depicting electric and magnetic fields for an electromagnetic wave propagating along the Z-direction.
questions.answer:
An oscillating charge is an accelerated charge; it produces an oscillating electric field, which in turn produces an oscillating magnetic field at right angles to it, and each regenerates the other, so the disturbance propagates through space as an electromagnetic wave, without needing any medium.
For a wave travelling along the Z-direction, the electric field $\vec{E}$ oscillates along the X-axis and the magnetic field $\vec{B}$ oscillates along the Y-axis, both varying sinusoidally, mutually perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation (Z-axis).

questions.question: Answer the following questions: (a) Optical and radio telescopes are built on the ground while X-ray astronomy is possible only from satellites orbiting the Earth. Why? (b) The small ozone layer on top of the stratosphere is crucial for human survival. Why?
questions.answer:
(a) X-rays are strongly absorbed by the Earth's atmosphere (they do not fall in the atmospheric "windows" like visible light and radio waves do), so X-ray astronomy must be carried out from satellites above the atmosphere, whereas optical and radio waves can pass through the atmosphere and be observed from the ground.
(b) The ozone layer absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun; without it, UV rays reaching the Earth's surface would cause genetic damage and skin cancer in living organisms.

questions.question: Define magnetic susceptibility of a material. Name two elements, one having positive susceptibility and the other having negative susceptibility. What does negative susceptibility signify?
questions.answer:
Magnetic susceptibility $\chi = \dfrac{M}{H}$ is the ratio of the intensity of magnetization $M$ induced in a material to the magnetizing field intensity $H$.
Aluminium has positive susceptibility (paramagnetic), while bismuth has negative susceptibility (diamagnetic).
Negative susceptibility signifies that the material is diamagnetic, i.e., it develops magnetization opposite to the applied magnetizing field.

questions.question: What is meant by the transverse nature of electromagnetic waves? Draw a diagram showing the propagation of an electromagnetic wave along the x-direction, indicating clearly the directions of the oscillating electric and magnetic fields associated with it.
questions.answer:
Transverse nature means that in an electromagnetic wave, the electric field $\vec{E}$ and magnetic field $\vec{B}$ oscillate perpendicular to each other, and both are perpendicular to the direction of propagation of the wave, unlike longitudinal waves.
For propagation along the x-direction, $\vec{E}$ oscillates along the y-axis and $\vec{B}$ oscillates along the z-axis, with the wave travelling along the x-axis; a sketch would show sinusoidal $E$ (in the xy-plane) and $B$ (in the xz-plane) curves, mutually perpendicular, moving along x.

questions.question: Find the wavelength of electromagnetic waves of frequency $5 \times 10^{19} Hz$ in free space. Give its two applications.
questions.answer:
$\lambda = \dfrac{c}{\nu} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^{8}}{5 \times 10^{19}} = 6 \times 10^{-12}$ m, which lies in the gamma ray region.
Applications: (1) used in radiotherapy to destroy cancer cells, (2) used to sterilize surgical instruments and food items.

questions.question: Name the electromagnetic waves which are used for: (i) detection of fractures in bones (ii) physiotherapy (iii) radar systems Also write their wavelength range.
questions.answer:
(i) Detection of fractures in bones: X-rays, wavelength range $10^{-8}$ m to $10^{-13}$ m.
(ii) Physiotherapy: Infrared waves, wavelength range $7 \times 10^{-7}$ m to $10^{-3}$ m.
(iii) Radar systems: Microwaves, wavelength range $10^{-3}$ m to $0.3$ m.

questions.question: Name the electromagnetic waves which are used: (i) as a diagnostic tool in medicine (ii) in remote switches for TV sets (iii) in water purifiers Also write their wavelength range.
questions.answer:
(i) Diagnostic tool in medicine: X-rays, wavelength range $10^{-8}$ m to $10^{-13}$ m.
(ii) Remote switches for TV sets: Infrared waves, wavelength range $7 \times 10^{-7}$ m to $10^{-3}$ m.
(iii) Water purifiers: Ultraviolet rays, wavelength range $6 \times 10^{-10}$ m to $4 \times 10^{-7}$ m.

questions.question: Name the electromagnetic waves which are (i) also known as ’heat waves’, (ii) used in LASIK eye surgery, (iii) used to destroy cancer cells. Also write their wavelength range.
questions.answer:
(i) Also known as 'heat waves': Infrared waves, wavelength range $7 \times 10^{-7}$ m to $10^{-3}$ m.
(ii) Used in LASIK eye surgery: Ultraviolet rays, wavelength range $6 \times 10^{-10}$ m to $4 \times 10^{-7}$ m.
(iii) Used to destroy cancer cells: Gamma rays, wavelength range $10^{-14}$ m to $10^{-10}$ m.

questions.question: (a) Depict the variation of electric field $(\vec{E})$ and magnetic field $(\vec{B})$ with respect to the direction of propagation of an electromagnetic wave. Write their two important characteristics. (b) Show that $\frac{1}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_{0}\mu_{0}}}$ gives the velocity of an electromagnetic wave in free space.
questions.answer:
(a) In an electromagnetic wave, $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ are mutually perpendicular to each other and both are perpendicular to the direction of propagation, varying sinusoidally in phase.
Two characteristics: (i) They travel through vacuum with speed $c = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_{0}\mu_{0}}}$. (ii) At every point $E_{0}B_{0}$ ratio equals $c$, i.e., $\frac{E_{0}}{B_{0}} = c$, and $E$, $B$ reach maxima and minima together.
(b) Maxwell's equations give the wave equations $\frac{\partial^{2}E}{\partial x^{2}} = \mu_{0}\varepsilon_{0}\frac{\partial^{2}E}{\partial t^{2}}$ and similarly for $B$.
Comparing with the standard wave equation $\frac{\partial^{2}y}{\partial x^{2}} = \frac{1}{v^{2}}\frac{\partial^{2}y}{\partial t^{2}}$, the speed of the wave is $v = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_{0}\mu_{0}}}$.
On substituting $\varepsilon_{0} = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}$ $\text{C}^2\text{N}^{-1}\text{m}^{-2}$ and $\mu_{0} = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}$ $\text{TmA}^{-1}$, this gives $v = 3 \times 10^{8}$ $\text{ms}^{-1}$, equal to the speed of light, confirming light is an electromagnetic wave.

questions.question: What are microwaves? How are they produced? Give any two uses of microwaves.
questions.answer:
Microwaves are electromagnetic waves with wavelength range from about $0.1$ mm to $30$ cm (frequency $\sim 10^{9}$ to $10^{11}$ Hz).
They are produced by special vacuum tubes such as klystrons, magnetrons and Gunn diodes, which generate oscillating electric fields at these high frequencies.
Uses: (i) In radar systems for aircraft navigation and speed detection. (ii) In microwave ovens for cooking and in analysing molecular/atomic structure.

questions.question: What is displacement current ($i_{d}$)? Considering the case of charging of a capacitor, show that $i_{d} = \varepsilon_{0}\frac{d\Phi_{E}}{dt}$. What is the value of $i_{d}$ for a conductor across which a constant voltage is applied?
questions.answer:
Displacement current is the current that arises due to a time-varying electric field (electric flux) in a region, and it produces a magnetic field just like a conduction current, even in the absence of actual charge flow.
While charging a capacitor, conduction current $I_{c}$ flows in the connecting wires but not between the plates, since there is a gap.
Between the plates, the electric field $E = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_{0}A}$ changes as charge $Q$ builds up, so electric flux $\Phi_{E} = EA = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_{0}}$.
Thus $\varepsilon_{0}\frac{d\Phi_{E}}{dt} = \frac{dQ}{dt} = I_{c}$, and this is defined as displacement current $i_{d} = \varepsilon_{0}\frac{d\Phi_{E}}{dt}$, which equals $I_{c}$ and maintains continuity of current in the circuit.
For a conductor with a constant (steady) voltage applied, the electric field is constant, so $\frac{d\Phi_{E}}{dt} = 0$, hence $i_{d} = 0$.

questions.question: Differentiate between conduction current and displacement current. A capacitor is connected across a source providing time-dependent current. Explain how the total current at an instant is the sum of conduction current and displacement current in the circuit at that instant.
questions.answer:
Conduction current is due to actual flow of charges (electrons) in a conductor, given by $I_{c} = \frac{dQ}{dt}$, and it exists only where a conducting path is present.
Displacement current arises from a time-varying electric field in a region (such as between capacitor plates) where no charge actually flows, given by $i_{d} = \varepsilon_{0}\frac{d\Phi_{E}}{dt}$.
In a circuit with a capacitor connected to a time-varying source, conduction current flows in the wires, and between the plates the changing electric field produces an equal displacement current, so that $I_{c} = i_{d}$ at every instant.
Hence the total current, $I = I_{c} + i_{d}$, remains continuous throughout the circuit, satisfying Ampere-Maxwell's law and ensuring current continuity even through the capacitor gap.

questions.question: (a) A parallel plate capacitor is charged by an ac source. Show that the sum of conduction current ($I_{c}$) and the displacement current ($I_{d}$) has the same value at all points of the circuit. (b) In case (a) above, is Kirchhoff’s first rule (junction rule) valid at each plate of the capacitor? Explain.
questions.answer:
(a) When an ac source charges a parallel plate capacitor, conduction current $I_{c} = \frac{dQ}{dt}$ flows in the connecting wires.
Between the plates, the electric field $E = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_{0}A}$ varies with time, giving electric flux $\Phi_{E} = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon_{0}}$, so displacement current $I_{d} = \varepsilon_{0}\frac{d\Phi_{E}}{dt} = \frac{dQ}{dt}$.
Since $I_{c} = \frac{dQ}{dt} = I_{d}$ at every instant, the sum $I_{c} + I_{d}$ is the same at all points of the circuit, whether in the wire (only $I_{c}$) or between the plates (only $I_{d}$), satisfying Ampere-Maxwell's law.
(b) Kirchhoff's junction rule, as stated for conduction current alone, is not valid at the capacitor plates since $I_{c}$ is discontinuous there.
However, if displacement current is included along with conduction current, the total current ($I_{c} + I_{d}$) is continuous and the junction rule holds in this generalised sense.

questions.question: (a) The electric field $\vec{E}$ of an electromagnetic wave propagating in north direction is oscillating in up and down direction. Describe the direction of magnetic field $\vec{B}$ of the wave. (b) Are the wave length of radio waves and microwaves longer or shorter than those detectable by human eyes? (c) Write main use of each of the following in human life: (i) Infrared waves (ii) Gamma rays
questions.answer:
(a) Since $\vec{E}$, $\vec{B}$ and the direction of propagation are mutually perpendicular, with propagation towards north and $\vec{E}$ oscillating up-down (vertical), $\vec{B}$ must oscillate along the east-west (horizontal) direction.
(b) The wavelengths of radio waves and microwaves are both longer than those detectable by the human eye (visible light, $\sim 400$-$700$ nm).
(c) (i) Infrared waves are used for producing dry heat, in physiotherapy, and in remote controls/night-vision devices. (ii) Gamma rays are used in medicine to destroy cancer cells (radiotherapy) and in sterilizing surgical instruments.

questions.question: (a) How is an electromagnetic wave produced? (b) An electromagnetic wave is travelling in vertically upward direction. At an instant, its electric field vector points in west direction. In which direction does the magnetic field vector point at that instant? (c) Estimate the ratio of shortest wave length of radio waves to the longest wave length of gamma waves.
questions.answer:
(a) An electromagnetic wave is produced by an accelerated (oscillating) charge, which creates mutually perpendicular oscillating electric and magnetic fields that regenerate each other and propagate through space, requiring no medium.
(b) With propagation vertically upward and $\vec{E}$ along west, using the mutual perpendicularity of $\vec{E}$, $\vec{B}$ and direction of propagation ($\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$ along propagation direction), $\vec{B}$ must point towards the south.
(c) Radio waves have wavelength up to about $10^{4}$ m (shortest $\sim 0.1$ m), and gamma rays have wavelength as long as about $10^{-10}$ m.
Ratio of shortest wavelength of radio waves to longest wavelength of gamma rays $= \frac{10^{-1}}{10^{-10}} = 10^{9}$.

questions.question: (a) The amplitude of a light wave becomes n times. This results in intensity of the wave becoming m times. What is the relation between n and m? (b) White light is incident on three identical surfaces - a black surface, a yellow surface and a white surface, one by one. For which surface, the pressure exerted on the surface by the incident light will be (i) maximum (ii) minimum? Justify your answer.
questions.answer:
(a) Intensity of a wave is proportional to the square of its amplitude, $I \propto A^{2}$.
If amplitude becomes $n$ times, intensity becomes $n^{2}$ times, so $m = n^{2}$.
(b) (i) Radiation pressure is maximum for the white surface, since it reflects almost all the incident light, and reflection transfers momentum $\frac{2\Delta p}{\Delta t}$ (double that of absorption).
(ii) Radiation pressure is minimum for the black surface, since it absorbs almost all the incident light, transferring only momentum $\frac{\Delta p}{\Delta t}$ per unit time, without added reflection.

questions.question: (a) State any three characteristics of electromagnetic waves. (b) Briefly explain how and where the displacement current exists during the charging of a capacitor.
questions.answer:
(a) Three characteristics of electromagnetic waves: (i) They consist of mutually perpendicular, oscillating electric and magnetic fields, both perpendicular to the direction of propagation (transverse in nature). (ii) They travel through vacuum with speed $c = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_{0}\mu_{0}}} = 3 \times 10^{8}$ $\text{ms}^{-1}$, needing no material medium. (iii) They carry energy and momentum, and exert radiation pressure on a surface.
(b) During charging of a capacitor, displacement current exists in the gap between the plates, where the electric field (and hence electric flux) is changing with time due to the accumulating charge; it equals the conduction current $I_{c} = \frac{dQ}{dt}$ flowing in the connecting wires, given by $i_{d} = \varepsilon_{0}\frac{d\Phi_{E}}{dt}$, thereby maintaining continuity of current in the circuit.

questions.question: Name the electromagnetic wave used (i) in radar, (ii) in eye surgery and (iii) as diagnostic tool in medicine. Write their wavelength range also.
questions.answer:
(i) Radar: microwaves, wavelength range $0.1$ mm to $30$ cm.
(ii) Eye surgery: ultraviolet rays (excimer laser), wavelength range about $1$ nm to $400$ nm.
(iii) Diagnostic tool in medicine: X-rays, wavelength range about $10^{-3}$ nm to $1$ nm.

questions.question: (a) Differentiate between ’conduction current’ and ’displacement current’, giving one similarity and one dissimilarity between them. (b) Explain the existence of electromagnetic waves in free space, using the concept of displacement current.
questions.answer:
(a) Conduction current $I_c$ arises due to actual flow of charges (electrons) in a conductor, while displacement current $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$ arises due to a time-varying electric field, as in the gap between capacitor plates, without actual charge flow.
Similarity: both produce a magnetic field and appear together in Ampere-Maxwell law, $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0(I_c+I_d)$.
Dissimilarity: $I_c$ needs a conducting path and moving charges; $I_d$ exists even in vacuum/dielectric and needs only a changing electric flux.
(b) A changing electric field produces a displacement current, which generates a magnetic field; this changing magnetic field in turn produces a changing electric field. This mutual regeneration of $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ fields, perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation, sustains itself and propagates through free space as an electromagnetic wave, even without any medium.

questions.question: (a) How are electromagnetic waves produced? (b) Write the wavelength range and one use of: (i) Microwaves, and (ii) Ultraviolet waves.
questions.answer:
(a) Electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerated (oscillating) electric charges. An oscillating charge creates an oscillating electric field, which produces an oscillating magnetic field; these mutually sustaining, time-varying fields propagate through space as an electromagnetic wave, perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation.
(b) (i) Microwaves: wavelength range $10^{-3}$ m to $0.3$ m; used in radar systems for aircraft navigation and in microwave ovens for cooking.
(ii) Ultraviolet waves: wavelength range $4 \times 10^{-7}$ m to $6 \times 10^{-10}$ m; used to preserve food items and to kill germs in water purifiers.

questions.question: Name the electromagnetic radiations and write their frequency range: (a) Used to take the photograph of the bones (b) Produced by hot bodies (c) Used in television communication systems
questions.answer:
(a) X-rays are used to photograph bones; frequency range $3 \times 10^{16}$ Hz to $3 \times 10^{19}$ Hz.
(b) Infrared waves are produced by hot bodies and molecules; frequency range $3 \times 10^{11}$ Hz to $4 \times 10^{14}$ Hz.
(c) Radio waves (specifically VHF/UHF band) are used in television communication; frequency range about $50$ MHz to $1000$ MHz (i.e. $5 \times 10^{7}$ Hz to $10^{9}$ Hz).

questions.question: (a) "The wavelength of the electromagnetic wave is often correlated with the characteristic size of the system that radiates." Give two examples to justify this statement. (b) (i) Long distance radio broadcasts use short-wave bands. Why? (ii) Optical and radio telescopes are built on the ground, but X-ray astronomy is possible only from satellites orbiting the Earth. Why?
questions.answer:
(a) The wavelength radiated by an antenna/system is of the order of its own size, since the source must resonate with the wave it emits.
Example 1: Radio/TV antennas, which are metre-sized, radiate radio waves of wavelength of the order of metres.
Example 2: Atoms and nuclei, of size $10^{-10}$ m to $10^{-15}$ m, emit visible/UV light and gamma rays of correspondingly short wavelength.
(b) (i) Short-wave radio bands get reflected repeatedly between the ionosphere and the Earth's surface, enabling them to travel very long distances despite the curvature of the Earth.
(ii) X-rays are absorbed by the Earth's atmosphere, so X-ray astronomy requires detectors placed above the atmosphere on satellites, whereas optical and radio waves pass through the atmosphere and can be observed from the ground.

questions.question: (a) On what factors does the speed of an electromagnetic wave in a medium depend? (b) How is an electromagnetic wave produced? (c) Sketch a schematic diagram depicting the electric and magnetic fields for an electromagnetic wave propagating along z-axis.
questions.answer:
(a) The speed of an electromagnetic wave in a medium, $v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu\epsilon}}$, depends on the permeability $\mu$ and permittivity $\epsilon$ of the medium (i.e., on its electric and magnetic properties), and not on the amplitude of the fields.
(b) An electromagnetic wave is produced by an accelerated (oscillating) charge. The oscillating electric field produces an oscillating magnetic field, and this changing magnetic field regenerates an oscillating electric field; these mutually sustaining, mutually perpendicular fields propagate through space as an electromagnetic wave.
(c) For a wave travelling along the $z$-axis, $\vec{E}$ oscillates along the $x$-axis and $\vec{B}$ oscillates along the $y$-axis, both varying sinusoidally, in phase, and perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation ($z$-axis), consistent with $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$ pointing along $\hat{z}$.

questions.question: The electric field in an electromagnetic wave in vacuum is given by: $\vec{E} = (6.3$ N/C $)[\cos((1.5$ rad/m $)y+ (4.5 \times 10^{8}$ rad/s $)t)]\hat{i}$ (a) Find the wavelength and frequency of the wave. (b) What is the amplitude of the magnetic field of the wave? (c) Write an expression for the magnetic field of this wave.
questions.answer:
(a) Comparing with $E = E_0\cos(ky+\omega t)$: $k = 1.5$ rad/m, $\omega = 4.5\times10^{8}$ rad/s.
Wavelength: $\lambda = \dfrac{2\pi}{k} = \dfrac{2\pi}{1.5} \approx 4.19$ m
Frequency: $\nu = \dfrac{\omega}{2\pi} = \dfrac{4.5\times10^{8}}{2\pi} \approx 7.16 \times 10^{7}$ Hz
(b) $B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{c} = \dfrac{6.3}{3\times10^{8}} = 2.1\times10^{-8}$ T
(c) Since the wave travels along $-y$ with $\vec{E}$ along $x$, $\vec{B}$ must be along $z$ (as $\vec{E}\times\vec{B}$ gives propagation direction):
$\vec{B} = (2.1\times10^{-8} \text{ T})[\cos((1.5 \text{ rad/m})y + (4.5\times10^{8} \text{ rad/s})t)]\hat{k}$

questions.question: Name the electromagnetic waves with their wavelength range which are used for (i) FM radio broadcast (ii) detection of fracture in bones (iii) treatment of muscular strain
questions.answer:
(i) FM radio broadcast uses radio waves (VHF band), wavelength range about $1$ m to $10$ m.
(ii) Detection of fracture in bones uses X-rays, wavelength range about $10^{-8}$ m to $10^{-13}$ m.
(iii) Treatment of muscular strain uses infrared rays, wavelength range about $10^{-3}$ m to $7\times10^{-7}$ m.

questions.question: What is meant by displacement current? How is this current different from the conduction current? A capacitor is being charged by a source of emf. Justify the continuity of current in the circuit.
questions.answer:
Displacement current is the current that arises due to a time-varying electric field (electric flux) between the plates of a capacitor, given by $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$, even though no actual charge crosses the gap.
It differs from conduction current, which is due to the actual flow of charges through a conductor and requires a conducting path, whereas displacement current exists in vacuum/dielectric wherever the electric field is changing.
While charging, conduction current $I_c$ flows in the connecting wires but stops at the capacitor plates (gap), while the electric field between the plates increases, producing an equal displacement current $I_d = I_c$ across the gap. Thus $I_c + 0 = I_d$ ensures the total (Maxwell) current remains continuous throughout the circuit, including the gap between the plates.

questions.question: Explain the following giving reasons: (i) ’Electromagnetic waves differ considerably in their mode of interaction with matter’. (ii) ’Food items to be heated in microwave oven must contain water’. (iii) ’Welders wear face mask with glasses during welding’.
questions.answer:
(i) Electromagnetic waves of different wavelengths carry different energies ($E = h\nu$) and interact differently with atoms/molecules of matter; for example gamma rays and X-rays, being highly energetic, penetrate and ionize matter, while radio waves of low energy mostly pass through or reflect off surfaces without much interaction.
(ii) Water molecules are polar and absorb microwave energy efficiently through rotational motion, producing heat; hence food must contain water for microwave ovens to heat it effectively.
(iii) The welding arc emits intense ultraviolet radiation along with visible light; the protective glasses in the mask absorb harmful UV rays and reduce glare, protecting the welder's eyes from damage.

questions.question: (a) Name the parts of the electromagnetic spectrum which are (i) also known as ’heat waves’ and (ii) absorbed by ozone layer in the atmosphere. (b) Write briefly one method each, of the production and detection of these radiations.
questions.answer:
(a) (i) Infrared waves are known as heat waves.
(ii) Ultraviolet radiation is absorbed by the ozone layer in the atmosphere.
(b) Infrared waves are produced by hot bodies and molecules due to vibrational and rotational motion, and are detected using thermopiles, bolometers, or infrared photographic film.
Ultraviolet radiation is produced by special lamps (mercury vapour lamps) and from very hot bodies/stars, and is detected using photocells and photographic film sensitive to UV.

questions.question: Name the part of the electromagnetic spectrum which are: (i) stopped by face mask worn by welders. (ii) used in detectors in Earth satellites. (iii) used in ’short-wave band’ in communication. Also write the order of wavelengths, in each case.
questions.answer:
(i) Ultraviolet rays are stopped by the welder's face mask; wavelength order $10^{-8}$ m to $4 \times 10^{-7}$ m.
(ii) Infrared waves are used in detectors in Earth satellites; wavelength order $10^{-3}$ m to $7 \times 10^{-7}$ m.
(iii) Short-wave communication uses radio waves (short-wave band); wavelength order $10$ m to $100$ m.

questions.question: (i) Depict a plane electromagnetic wave propagating along the $x$-axis. Write the expressions for its oscillating electric and magnetic fields. (ii) Write three characteristics of electromagnetic waves.
questions.answer:
(i) For a wave travelling along the $x$-axis with $E$ along $y$ and $B$ along $z$:
$E_y = E_0 \sin(kx - \omega t)$
$B_z = B_0 \sin(kx - \omega t)$
where $E_0/B_0 = c$.
(ii) Characteristics:
1. Electromagnetic waves are transverse; $\vec{E}$, $\vec{B}$ and the direction of propagation are mutually perpendicular.
2. They do not require a material medium and travel through vacuum with speed $c = 1/\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}$.
3. $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ are in phase and carry energy and momentum.

questions.question: Name the electromagnetic waves which are produced by the following: (i) Radioactive decays of nucleus (ii) Welding arcs (iii) Hot bodies Write one use each of these waves.
questions.answer:
(i) Radioactive decay of nucleus produces gamma rays; used in treatment of cancer cells (radiotherapy).
(ii) Welding arcs produce ultraviolet rays; used to sterilise water/surgical instruments.
(iii) Hot bodies produce infrared rays; used in night-vision devices and remote sensing.

questions.question: Electromagnetic waves of wavelengths $\lambda_{1}$, $\lambda_{2}$ and $\lambda_{3}$ are used in radar systems, in water purifiers and in remote switches of TV, respectively. (i) Identify the electromagnetic waves, and (ii) Write one source of each of them.
questions.answer:
(i) $\lambda_1$ used in radar is a microwave; $\lambda_2$ used in water purifiers is an ultraviolet wave; $\lambda_3$ used in remote switches of TV is an infrared wave.
(ii) Source of microwaves: klystron valve/magnetron.
Source of ultraviolet: mercury vapour lamps, sun.
Source of infrared: hot bodies, LEDs (infrared lamps).

questions.question: Identify electromagnetic waves which: (i) are used in radar system. (ii) affect a photographic plate. (iii) are used in surgery. Write their frequency range.
questions.answer:
(i) Radar systems use microwaves; frequency range $10^{9}$ Hz to $10^{11}$ Hz.
(ii) Photographic plates are affected by ultraviolet rays; frequency range $8 \times 10^{14}$ Hz to $5 \times 10^{16}$ Hz.
(iii) Surgery uses X-rays; frequency range $10^{16}$ Hz to $10^{21}$ Hz.

questions.question: (i) Arrange the following electromagnetic radiation in the ascending order of their frequencies: X-rays, microwaves, gamma rays, radio waves (ii) Write two uses of any two of these radiation.
questions.answer:
(i) Ascending order of frequency: radio waves $<$ microwaves $<$ X-rays $<$ gamma rays.
(ii) Radio waves: used in radio and television broadcasting; used in long-distance communication.
X-rays: used in medical diagnosis (imaging bones); used in detecting cracks/flaws in metals.

questions.question: Write the expression for the speed of light in a material medium of relative permittivity $\varepsilon_{r}$ and relative magnetic permeability $\mu_{r}$.
questions.answer:
Speed of light in a material medium is $v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0\mu_r\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_r}} = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r\varepsilon_r}}$
where $c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}}$ is the speed of light in vacuum.
Thus the refractive index of the medium is $n = \sqrt{\mu_r\varepsilon_r}$.

questions.question: Write the wavelength range and name of the electromagnetic waves which are used in (i) radar systems for aircraft navigation, and (ii) Earth satellites to observe the growth of the crops.
questions.answer:
(i) Radar systems for aircraft navigation use microwaves; wavelength range $1$ mm to $0.1$ m.
(ii) Earth satellites observing crop growth use infrared waves; wavelength range $700$ nm to $1$ mm.

questions.question: Name the electro-magnetic waves with their frequency range, produced in (a) some radioactive decay (b) sparks during electric welding (c) TV remote
questions.answer:
(a) Radioactive decay produces gamma rays; frequency range $10^{18}$ Hz to $10^{22}$ Hz.
(b) Sparks during electric welding produce ultraviolet waves; frequency range $8 \times 10^{14}$ Hz to $5 \times 10^{16}$ Hz.
(c) TV remote produces infrared waves; frequency range $3 \times 10^{11}$ Hz to $4 \times 10^{14}$ Hz.

questions.question: (a) We feel the warmth of the sun light but not the pressure on our hands. Explain. (b) Which out of wavelength, frequency and speed of an electro-magnetic wave does not change on passing from one medium to another? (c) A thin ozone layer in the upper atmosphere is crucial for human survival on earth, why?
questions.answer:
(a) The warmth felt is due to the energy carried by sunlight being absorbed and converted to heat, which is significant; the radiation pressure $p = I/c$ is extremely small because $c$ is very large, so the force on our hands is too feeble to be felt.
(b) The frequency of an electromagnetic wave does not change on passing from one medium to another; wavelength and speed both change since $v = f\lambda$ and $v$ depends on the medium.
(c) The ozone layer absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun and prevents it from reaching the Earth's surface; without it, UV rays would cause skin cancer and other damage to living organisms, so it is crucial for human survival.

questions.question: (a) How are electro-magnetic waves produced? Depict an electro-magnetic wave propagating in $Z$-direction with its magnetic field $\vec{B}$ oscillating along $X$-direction. (b) Write two characteristics of electro-magnetic waves.
questions.answer:
(a) Electromagnetic waves are produced by an accelerated (or oscillating) electric charge. The oscillating charge produces an oscillating electric field, which produces an oscillating magnetic field, which in turn produces an oscillating electric field, and so on; these mutually perpetuating, mutually perpendicular oscillating fields regenerate each other and propagate through space even without a material medium.
For a wave travelling along $Z$-direction with $\vec{B}$ along $X$-direction, $\vec{E}$ must be along $Y$-direction, since $\vec{E}$, $\vec{B}$ and the direction of propagation $\vec{k}$ form a mutually perpendicular right-handed set: $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$ is along $\vec{k}$ ($Z$-direction). So $E_y = E_0 \sin(kz - \omega t)$ and $B_x = B_0 \sin(kz - \omega t)$, oscillating in phase with each other and perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation.
(b) (i) Electromagnetic waves do not require a material medium to travel and can propagate through vacuum.
(ii) In free space, $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ are in phase, perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation, and travel with speed $c = 1/\sqrt{\mu_0 \epsilon_0}$.

questions.question: Identify the part of the electromagnetic spectrum used in (i) radar and (ii) eye surgery. Write their frequency range.
questions.answer:
(i) Radar uses microwaves, which have a frequency range of about $10^9$ Hz to $3 \times 10^{11}$ Hz (or wavelength $0.1$ mm to $30$ cm).
(ii) Eye surgery uses ultraviolet rays (UV lasers, e.g. LASIK), which have a frequency range of about $8 \times 10^{14}$ Hz to $3 \times 10^{17}$ Hz.
Both are electromagnetic waves that travel with speed $c$ in vacuum but differ greatly in frequency and hence in their interaction with matter, microwaves being used for their penetrating/reflecting property in navigation, and UV for its ability to be focused precisely to reshape tissue.

questions.question: Prove that the average energy density of the oscillating electric field is equal to that of the oscillating magnetic field.
questions.answer:
Average energy density of the electric field is $u_E = \dfrac{1}{2}\epsilon_0 E^2$, and of the magnetic field is $u_B = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{B^2}{\mu_0}$.
For an electromagnetic wave in free space, $E = cB$, where $c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \epsilon_0}}$.
So $u_B = \dfrac{B^2}{2\mu_0} = \dfrac{(E/c)^2}{2\mu_0} = \dfrac{E^2}{2\mu_0 c^2} = \dfrac{E^2}{2\mu_0} \times \mu_0 \epsilon_0 = \dfrac{1}{2}\epsilon_0 E^2$.
Thus $u_B = u_E$, i.e., the average energy density of the electric field equals that of the magnetic field, and each carries half the total energy of the wave.

questions.question: Name the radiation of the electromagnetic spectrum which is used for the following: (a) Radar (b) To photograph internal parts of human body (c) For taking photographs of the sky during night and foggy conditions Give the frequency range in each case.
questions.answer:
(a) Radar uses microwaves, frequency range about $10^9$ Hz to $3 \times 10^{11}$ Hz.
(b) Photographing internal parts of the human body uses X-rays, frequency range about $3 \times 10^{16}$ Hz to $3 \times 10^{19}$ Hz.
(c) Photographing the sky during night and foggy conditions uses infrared rays, frequency range about $3 \times 10^{11}$ Hz to $4 \times 10^{14}$ Hz, since IR can penetrate fog/haze and is emitted by warm objects, allowing imaging in low visibility.

questions.question: When a parallel plate capacitor is being charged by a dc battery, why does a galvanometer show a momentary deflection? Obtain the expression for the displacement current and show how it is related to conduction current in a steady state.
questions.answer:
While the capacitor is charging, the charge on its plates and hence the electric field between the plates keeps changing with time. Although no actual conduction current flows across the gap between the plates, a changing electric flux between the plates gives rise to a displacement current, $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$, which maintains continuity of current in the circuit; this displacement current causes the momentary deflection of the galvanometer, which stops once the capacitor is fully charged and the electric field becomes steady (no current flows in dc steady state).
For a parallel plate capacitor, $\Phi_E = EA = \dfrac{Q}{\epsilon_0}$, so $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt} = \dfrac{dQ}{dt}$, which is exactly equal to the conduction current $I_c = \dfrac{dQ}{dt}$ flowing in the connecting wires. Thus at every instant, $I_d = I_c$, ensuring current continuity in the circuit even though no charge actually crosses the gap between the plates.

questions.question: Write the range of the wavelength of the following electromagnetic radiations: (a) Infrared rays (b) Ultraviolet rays (c) $\gamma$-rays Write one use of each of the above.
questions.answer:
(a) Infrared rays: wavelength range about $1$ mm to $700$ nm; used in remote controls for household electronic devices (TV, AC).
(b) Ultraviolet rays: wavelength range about $400$ nm to $1$ nm; used to preserve food by killing bacteria (also LASIK eye surgery, detecting forgery).
(c) $\gamma$-rays: wavelength range about $10^{-10}$ m to less than $10^{-14}$ m; used in radiotherapy to treat cancer cells/tumours (also in sterilizing medical equipment).

questions.question: Define displacement current. What role does it play while charging a capacitor by dc source. Is the value of displacement current same as that of the conduction current? Explain.
questions.answer:
Displacement current is the current that arises due to a time-varying electric field (electric flux) between the plates of a capacitor, given by $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$.
While charging a capacitor by a dc source, no actual charge crosses the gap between the plates, but the changing electric field between the plates produces a displacement current that maintains the continuity of current in the circuit, allowing current to "flow" through the capacitor as far as Ampere's circuital law (modified by Maxwell) is concerned.
Yes, at every instant the displacement current equals the conduction current in the connecting wires, since $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt} = \dfrac{dQ}{dt} = I_c$; this equality ensures that the total current (conduction + displacement) is continuous across any cross-section, including the gap between the plates.

questions.question: (a) How are electromagnetic waves produced? Explain. (b) A plane electromagnetic wave is travelling through a medium along the $+$ ve $z$ direction. Depict the electromagnetic wave showing the directions of the oscillating electric and magnetic fields.
questions.answer:
(a) Electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerated (oscillating) electric charges. An oscillating charge creates a time-varying electric field, which by Maxwell's equations produces a time-varying magnetic field; this changing magnetic field in turn produces a changing electric field, and this process repeats, generating mutually perpendicular, mutually regenerating $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ fields that propagate through space (even vacuum) as an electromagnetic wave, carrying energy away from the source.
(b) For a wave travelling along $+z$ direction, $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ are perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation, e.g. $E_x = E_0 \sin(kz - \omega t)$ along $X$-axis and $B_y = B_0 \sin(kz - \omega t)$ along $Y$-axis, such that $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$ points along $+z$, with $\vec{E}$, $\vec{B}$ oscillating in phase.

questions.question: (i) Identify the part of the electromagnetic spectrum which is: (a) suitable for radar system used in aircraft navigation, (b) produced by bombarding a metal target by high speed electrons. (ii) Why does a galvanometer show a momentary deflection at the time of charging or discharging a capacitor? Write the necessary expression to explain this observation.
questions.answer:
(i) (a) Microwaves are suitable for radar systems used in aircraft navigation.
(b) X-rays are produced by bombarding a metal target with high speed electrons.
(ii) A galvanometer shows a momentary deflection at the time of charging or discharging a capacitor because a changing electric flux between the plates produces a displacement current, $I_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$, which is equal to the conduction current $I_c = \dfrac{dQ}{dt}$ in the connecting wires; once the capacitor is fully charged (or discharged), the electric field becomes steady, $\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt} = 0$, so the current and hence deflection ceases.

questions.question: How are electromagnetic waves produced? What is the source of energy of these waves? Write mathematical expressions for electric and magnetic fields of an electromagnetic wave propagating along the $z$-axis. Write any two important properties of electromagnetic waves.
questions.answer:
Electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerated (oscillating) electric charges. A charge oscillating with some frequency produces an oscillating electric field, which produces an oscillating magnetic field of the same frequency; these two fields, being sources of each other as per Maxwell's equations, sustain each other and propagate through space as an electromagnetic wave, even in vacuum.
The energy of these waves comes from the energy source (e.g., battery/oscillator circuit) that drives and sustains the oscillatory acceleration of the charge.
For propagation along the $z$-axis: $E_x = E_0 \sin(kz - \omega t)$ and $B_y = B_0 \sin(kz - \omega t)$, with $\vec{E}$, $\vec{B}$ mutually perpendicular and both perpendicular to $\vec{k}$ (the direction of propagation), and $E_0/B_0 = c$.
Two important properties: (i) they travel through vacuum with speed $c = 1/\sqrt{\mu_0 \epsilon_0}$; (ii) $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ oscillate in phase and are perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation.
