questions.question: A long straight wire is held vertically and carries a steady current in upward direction. The shape of magnetic field lines produced by the current-carrying wire are: (A) horizontal straight lines directed radially out from the wire. (B) straight lines parallel to the current-carrying wire. (C) concentric horizontal circles around the wire. (D) coaxial helixes around the wire.
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
By the right-hand rule, the magnetic field of a straight current-carrying wire forms concentric circular field lines lying in planes perpendicular to the wire, i.e. horizontal circles around a vertical wire.

questions.question: A particle having charge $+q$ enters a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ as shown in the figure. The particle will describe: (A) a circular path in $XZ$ plane (B) a semicircular path in $XY$ plane (C) a helical path with its axis parallel to $Y$ -axis (D) a semicircular path in $Y Z$ plane
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
The magnetic force $\vec{F}=q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}$ acts perpendicular to both $\vec{v}$ and $\vec{B}$; for the given orientation this confines the particle's motion to the $YZ$-plane, and since the field exists only over part of the region, the particle traces a semicircular path before leaving the field.

questions.question: A particle with charge $q$ moving with velocity $\vec{v} = v_{0}\hat{i}$ enters a region with magnetic field $B = B_{1}\hat{j} + B_{2}\hat{k}$. The magnitude of force experienced by the particle is: (A) $qv_{0}(B_{1} + B_{2})$ (B) $qv_{0}{}^{2}( \frac{B_{1}+ B_{2})}{B^{2}+ B^{2}}$ (C) $qv_{0}p \frac{12}{B^{2}+ B^{2}}$ (D) $qv^{2}p ^{0}{}^{1}{}^{2}$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
$\vec{F}=q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}=q(v_0\hat{i})\times(B_1\hat{j}+B_2\hat{k})=qv_0B_1\hat{k}-qv_0B_2\hat{j}$, so $|\vec{F}|=qv_0\sqrt{B_1^2+B_2^2}$.

questions.question: A particle of mass $m$ and charge $q$ moves along $y$-axis in a region in which a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is pointing along $x$-axis. The Lorentz force acting on the charge will point along: (A) $x$-axis (B) $y$-axis (C) $z$-axis (D) negative $z$-axis
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
$\vec{F}=q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}=q(v\hat{j})\times(B\hat{i})=qvB(\hat{j}\times\hat{i})=-qvB\hat{k}$, so the force points along the negative $z$-axis.

questions.question: Case Study: A galvanometer is an instrument used to show the direction and strength of the current passing through it. In a galvanometer, a coil placed in a magnetic field experiences a torque and hence gets deflected when a current passes through it. The name is derived from the surname of Italian scientist L. Galvani, who in 1791 discovered that electric current makes a dead frog’s leg jerk. A spring attached with the coil provides a counter torque. In equilibrium, the deflecting torque is balanced by the restoring torque of the spring and we have: $NBAI = k\phi$, where $N$ is the total number of turns in the coil, $A$ is the area of cross-section of each turn, $B$ is the radial magnetic field, $k$ is the torsional constant of the spring, $\phi$ is the angular deflection of the coil. As the current ($I_{g}$) which produces full scale deflection in the galvanometer is very small, the galvanometer cannot as such be used to measure current in electric circuits. A small resistance, called shunt, of a suitable value is connected with the galvanometer to convert it into an ammeter of desired range. By using a higher resistance, a galvanometer can also be converted into a voltmeter. (i) The value of the current sensitivity of a galvanometer is given by: (A) $\frac{k}{NBA}$ (B) $\frac{NBA}{k}$ (C) $\frac{kBA}{N}$ (D) $\frac{kNB}{A}$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Current sensitivity is $\frac{\phi}{I}=\frac{NBA}{k}$, obtained directly from the equilibrium condition $NBAI=k\phi$.

questions.question: (ii) A galvanometer of resistance $6 \Omega$ shows full scale deflection for a current of $0.2$ A. The value of shunt to be used with this galvanometer to convert it into an ammeter of range $(0 -5$ A $)$ is: (A) $0.25 \Omega$ (B) $0.30 \Omega$ (C) $0.50 \Omega$ (D) $6.0 \Omega$
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Using $I_gR_g=(I-I_g)S$: $S=\frac{I_gR_g}{I-I_g}=\frac{0.2\times6}{5-0.2}=\frac{1.2}{4.8}=0.25\ \Omega$.

questions.question: (iii) The value of resistance of the ammeter in case (ii) will be: (A) $0.20 \Omega$ (B) $0.24 \Omega$ (C) $6.0 \Omega$ (D) $6.25 \Omega$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Ammeter resistance $=\frac{R_gS}{R_g+S}=\frac{6\times0.25}{6.25}=0.24\ \Omega$.

questions.question: (iv) (a) A galvanometer is converted into a voltmeter of range $(0 -V )$ by connecting with it, a resistance $R_{1}$. If $R_{1}$ is replaced by $R_{2}$, the range becomes $(0 -2V )$. The resistance of the galvanometer is: OR (b) A current of $5$ mA flows through a galvanometer. Its coil has $100$ turns, each of area of cross-section $18$ cm $2$ and is suspended in a magnetic field $0.20$ T. The deflecting torque acting on the coil will be: (A) (a) $(R2R)$ OR (b) $3.6 \times 10^{-2}$ Nm $^{2} -^{1}$ (B) (a) $(RR)$ OR (b) $1.8 \times 10^{-4}$ Nm $^{2} -^{1}$ (C) (a) $(R R)$ OR (b) $2.4 \times 10^{-3}$ Nm $^{1} +^{2}$ (D) (a) $(R2R)$ OR (b) $1.2 \times 10^{-4}$ Nm $^{1} -^{2}$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
(a) From $V=I_g(G+R_1)$ and $2V=I_g(G+R_2)$, dividing gives $2(G+R_1)=G+R_2$, so $G=R_2-2R_1$.
OR (b) $\tau=NIAB=100\times(5\times10^{-3})\times(18\times10^{-4})\times0.2=1.8\times10^{-4}$ Nm.

questions.question: A charged particle gains a speed of $10^{7}$ ms $-1$, when accelerated from rest through a potential difference $10$ kV. It enters a region of magnetic field of $0.4$ T such that $\vec{V} \perp\vec{B}$. The radius of circular path described by it is: (A) $2.5$ cm (B) $5$ cm (C) $8$ cm (D) $10$ cm $[]$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Since $qV=\frac{1}{2}mv^2$, eliminating $q$ and $m$ gives $r=\frac{mv}{qB}=\frac{2V}{vB}=\frac{2\times10^4}{10^6\times0.4}=5\times10^{-2}$ m $=5$ cm.

questions.question: A current of $\frac{10}{\pi}$ A is maintained in a circular loop of radius $14$ cm. The value of dipole moment associated with the loop is: (A) $0.019$ Am $2$ (B) $0.14$ Am $2$ (C) $0.196$ Am $2$ (D) $0.615$ Am $2$
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
The magnetic dipole moment is $m = IA = \frac{10}{\pi}\times \pi (0.14)^2 = 0.196$ Am$^2$.

questions.question: The value of magnetic field at point $O$ in the given figure is: (A) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi R}$ (B) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{\pi R}$ (C) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{4R}$ (D) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{R}$
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
For a semicircular arc of radius $R$, the straight portions lie along lines passing through $O$ and contribute no field, while the arc gives $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4R}$.

questions.question: A galvanometer can be converted into an ammeter of desired range by connecting a: (A) small resistance in series (B) large resistance in series (C) small resistance in parallel (D) large resistance in parallel
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
A small resistance (shunt) connected in parallel with the galvanometer diverts most of the current, converting it into an ammeter of the desired range.

questions.question: A proton and an $\alpha$-particle enter with the same velocity $\vec{V}$ in a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ such that $\vec{V} \perp\vec{B}$. The ratio of the radii of their paths is: (A) $2$ (B) $\frac{1}{2}$ (C) $\frac{1}{4}$ (D) $4$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Since $r = \frac{mv}{qB}$, $\frac{r_p}{r_\alpha} = \frac{m_p/e}{4m_p/2e} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.question: A straight conductor is carrying a current of $2$ A in $+x$ direction along it. A uniform magnetic field $\vec{B} = (0$· $6 \hat{j} + 0$· $8 \hat{k})$ T is switched on, in the region. The force acting on $10$ cm length of the conductor is: (A) $(0$· $12 \hat{j} -0$· $16 \hat{k})$ N (B) $(-0$· $16 \hat{j} + 0$· $12 \hat{k})$ N (C) $(0$· $12 \hat{j} + 0$· $16 \hat{k})$ N (D) $(0$· $16 \hat{j} -0$· $12 \hat{k})$ N
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
$\vec{F} = I\vec{L}\times\vec{B} = 2(0.1\hat{i})\times(0.6\hat{j}+0.8\hat{k}) = (-0.16\hat{j}+0.12\hat{k})$ N.

questions.question: Assertion (A): A charged particle is moving with velocity $v$ in $x$- $y$ plane, making an angle $\theta (0 < \theta <^{\frac{\pi}{2}})$ with $x$-axis. If a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is applied in the region, along $y$-axis, the particle will move in a helical path with its axis parallel to $x$-axis. Reason (R): The direction of the magnetic force acting on a charged particle moving in a magnetic field is along the velocity of the particle. Select the correct answer: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. (D) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
Since $\vec{B}$ is along the $y$-axis, the helix axis is along $y$, not $x$, so (A) is false; also the magnetic force $\vec{F}=q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{v}$, not along it, so (R) is false.

questions.question: In a circular loop of radius $R$, current $I$ enters at point $A$ and exits at point $B$, as shown in the figure. The value of the magnetic field at the centre $O$ of the loop is: (A) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{R}$ (B) zero (C) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{2R}$ (D) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{4R}$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
The two arcs act like parallel resistors, so the current in each arc is inversely proportional to its length; since $B \propto I\theta$ for each arc, the contributions of the two arcs are equal and opposite, giving zero net field at $O$.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Two long parallel wires, freely suspended and connected in series to a battery, move apart. Reason (R): Two wires carrying current in opposite directions repel each other. (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. (D) Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
In a series loop the current flows in opposite directions in the two wires, and antiparallel currents repel, correctly explaining why the wires move apart.

questions.question: A loop carrying a current I clockwise is placed in $x -y$ plane, in a uniform magnetic field directed along z-axis. The tendency of the loop will be to: (A) move along x-axis (B) move along y-axis (C) shrink (D) expand
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
For this current direction the magnetic moment is antiparallel to $\vec{B}$, so each current element experiences a radially inward force $I\,d\vec{l}\times\vec{B}$, making the loop shrink to lower its potential energy $U=-\vec{m}\cdot\vec{B}$.

questions.question: A 10 cm long wire lies along y-axis. It carries a current of $1.0$ A in positive y-direction. A magnetic field $\vec{B} = (5$ mT $)\hat{j} -(8$ mT $)\hat{k}$ exists in the region. The force on the wire is: (A) $(0.8$ mN $)\hat{i}$ (B) $-(0.8$ mN $)\hat{i}$ (C) $(8.0$ mN $)\hat{i}$ (D) $-(8.0$ mN $)\hat{i}$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
$\vec{F}=I\vec{L}\times\vec{B} = (1.0)(0.1\hat{j})\times(5\hat{j}-8\hat{k})\text{ mT} = -0.8\hat{i}$ mN.

questions.question: A galvanometer of resistance $G \Omega$ is converted into an ammeter of range 0 to $I$ A. If the current through the galvanometer is $0.1\%$ of $I$ A, the resistance of the ammeter is: (A) $\frac{G}{999}\Omega$ (B) $\frac{G}{1000}\Omega$ (C) $\frac{G}{1001}\Omega$ (D) $\frac{G}{100.1}\Omega$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Shunt resistance $S = \frac{G I_g}{I - I_g} = \frac{G(0.001I)}{0.999I} = \frac{G}{999}$, and the ammeter resistance (galvanometer parallel with shunt) is $R_A = \frac{GS}{G+S} = \frac{G}{1000}\,\Omega$.

questions.question: A piece of wire bent in the form of a circular loop $A$ carries a current $I$. The wire is then bent into a circular loop $B$ of two turns and carries the same current. The ratio of magnetic fields at the centre of loop $A$ to that of loop $B$ will be: (A) $\frac{1}{16}$ (B) $16$ (C) $4$ (D) $\frac{1}{4}$
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
For loop A (1 turn, length $L$): $B_A = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R_A} = \frac{\mu_0 I \pi}{L}$; for loop B (2 turns, same wire, each turn radius $L/4\pi$): $B_B = \frac{\mu_0 (2I)}{2R_B} = \frac{4\mu_0 I \pi}{L}$, giving $\frac{B_A}{B_B} = \frac{1}{4}$.

questions.question: Two charged particles, $P$ and $Q$, each having charge $q$ but of masses $m_{1}$ and $m_{2}$, are accelerated through the same potential difference $V$. They enter a region of magnetic $[]$ field $\vec{B} (\perp\vec{v})$ and describe the circular paths of radii $a$ and $b$ respectively. Then $\frac{m_{1}}{m_{2}}$ is equal to: (A) $\frac{a}{b}$ (B) $\frac{b}{a} (\frac{a}{b})^{2}$ (C) $[]^{2}$ (D) $\frac{b}{a}$
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
Since $qV = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ and $r = \frac{mv}{qB}$, combining gives $r = \frac{1}{B}\sqrt{\frac{2mV}{q}}$, so $r \propto \sqrt{m}$ and $\frac{m_1}{m_2} = \left(\frac{a}{b}\right)^2$.

questions.question: Assertion (A): An electron and a proton enter with the same momentum $\vec{p}$ in a magnetic field $\vec{B}$ such that $\vec{p} \perp\vec{B}$. Then both describe a circular path of the same radius. Reason (R): The radius of the circular path described by the charged particle (charge q, mass m) moving in the magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is given by $r = \frac{mv}{qB}$. (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. (D) Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Since $r = \frac{mv}{qB} = \frac{p}{qB}$ and both electron and proton have the same magnitude of charge $q$ and the same momentum $p$ in the same field $B$, they describe circles of equal radius, so both A and R are true and R correctly explains A.

questions.question: A wire of length 4.4 m is bent round in the shape of a circular loop and carries a current of 1.0 A. The magnetic moment of the loop will be: (A) $0.7 Am^{2}$ (B) $1.54 Am^{2}$ (C) $2.10 Am^{2}$ (D) $3.5 Am^{2}$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Circumference $2\pi r = 4.4$ m gives $r = 0.7$ m, so magnetic moment $m = I\pi r^2 = 1.0 \times \pi \times (0.7)^2 = 1.54\ Am^2$.

questions.question: Assertion (A): A proton and an electron enter a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ with the same momentum $\vec{p}$ such that $\vec{p}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{B}$. They describe circular paths of the same radius. Reason (R): In a magnetic field, orbital radius $r$ is equal to $\frac{p}{qB}$. (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. (D) Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Since $r = \frac{p}{qB}$ and both particles have equal charge magnitude $q$ and equal momentum $p$ in the same field $B$, they trace circles of the same radius, so both statements are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.question: A $2.0$ cm segment of wire, carrying $5.0$ A current in positive y-direction lies along y-axis, as shown in the figure. The magnetic field at a point $(3$ m $, 4$ m $, 0)$ due to this segment (part of a circuit) is: (A) $(0.12$ nT $) \hat{j}$ (B) $-(0.10$ nT $) \hat{j}$ (C) $-(0.24$ nT $) \hat{k}$ (D) $(0.24$ nT $) \hat{k}$
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
By the Biot-Savart law, $d\vec{B} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi}\frac{d\vec{l}\times\hat{r}}{r^2}$; with $d\vec{l} = dl\,\hat{j}$ and $\hat{r} = 0.6\hat{i}+0.8\hat{j}$ (since $r=5$ m), $d\vec{l}\times\hat{r} = -0.6\,dl\,\hat{k}$, giving $d\vec{B} = -0.24\ \text{nT}\,\hat{k}$.

questions.question: A circular loop of wire, carrying a current $I$ is lying in xy-plane with its centre coinciding with the origin. It is subjected to a uniform magnetic field pointing along $+z$-axis. The loop will: (A) move along x-axis (B) move along $-y$-axis (C) move along z-axis (D) remain stationary
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
The magnetic moment $\vec{m}$ of the loop is along the $z$-axis, parallel (or antiparallel) to $\vec{B}$, so the torque $\vec{\tau} = \vec{m}\times\vec{B} = 0$ and, being a uniform field, the net force is also zero, so the loop remains stationary.

questions.question: Two thin long parallel wires separated by a distance ’ $a$’ carry current $I$ in opposite directions. The wires will: $2$ (A) Repel each other with a force $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi a^{2}}$ per unit length. $2$ (B) Attract each other with a force $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi a^{2}}$ per unit length. $2$ (C) Attract each other with a force $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi a}$ per unit length. $2$ (D) Repel each other with a force $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi a}$ per unit length.
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
For opposite currents the wires repel each other, with force per unit length $\frac{F}{l} = \frac{\mu_0 I^2}{2\pi a}$.

questions.question: A straight wire is kept horizontally along east-west direction. If a steady current flows in wire from east to west, the magnetic field at a point above the wire will point towards (A) East (B) West (C) North (D) South
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
Taking east as $+\hat{x}$, north as $+\hat{y}$ and up as $+\hat{z}$, the current direction is $-\hat{x}$; using $\vec{B}\propto \hat{I}\times\hat{r}$ with $\hat{r}=\hat{z}$ (point above the wire) gives $(-\hat{x})\times\hat{z} = \hat{y}$, i.e., the field points North.

questions.question: A galvanometer of resistance $100 \Omega$ is converted into an ammeter of range $(0$– $1$ A $)$ using a resistance of $0.1 \Omega$. The ammeter will show full scale deflection for a current of about (A) $0.1$ mA (B) $1$ mA (C) $10$ mA (D) $0.1$ A
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
At full deflection, $I_g G = (I - I_g)S$, so $I_g(100) = (1-I_g)(0.1)$, giving $I_g \approx 1$ mA.

questions.question: A circular loop $A$ of radius $R$ carries a current $I$. Another circular loop $B$ of radius $(^{\frac{R}{2}})$ is placed concentrically in the plane of $A$. The magnetic flux linked with loop $B$ is proportional to (A) $R$ (B) $\sqrt{R} \frac{3}{2}$ (C) $R$ (D) $R^{2}$
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Since $R/2 \ll R$ is not required exactly, but for a small concentric loop the field of $A$ at the centre is $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$ (uniform over $B$'s area), so flux $= B \times \pi\left(\frac{R}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{\mu_0 I \pi R}{8}$, which is proportional to $R$.

questions.question: A particle of mass $m$ and charge $q$ is moving with velocity $\vec{v} = v_{x}\hat{i} + v_{y}\hat{j}$. If it is subjected to a magnetic field $\vec{B} = B_{0}\hat{i}$, it will move in a (A) straight line path (B) circular path (C) helical path (D) parabolic path
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
The component $v_x$ along $\vec{B}$ is unaffected, while $v_y$ produces a force $q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}$ causing circular motion in the plane perpendicular to $\vec{B}$; the combination of uniform motion along $\vec{B}$ and circular motion perpendicular to it gives a helical path.

questions.question: Two long straight parallel conductors $A$ and $B$, kept at a distance $r$, carry current $I$ in opposite directions. A third identical conductor $C$, kept at a distance $(^{\frac{r}{2}})$ from $A$ carries current $I$, in the same direction as in $A$. The net magnetic force on unit length of $C$ is $2$ (A) $\frac{5\mu_{0}I}{2\pi r}$ towards $A 2$ (B) $\frac{5\mu_{0}I}{2\pi r}$ towards $B 2$ (C) $\frac{3\mu_{0}I}{4\pi r}$ towards $A 2$ (D) $\frac{3\mu_{0}I}{4\pi r}$ towards $B$
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Since $C$ carries current in the same direction as $A$, it is attracted towards $A$, and since $B$ carries current opposite to $C$, it is repelled away from $B$; both effects push $C$ towards $A$, so the resultant force per unit length on $C$ is directed towards $A$.

questions.question: Assertion (A): The energy of a charged particle moving in a magnetic field does not change. Reason (R): It is because the work done by the magnetic force on the charge moving in a magnetic field is zero. (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is correct explanation of Assertion (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false. (D) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
The magnetic force $q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}$ is always perpendicular to $\vec{v}$, so it does no work on the charge, leaving its kinetic energy unchanged.

questions.question: A particle of mass $m$ and charge $q$ describes a circular path of radius $R$ in a magnetic field. If its mass and charge were $2m$ and $\frac{q}{2}$ respectively, the radius of its path would be: (A) $\frac{R}{4}$ (B) $\frac{R}{2}$ (C) $2R$ (D) $4R$
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
Since $r = \frac{mv}{qB}$, doubling $m$ and halving $q$ scales $r$ by $\frac{2m}{q/2} \div \frac{m}{q} = 4$, giving radius $4R$.

questions.question: A galvanometer of resistance $50 \Omega$ is converted into a voltmeter of range $(0$- $2$ V $)$ using a resistor of $1.0$ k $\Omega$. If it is to be converted into a voltmeter of range $(0$- $10$ V $)$, the resistance required will be: (A) $4.8$ k $\Omega$ (B) $5.0$ k $\Omega$ (C) $5.2$ k $\Omega$ (D) $5.4$ k $\Omega$
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
From $I_g = \frac{2}{G+R_1} = \frac{2}{50+1000} = \frac{2}{1050}$ A, the new resistance is $R_2 = \frac{10}{I_g} - G = \frac{10 \times 1050}{2} - 50 = 5200\ \Omega = 5.2$ k$\Omega$.

questions.question: A galvanometer shows full scale deflection for a current $I_{g}$. If a shunt of resistance $S_{1}$ is connected to the galvanometer, it gets converted into an ammeter of range $(0$- $I)$. When resistance of the shunt is made $S_{2}$, its range becomes $(0$- $2I)$. Then $\frac{S_{1}}{S_{2}}$ is: (A) $\frac{I+ I_{g}}{I-I_{g}}$ (B) $\frac{I-I_{g}}{I+ I_{g}}$ (C) $\frac{2I-I_{g}}{I-I_{g}}$ (D) $\frac{I-I_{g}}{2I-I_{g}}$
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
Using $I_g G = (I-I_g)S_1$ and $I_g G = (2I-I_g)S_2$, dividing gives $\frac{S_1}{S_2} = \frac{2I-I_g}{I-I_g}$.

questions.question: Two insulated concentric coils, each of radius $R$, placed at right angles to each other, carry currents $I$ and $\sqrt{3} I$ respectively. The magnitude of the net magnetic field at their common centre will be: (A) $\frac{\mu^{0} I}{R}$ (B) $\frac{\mu^{0} I}{2R}$ (C) $\frac{\mu^{0} I}{4R}$ (D) $\frac{2\mu_{0} I}{R}$
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
$B_1 = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$ and $B_2 = \frac{\mu_0 \sqrt{3}I}{2R}$ are perpendicular, so $B_{net} = \sqrt{B_1^2+B_2^2} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}\sqrt{1+3} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{R}$.

questions.question: A galvanometer of resistance $100 \Omega$ gives full scale deflection for a current of $1.0$ mA. It is converted into an ammeter of range $(0$- $1$ A $)$. The resistance of the ammeter will be close to: (A) $0.1 \Omega$ (B) $0.8 \Omega$ (C) $1.0 \Omega$ (D) $10 \Omega$
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
The shunt required is $S = \frac{I_g G}{I-I_g} = \frac{0.001\times100}{0.999} \approx 0.1\ \Omega$, and since $S \ll G$, the ammeter resistance $\frac{GS}{G+S} \approx S \approx 0.1\ \Omega$.

questions.question: Beams of electrons and protons move parallel to each other in the same direction. They (A) attract each other. (B) repel each other. (C) neither attract nor repel. (D) force of attraction or repulsion depends upon speed of beams.
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
An electron moving forward constitutes a conventional current in the opposite direction, so the two beams correspond to antiparallel currents; antiparallel currents repel each other.

questions.question: A long straight wire of radius ’ $a$’ carries a steady current ’ $I$’. The current is uniformly distributed across its area of cross-section. The ratio of magnitude of magnetic field $B_{1}$ at $\frac{a}{2}$ and $B$ at distance $2a$ is $2$ (A) $\frac{1}{2}$ (B) $1$ (C) $2$ (D) $4$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Inside the wire, $B_{1} = \dfrac{\mu_{0}Ir}{2\pi a^{2}}$; at $r = \dfrac{a}{2}$, $B_{1} = \dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{4\pi a}$.
Outside the wire, $B = \dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi r}$; at $r = 2a$, $B = \dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{4\pi a}$.
Hence $\dfrac{B_{1}}{B} = 1$.

questions.question: Assertion (A): When radius of a circular loop carrying a steady current is doubled, its magnetic moment becomes four times. Reason (R): The magnetic moment of a circular loop carrying a steady current is proportional to the area of the loop. (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. (D) Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Magnetic moment $m = IA = I\pi r^{2}$, so $m \propto r^{2}$; doubling $r$ makes $m$ four times, and this proportionality to area is exactly the reason stated.

questions.question: Which of the following graphs correctly represents the variation of the magnitude of the magnetic field outside a straight infinite current-carrying wire of radius ’ $a$’, as a function of distance ’ $r$’ from the centre of the wire? (A) Graph (a) (B) Graph (b) (C) Graph (c) (D) Graph (d)
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Outside the wire ($r > a$), the field is $B = \dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi r}$, so $B$ falls off smoothly as $\dfrac{1}{r}$, joining continuously (no discontinuity) with the linearly rising field $B = \dfrac{\mu_{0}Ir}{2\pi a^{2}}$ inside the wire at $r=a$.

questions.question: A particle of mass $m$ and charge $q$ moving with a uniform velocity $\vec{v} = v_{0x}\hat{i} + v_{0y} \hat{j}$ enters a region with a magnetic field $\vec{B} = B_{0} \hat{j}$. After some time, an electric field $\vec{E} = E_{0} \hat{j}$ is also switched on in the region. The resulting path described by the particle will be: (A) a circle in $x$- $z$ plane (B) a parabola in $x$- $y$ plane (C) a helix with constant pitch (D) a helix with increasing pitch
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
With only $\vec{B} = B_{0}\hat{j}$, the component $v_{0x}$ produces circular motion in the $x$-$z$ plane while $v_{0y}$ (parallel to $\vec{B}$) stays unaffected, giving a helix of constant pitch.
Once $\vec{E} = E_{0}\hat{j}$ is switched on, it accelerates the particle along $\hat{j}$ (parallel to $B$, so it does not disturb the circular motion), making the axial velocity increase with time.
Since the pitch depends on this increasing axial velocity while the circular period stays fixed, the path becomes a helix with increasing pitch.

questions.question: In a moving coil galvanometer, the deflecting torque $\tau$ acting on the coil is related to the current $I$ flowing through it as: (A) $\tau \propto I^{3}$ (B) $\tau \propto I^{2}$ (C) $\tau \propto I$ (D) $\tau \propto\sqrt{I}$
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
In a moving coil galvanometer $\tau = NIAB$, so for fixed $N$, $A$, $B$, the torque is directly proportional to $I$, giving a linear scale.

questions.question: Two thin long parallel wires $A$ and $B$ are separated by a distance $r$ and carry current $I$ each in the same direction. The force per unit length exerted by $A$ on wire $B$ is: $2$ (A) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{2r}$, attractive $2$ (B) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{r}$, repulsive $2$ (C) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi r}$, attractive $2$ (D) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi r}$, repulsive
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
For two parallel wires carrying currents $I$ each, the force per unit length is $\dfrac{F}{l} = \dfrac{\mu_{0}I^{2}}{2\pi r}$, and since the currents are in the same direction the force is attractive.

questions.question: Assertion (A): A current carrying square loop made of a wire of length $L$ is placed in a magnetic field. It experiences a torque which is greater than the torque on a circular loop made of the same wire carrying the same current in the same magnetic field. Reason (R): A square loop occupies more area than a circular loop, both made of wire of the same length. (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. (D) Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
For a given wire length $L$, the circular loop encloses the largest possible area, so a square loop (same length) has smaller area, smaller magnetic moment $m = IA$, and hence smaller torque $\tau = mB\sin\theta$ than the circular loop — the opposite of what the Assertion claims, so both Assertion and Reason are false.

questions.question: An electron enters a uniform magnetic field with speed $v$. It describes a semicircular path and comes out of the field. The final speed of the electron is: (A) Zero (B) $v$ (C) $\frac{v}{2}$ (D) $2v$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
The magnetic force $q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}$ is always perpendicular to velocity and does no work, so it changes only the direction, not the magnitude, of velocity; the final speed remains $v$.

questions.question: Assertion (A): The deflecting torque acting on a current carrying loop is zero when its plane is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field. Reason (R): The deflecting torque acting on a loop of magnetic moment $\vec{m}$ in a magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is given by the dot product of $\vec{m}$ and $\vec{B}$. (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false. (D) Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
When the loop's plane is perpendicular to $\vec{B}$, its magnetic moment $\vec{m}$ (normal to the plane) is parallel to $\vec{B}$, so $\theta = 0$ and $\tau = mB\sin\theta = 0$, making Assertion true.
However, the torque on a current loop is given by the cross product $\vec{\tau} = \vec{m}\times\vec{B}$, not the dot product, so Reason is false.

questions.question: Two long parallel wires kept 2 m apart carry 3A current each, in the same direction. The force per unit length on one wire due to the other is (A) $4.5 \times 10^{5}$ N/m, attractive (B) $4.5 \times 10^{-7}$ N/m, repulsive (C) $9 \times 10^{-7}$ N/m, repulsive (D) $9 \times 10^{5}$ N/m, attractive
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
Force per unit length $= \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d} = \frac{2\times 10^{-7}\times 3\times 3}{2} = 9\times 10^{-7}$ N/m, and since the currents are in the same direction the wires attract each other.

questions.question: Two horizontal thin long parallel wires, separated by a distance r carry current I each in the opposite directions. The net magnetic field at a point midway between them, will be (A) zero (B) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{\pi r}$, vertically downward (C) $\frac{2\mu_{0}I}{\pi r}$, vertically upward (D) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{\pi r}$, vertically downward
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
Each wire produces $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi (r/2)} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{\pi r}$ at the midpoint, and since the currents are anti-parallel, the fields from both wires add up in the same direction, giving $B_{net} = \frac{2\mu_0 I}{\pi r}$, vertically upward.

questions.question: Two statements are given - one labelled Assertion (A) and the other labelled Reason (R). Select the correct answer to this question from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false. (D) Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false. Assertion (A): Higher the range of an ammeter, smaller is its resistance. Reason (R): To increase the range of the ammeter, additional shunt needs to be connected across it.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
A smaller resistance (obtained by connecting a smaller value shunt in parallel with the galvanometer) allows a larger fraction of current to bypass through the shunt, thereby increasing the range of the ammeter.

questions.question: The magnetic dipole moment of a current carrying coil does not depend upon (A) number of turns of the coil. (B) cross-sectional area of the coil. (C) current flowing in the coil. (D) material of the turns of the coil.
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
$m = NIA$ depends on the number of turns, area and current, but not on the material of the wire used to make the turns.

questions.question: An electron is released from rest in a region of uniform electric and magnetic fields acting parallel to each other. The electron will (A) move in a straight line. (B) move in a circle. (C) remain stationary. (D) move in a helical path.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Since the electron starts from rest and $E \parallel B$, its velocity always remains along the field direction, so $v \times B = 0$ and only the electric force acts, accelerating it in a straight line.

questions.question: A straight current carrying conductor is placed inside a uniform magnetic field. The force per unit length acting on the conductor is (A) maximum when the conductor is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field. (B) maximum when the conductor is along the direction of magnetic field. (C) minimum when the conductor is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field. (D) minimum when the conductor makes an angle of $45^{^{\circ}}$ with the direction of magnetic field.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
$\frac{F}{l} = BI\sin\theta$ is maximum at $\theta = 90^{\circ}$, i.e., when the conductor is perpendicular to the magnetic field.

questions.question: An isosceles right angled current carrying loop PQR is placed in a uniform magnetic field $B$ pointing along PR. If the magnetic force acting on the arm PQ is $F$, then the magnetic force which acts on the arm QR will be (A) $F$ (B) $\frac{F}{\sqrt{2}}$ (C) $\sqrt{2} F$ (D) $-F$
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
For a closed current loop, $F_{PQ} + F_{QR} + F_{RP} = 0$; since $F_{RP} = 0$ (PR is along $B$), $F_{QR} = -F_{PQ} = -F$.

questions.question: A region has a uniform magnetic field in it. A proton enters into the region with velocity making an angle of $45^{^{\circ}}$ with the direction of the magnetic field. In this region the proton will move on a path having the shape of a (A) straight line (B) circle (C) spiral (D) helix
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
The velocity component along $B$ causes uniform motion along the field while the perpendicular component causes circular motion, and together they produce a helical path.

questions.question: A current $I$ flows through a long straight conductor which is bent into a circular loop of radius $R$ in the middle as shown in the figure. The magnitude of the net magnetic field at point $O$ will be (A) Zero $[]$ (B) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{2R}1 + \frac{1}{\pi}$ (C) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{4\pi R} []$ (D) $\frac{\mu_{0}I}{2R}1 -\frac{1}{\pi}$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
The circular part contributes $\frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$ at $O$, and the two straight (tangential) segments, each a semi-infinite wire at perpendicular distance $R$ from $O$, contribute $\frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi R}$; adding these gives $B_O = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2R}\left(1+\frac{1}{\pi}\right)$.

questions.question: A circular loop of radius $r$, carrying a current $I$ lies in $y$- $z$ plane with its centre at the origin. The net magnetic flux through the loop is: (A) directly proportional to $r$ (B) zero (C) inversely proportional to $r$ (D) directly proportional to $I$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
By symmetry, the magnetic field lines of the current loop that pass through the plane in one direction on one side return through the plane in the opposite direction on the other side, so the net flux through the plane of the loop is zero.

questions.question: A current of $10$ A is flowing from east to west in a long straight wire kept on a horizontal table. The magnetic field developed at a distance of $10$ cm due north on the table is: (A) $2 \times 10^{-5}$ T, acting downwards (B) $2 \times 10^{-5}$ T, acting upwards (C) $4 \times 10^{-5}$ T, acting downwards (D) $4 \times 10^{-5}$ T, acting upwards
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Using $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi d} = \frac{2\times10^{-7}\times10}{0.1} = 2\times10^{-5}$ T, and applying the right-hand rule to a current flowing westward with the field point due north, $\vec{B}$ points vertically downward.

questions.question: An electron and a proton are moving along the same direction with the same kinetic energy. They enter a uniform magnetic field acting perpendicular to their velocities. The dependence of radius of their paths on their masses is: (A) $r \propto m$ (B) $r \propto\sqrt{m}$ (C) $r \propto\frac{1}{m}$ (D) $r \propto\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Since $KE = \frac{p^2}{2m}$, $p = \sqrt{2mKE}$, and $r = \frac{p}{qB} = \frac{\sqrt{2mKE}}{qB}$, so for the same $KE$ and $q$, $r \propto \sqrt{m}$.

questions.question: There are uniform electric and magnetic fields in a region pointing along $X$-axis. An $\alpha$-particle is projected along $Y$ -axis with a velocity $v$. The shape of the trajectory will be (A) circular in $XZ$ plane (B) circular in $Y Z$ plane (C) helical with its axis parallel to $X$-axis (D) helical with its axis parallel to $Y$ -axis
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
The magnetic force ($q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}$) makes the particle circle in the $YZ$ plane, while the electric force $q\vec{E}$ (along $X$) continuously accelerates it along $X$, so the resultant path is a helix whose axis is parallel to the $X$-axis.

questions.question: Define the term ’current sensitivity’ of a moving coil galvanometer.
questions.answer:
Current sensitivity is the deflection produced in the galvanometer per unit current flowing through it.
It is given by $I_s = \dfrac{\theta}{I} = \dfrac{NBA}{k}$, where $N$, $B$, $A$ are the number of turns, magnetic field and coil area, and $k$ is the torsional constant of the suspension.

questions.question: An electron moves along $+x$ direction. It enters into a region of uniform magnetic field $B$ directed along $-z$ direction as shown in fig. Draw the shape of trajectory followed by the electron after entering the field. OR A square shaped current carrying loop $MNOP$ is placed near a straight long current carrying wire $AB$ as shown in the fig. The wire and the loop lie in the same plane. If the loop experiences a net force $F$ towards the wire, find the magnitude of the force on the side $NO$ of the loop.
questions.answer:
The electron moves in a circle in the $xy$-plane (perpendicular to $\vec{B}$), since the magnetic force $\vec{F} = -e(\vec{v}\times\vec{B})$ always acts perpendicular to its velocity, producing uniform circular motion of radius $r = \dfrac{mv}{eB}$.
With $\vec{v}$ along $+x$ and $\vec{B}$ along $-z$, the initial force is along $-y$, so the electron curves clockwise as viewed from the $+z$ axis, tracing a circle of radius $r$ in the plane of the page.

questions.question: A charge particle after being accelerated through a potential difference $V$ enters in a uniform magnetic field and moves in a circle of radius $r$. If $V$ is doubled, the radius of the circle will become (A) $2r$ (B) $\sqrt{2} r$ (C) $4r$ (D) $r/\sqrt{2}$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Since $r = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mqV}}{qB} \propto \sqrt{V}$, doubling $V$ makes the new radius $\sqrt{2}\,r$.

questions.question: A proton is accelerated through a potential difference $V$, subjected to a uniform magnetic field acting normal to the velocity of the proton. If the potential difference is doubled, how will the radius of the circular path described by the proton in the magnetic field change?
questions.answer: Since $r = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mqV}}{qB} \propto \sqrt{V}$, doubling the potential difference increases the radius by a factor of $\sqrt{2}$, i.e., the new radius becomes $\sqrt{2}\,r$.

questions.question: Write the relation for the force acting on a charged particle $q$ moving with velocity $\vec{v}$ in the presence of a magnetic field $\vec{B}$.
questions.answer: $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v}\times\vec{B})$

questions.question: When a charge $q$ is moving in the presence of electric ($\vec{E}$) and magnetic ($\vec{B}$) fields which are perpendicular to each other and also perpendicular to the velocity $\vec{v}$ of the particle, write the relation expressing $\vec{v}$ in terms of $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$.
questions.answer: For the particle to move undeflected, the electric and magnetic forces must balance: $qE = qvB$, giving $\vec{v} = \dfrac{\vec{E}\times\vec{B}}{B^2}$.

questions.question: A proton and an electron travelling along parallel paths enter a region of uniform magnetic field, acting perpendicular to their paths. Which of them will move in a circular path with higher frequency?
questions.answer: The electron moves with higher frequency, since $f = \dfrac{qB}{2\pi m}$ is inversely proportional to mass, and the electron's mass is much smaller than the proton's.

questions.question: What can be the cause of helical motion of a charged particle?
questions.answer:
The charged particle enters the magnetic field with a velocity that has both a component parallel to $\vec{B}$ and a component perpendicular to $\vec{B}$.
The perpendicular component causes circular motion while the parallel component causes uniform motion along $\vec{B}$, together producing a helical path.

questions.question: Write the expression, in a vector form, for the Lorentz magnetic force $\vec{F}$ due to a charge moving with velocity $\vec{V}$ in a magnetic field $\vec{B}$. What is the direction of the magnetic force?
questions.answer:
$\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$
The force is directed perpendicular to the plane containing $\vec{v}$ and $\vec{B}$, as given by the right-hand rule.

questions.question: Using the concept of force between two infinitely long parallel current carrying conductors, define one ampere of current.
questions.answer: One ampere is that constant current which, if maintained in each of two infinitely long, straight, parallel conductors of negligible cross-section placed $1$ m apart in vacuum, produces a force of $2 \times 10^{-7}$ N per metre of length between them.

questions.question: An electron and a proton, moving parallel to each other in the same direction with equal momenta, enter into a uniform magnetic field which is at right angles to their velocities. Trace their trajectories in the magnetic field.
questions.answer:
Since $r = p/(qB)$ and both have equal momentum $p$ and equal magnitude of charge $q$, they move in circles of the same radius.
Because the electron and proton carry opposite charges, they curve in opposite senses (one clockwise, the other anticlockwise).

questions.question: A narrow beam of protons and deuterons, each having the same momentum, enters a region of uniform magnetic field directed perpendicular to their direction of momentum. What would be the ratio of the radii of the circular paths described by them?
questions.answer:
The ratio is $1:1$.
Since $r = p/(qB)$, and both proton and deuteron carry the same charge magnitude $e$ with equal momentum $p$ in the same field $B$, their radii are equal.

questions.question: Magnetic field lines can be entirely confined within the core of a toroid, but not within a straight solenoid. Why?
questions.answer:
A toroid is an endless (closed) ring-shaped solenoid with no free ends, so the field lines form closed loops entirely within its core.
A straight solenoid has two open ends, so field lines must emerge from one end, pass through the surrounding space, and re-enter the other end, hence they cannot be confined within it.

questions.question: An electron does not suffer any deflection while passing through a region of uniform magnetic field. What is the direction of the magnetic field?
questions.answer:
The magnetic field must be parallel or antiparallel to the electron's velocity.
Then $\vec{v} \times \vec{B} = 0$, so the force $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$ is zero and the electron passes undeflected.

questions.question: What is the direction of the force acting on a charged particle $q$, moving with a velocity $\vec{v}$ in a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$?
questions.answer: The force is directed perpendicular to both $\vec{v}$ and $\vec{B}$, along $\vec{v} \times \vec{B}$ (reversed if $q$ is negative), as given by the right-hand rule.

questions.question: An electron is moving along $+ve x$-axis in the presence of uniform magnetic field along $+ve y$-axis. What is the direction of the force acting on it?
questions.answer:
Using $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$ with $\vec{v}$ along $+x$ and $\vec{B}$ along $+y$, $\vec{v} \times \vec{B}$ points along $+z$.
Since the electron's charge is negative, the force acts along the $-z$ direction.

questions.question: An electron beam projected along $+X$-axis, experiences a force due to a magnetic field along the $+Y$ -axis. What is the direction of the magnetic field?
questions.answer:
The magnetic field must be along the $+z$ direction.
This follows because for an electron (negative charge) moving along $+x$, the force $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$ points along $+y$ only when $\vec{B}$ is along $+z$.

questions.question: In the diagram below is shown a circular loop carrying current I. Show the direction of the magnetic field with the help of lines of force.
questions.answer:
The magnetic field lines are concentric circles close to the wire, becoming larger loops away from it, and along the axis they are straight lines perpendicular to the plane of the loop.
Their direction is given by the right-hand rule: curl the fingers along the direction of current $I$; the thumb points along $\vec{B}$ at the centre.

questions.question: A wire of length $L$ is bent round into (i) a square coil having $N$ turns and (ii) a circular coil having $N$ turns. The coil in both cases is free to turn about a vertical axis coinciding with the plane of the coil, in a uniform, horizontal magnetic field and carry the same currents. Find the ratio of the maximum value of the torque acting on the square coil to that on the circular coil.
questions.answer:
For the square coil: side $a = L/4N$, so magnetic moment $m_s = NIa^2 = IL^2/16N$.
For the circular coil: radius $r = L/2\pi N$, so $m_c = NI\pi r^2 = IL^2/4\pi N$.
Maximum torque $\tau_{max} = mB$, so $\dfrac{\tau_s}{\tau_c} = \dfrac{m_s}{m_c} = \dfrac{1/16}{1/4\pi} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

questions.question: A voltmeter of resistance $1000 \Omega$ can measure up to $25$ V. How will you convert it so that it can read up to $250$ V?
questions.answer:
To extend the range, a high resistance $R$ must be connected in series with the voltmeter.
Full-scale current $I_g = \dfrac{25}{1000} = 0.025$ A must remain the same for $250$ V, so $1000 + R = \dfrac{250}{0.025} = 10000\ \Omega$, giving $R = 9000\ \Omega$.
Thus a $9000\ \Omega$ resistor connected in series with the voltmeter converts it to a $0$–$250$ V voltmeter.

questions.question: A circular coil of wire having $200$ turns, each of radius $4.0$ cm is placed in a horizontal plane. It carries a current of $0.40$ A in clockwise direction. Find the magnitude and direction of the magnetic field at the centre of the coil.
questions.answer:
$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 N I}{2r} = \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 200 \times 0.40}{2 \times 0.04}$
$B = 1.26 \times 10^{-3}$ T.
Since the current flows clockwise as seen from above, by the right-hand rule the field at the centre points vertically downward.

questions.question: A current of $5$ A is passing along $+X$ direction through a wire lying along $X$-axis. Find the magnetic field $\vec{B}$ at a point $\vec{r} = (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j})$ m due to $1$ cm element of the wire, centered at origin.
questions.answer:
By Biot-Savart law, $d\vec{B} = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I\, d\vec{l} \times \hat{r}}{r^2}$, with $d\vec{l} = 0.01\,\hat{i}$ m, $\vec{r} = 3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}$ m, $r = 5$ m, $\hat{r} = 0.6\hat{i}+0.8\hat{j}$.
$d\vec{l} \times \hat{r} = 0.01(0.8)\hat{k} = 8\times10^{-3}\hat{k}$
$d\vec{B} = 10^{-7} \times \dfrac{5 \times 8\times 10^{-3}}{25}\hat{k} = 1.6 \times 10^{-10}\ \text{T}\,\hat{k}$, i.e., directed out of the plane along $+z$.

questions.question: Derive an expression for magnetic force $\vec{F}$ acting on a straight conductor of length $L$ carrying current $I$ in an external magnetic field $\vec{B}$. Is it valid when the conductor is in zig-zag form? Justify.
questions.answer:
Consider a straight conductor of length $L$, area of cross-section $A$, carrying current $I$ with free electron drift velocity $v_d$, placed in field $\vec{B}$.
Force on each charge carrier $= q\vec{v_d} \times \vec{B}$; total number of carriers $= nAL$.
So total force $\vec{F} = nAL\, q\vec{v_d}\times\vec{B} = I\vec{L}\times\vec{B}$, since $I = nAqv_d$.
Yes, it is valid for a zig-zag conductor because the force depends only on the vector $\vec{L}$ joining the two end points (in uniform $\vec{B}$), not on the actual path, as the individual force elements $Id\vec{l}\times\vec{B}$ sum vectorially to $I\vec{L}\times\vec{B}$.

questions.question: An alpha particle is projected with velocity $\vec{V} = (3.0 \times 10^{5}$ m/s $)\hat{i}$ into a region in which magnetic field $\vec{B} = [(0.4$ T $)\hat{i} + (0.3$ T $) \hat{j}]$ exists. Calculate the acceleration of the particle in the region. $\hat{i}$, $\hat{j}$ and $\hat{k}$ are unit vectors along $x$, $y$ and $z$ axis respectively and charge to mass ratio for alpha particle is $4.8 \times 10^{7}$ C/kg.
questions.answer:
Force $\vec{F} = q\vec{v}\times\vec{B} = q(v\hat{i})\times(B_x\hat{i}+B_y\hat{j}) = qvB_y\hat{k}$ (since $\hat{i}\times\hat{i}=0$).
Acceleration $\vec{a} = \dfrac{q}{m}vB_y\hat{k} = 4.8\times10^{7}\times 3.0\times10^{5}\times 0.3\,\hat{k}$
$\vec{a} = 4.32 \times 10^{12}\ \text{m/s}^2\,\hat{k}$, directed along the $+z$ axis.

questions.question: Briefly explain why and how a galvanometer is converted into an ammeter.
questions.answer:
A galvanometer has a coil of high resistance and can carry only a small current (of the order of mA) for full-scale deflection, so it cannot directly measure large currents.
It is converted into an ammeter by connecting a low resistance shunt $S$ in parallel with it, so that most of the current bypasses the galvanometer, and only a small fraction passes through the coil, giving full-scale deflection for the desired maximum current $I$: $S = \dfrac{I_g G}{I - I_g}$.

questions.question: A wire of length $l$ is in the form of a circular loop $A$ of one turn. This loop is reshaped into loop $B$ of three turns. Find the ratio of the magnetic fields at the centres of loop $A$ and loop $B$ for the same current through them.
questions.answer:
Radius of loop $A$: $2\pi r_A = l \Rightarrow r_A = l/2\pi$; field $B_A = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2r_A} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I \pi}{l}$.
Radius of loop $B$: $3(2\pi r_B) = l \Rightarrow r_B = l/6\pi$; field $B_B = \dfrac{\mu_0 (3) I}{2r_B} = \dfrac{9\pi \mu_0 I}{l}$.
Ratio $B_A : B_B = 1 : 9$.

questions.question: Two wires of equal lengths are shaped in the form of a square loop and a circular loop. Both loops are suspended in a uniform magnetic field. Prove that for the same current, the circular loop will experience larger torque.
questions.answer:
Let both loops be made from the same wire of length $L$, carrying current $I$ in field $B$.
Square loop: side $a = L/4$, area $A_s = a^2 = L^2/16$; torque $\tau_s = IA_sB = \dfrac{IL^2B}{16}$.
Circular loop: radius $r = L/2\pi$, area $A_c = \pi r^2 = L^2/4\pi$; torque $\tau_c = IA_cB = \dfrac{IL^2B}{4\pi}$.
Since $4\pi \approx 12.57 < 16$, $A_c > A_s$, so $\tau_c > \tau_s$; in fact $\dfrac{\tau_c}{\tau_s} = \dfrac{4}{\pi} \approx 1.27$, proving the circular loop experiences the larger torque for the same perimeter of wire.

questions.question: A wire of length $L$ is bent round in the form of (i) a square, and then (ii) an equilateral triangle. If current $I$ is passed through each of them, find the ratio of magnetic moment of the square loop to that of the triangle.
questions.answer:
Square: side $= L/4$, so magnetic moment $M_1 = I\left(\dfrac{L}{4}\right)^2 = \dfrac{IL^2}{16}$
Equilateral triangle: side $= L/3$, so magnetic moment $M_2 = I \times \dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}\left(\dfrac{L}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{\sqrt3\,IL^2}{36}$
Ratio $M_1 : M_2 = 3\sqrt3 : 4$

questions.question: A particle of charge $q$ and mass $m$ starts moving with uniform velocity $v\hat{i}$. Specify the direction of magnetic field which should be set up in the region so that the particle moves (a) straight undeviated, and (b) in a circle. Justify your answers.
questions.answer:
(a) $\vec{B}$ must be along $\pm\hat{i}$ (parallel or antiparallel to $\vec{v}$), since then $\vec{F} = q\vec{v}\times\vec{B} = 0$ and the particle moves straight undeviated.
(b) $\vec{B}$ must be perpendicular to $\vec{v}$, e.g. along $\hat{j}$ or $\hat{k}$, since then the force $qvB$ acts perpendicular to velocity at every instant and provides the centripetal force needed for circular motion.

questions.question: (a) Write the expression for the Lorentz force on a particle of charge $q$ moving with a velocity $\vec{v}$ in a magnetic field $\vec{B}$. When is the magnitude of this force maximum? Show that no work is done by this force on the particle during its motion from a point $\vec{r}_{1}$ to point $\vec{r}_{2}$. OR (b) A long straight wire AB carries a current I. A particle (mass m and charge q) moves with a velocity $\vec{v}$, parallel to the wire, at a distance d from it as shown in the figure. Obtain the expression for the force experienced by the particle and mention its directions.
questions.answer:
(a) The Lorentz force is $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v}\times\vec{B})$, with magnitude $F = qvB\sin\theta$, which is maximum $(=qvB)$ when $\vec{v} \perp \vec{B}$ (i.e. $\theta = 90^\circ$).
Since $\vec{F}$ is always perpendicular to $\vec{v}$, $\vec{F}\cdot\vec{v} = 0$ at every instant, so $dW = \vec{F}\cdot d\vec{r} = (\vec{F}\cdot\vec{v})\,dt = 0$.
Hence $W = \int_{\vec{r}_1}^{\vec{r}_2} dW = 0$; the magnetic force does no work on the particle.
OR
(b) The wire produces a field at the particle's location of magnitude $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi d}$, circling the wire.
Since $\vec{v}$ is parallel to the wire and $\vec{B}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{v}$, the force is $F = qvB = \dfrac{\mu_0 I q v}{2\pi d}$.
This force acts radially, directed towards or away from the wire (perpendicular to both $\vec{v}$ and the wire), depending on the sign of $q$ and the direction of $I$.

questions.question: (a) Two identical circular loops P and Q, each of radius R carrying current I are kept in perpendicular planes such that they have a common centre O as shown in the figure. Find the magnitude and direction of the net magnetic field at the point O. OR (b) A long straight conductor kept along $X^{'}X$ axis, carries a steady current $I$ along $+x$ direction. At an instant $t$, a particle of mass $m$ and charge $q$ at point $(x, y)$ moves with a velocity $v$ along $+y$ direction. Find the magnitude and direction of the force on the particle due to the conductor.
questions.answer:
(a) Field due to each loop at centre $O$: $B_P = B_Q = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$, directed along the respective loop axes, which are mutually perpendicular.
Net field: $B = \sqrt{B_P^2+B_Q^2} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{\sqrt2\,R}$, directed at $45^\circ$ to the planes of both loops (along the bisector of the two axes).
OR
(b) Field due to the wire at $(x,y)$: $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi y}$, directed out of the plane (along $\hat{k}$, by the right-hand rule), since the perpendicular distance of the particle from the wire is $y$.
Force on the particle: $F = qvB = \dfrac{\mu_0 I q v}{2\pi y}$, directed along the $x$-axis (parallel to the wire, sense depending on the sign of $q$), since $\vec{F} = q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}$ with $\vec{v}$ along $\hat{j}$ and $\vec{B}$ along $\hat{k}$.

questions.question: Two long straight parallel wires $A$ and $B$ separated by a distance $d$, carry equal current $I$ flowing in same direction as shown in the figure. (a) Find the magnetic field at a point $P$ situated between them at a distance $x$ from one wire. (b) Show graphically the variation of the magnetic field with distance $x$ for $0 < x < d$.
questions.answer:
(a) Field due to wire $A$ (distance $x$): $B_A = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi x}$; field due to wire $B$ (distance $d-x$): $B_B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi(d-x)}$.
Since the currents are in the same direction, these fields at $P$ are opposite in direction, so the net field is $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi}\left(\dfrac{1}{x} - \dfrac{1}{d-x}\right)$.
(b) The graph shows $B \to \infty$ as $x \to 0$, $B = 0$ at $x = d/2$, and $B \to -\infty$ (field reverses direction) as $x \to d$, giving an asymmetric curve about the midpoint.

questions.question: An ammeter of resistance $0.8 \Omega$ can measure a current up to $1.0$ A. Find the value of shunt resistance required to convert this ammeter to measure a current up to $5.0$ A.
questions.answer:
Shunt condition: $I_g G = (I-I_g)S$
$S = \dfrac{I_g G}{I - I_g} = \dfrac{1.0 \times 0.8}{5.0 - 1.0} = 0.2\ \Omega$
A shunt of $0.2\ \Omega$ must be connected in parallel with the ammeter.

questions.question: A galvanometer of resistance $16 \Omega$ shows full scale deflection for a current of $4$ mA. How will you convert it into a voltmeter to measure a voltage up to $3$ V?
questions.answer:
To convert into a voltmeter, connect a high resistance $R$ in series with the galvanometer such that $V = I_g(G+R)$.
$R = \dfrac{V}{I_g} - G = \dfrac{3}{4\times10^{-3}} - 16 = 750 - 16 = 734\ \Omega$
A resistance of $734\ \Omega$ should be connected in series with the galvanometer.

questions.question: A circular loop carrying a current $5$ A, produces a magnetic field of $\pi$ mT, at its centre. Find the value of the magnetic moment of the loop.
questions.answer:
$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R} \Rightarrow R = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2B} = \dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times5}{2\pi\times10^{-3}} = 1\times10^{-3}\ \text{m}$
Magnetic moment $M = I\pi R^2 = 5\times\pi\times(10^{-3})^2 = 1.57\times10^{-5}\ \text{A m}^2$

questions.question: An $\alpha$-particle and a proton of the same kinetic energy are in turn allowed to pass through a magnetic field $\vec{B}$, acting normal to the direction of motion of the particles. Calculate the ratio of radii of the circular paths described by them.
questions.answer:
Radius in a magnetic field for a given kinetic energy: $r = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mK}}{qB}$, so $r \propto \dfrac{\sqrt{m}}{q}$.
For the $\alpha$-particle, $m_\alpha = 4m_p$, $q_\alpha = 2e$; for the proton, $m_p$, $e$.
$\dfrac{r_\alpha}{r_p} = \dfrac{\sqrt{4m_p}}{2e}\times\dfrac{e}{\sqrt{m_p}} = \dfrac{2}{2} = 1$, so the ratio is $1:1$.

questions.question: A deuteron and an alpha particle having same momentum are in turn allowed to pass through a magnetic field $\vec{B}$, acting normal to the direction of motion of the particles. Calculate the ratio of the radii of the circular paths described by them.
questions.answer:
Radius for a given momentum: $r = \dfrac{p}{qB}$, so $r \propto \dfrac{1}{q}$ (since $p$ and $B$ are same for both).
For deuteron $q_d = e$; for $\alpha$-particle $q_\alpha = 2e$.
$\dfrac{r_d}{r_\alpha} = \dfrac{q_\alpha}{q_d} = \dfrac{2e}{e} = 2$, so the ratio is $2:1$.

questions.question: A charged particle $q$ is moving in the presence of a magnetic field $\vec{B}$ which is inclined to an angle $30^{^{\circ}}$ with the direction of the motion of the particle. Draw the trajectory followed by the particle in the presence of the field and explain how the particle describes this path.
questions.answer:
The particle traces a helical path with its axis along $\vec{B}$.
The velocity resolves into two components: $v\cos30^{\circ}$ along $\vec{B}$ and $v\sin30^{\circ}$ perpendicular to $\vec{B}$.
The parallel component is unaffected since $\vec{F}=q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}=0$ along $\vec{B}$, so the particle moves with uniform velocity in that direction.
The perpendicular component experiences a force $F=qv\sin30^{\circ}B$ that acts as centripetal force, producing uniform circular motion; the combination of the two gives a helical (spiral) trajectory around the field lines.

questions.question: A long straight wire AB carries a current of 4 A. A proton P travels at $4\times10^{6}$ m s $-1$ parallel to the wire $0.2$ m from it and in a direction opposite to the current as shown in the figure. Calculate the force which the magnetic field due to the current carrying wire exerts on the proton. Also specify its direction.
questions.answer:
Magnetic field due to the wire at the proton: $B=\dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi r}=\dfrac{2\times10^{-7}\times4}{0.2}=4\times10^{-6}$ T.
Force on the proton: $F=qvB=1.6\times10^{-19}\times4\times10^{6}\times4\times10^{-6}=2.56\times10^{-18}$ N.
Since the proton moves antiparallel to the current (like antiparallel currents, which repel), the force is directed away from the wire.

questions.question: Two long straight wires carrying currents of $2$ A and $5$ A in the same direction are kept parallel, $10$ cm apart from each other. Calculate the force acting between them and write its nature.
questions.answer:
Force per unit length between two long parallel currents: $\dfrac{F}{l}=\dfrac{\mu_{0}I_{1}I_{2}}{2\pi d}$.
Substituting, $\dfrac{F}{l}=\dfrac{2\times10^{-7}\times2\times5}{0.1}=2\times10^{-5}$ N m$^{-1}$.
Since the currents are in the same direction, the force is attractive.

questions.question: (a) Obtain the conditions under which an electron does not suffer any deflection while passing through a magnetic field. (b) Two protons P and Q moving with the same speed pass through the magnetic fields $B_{1}$ and $\vec{B}_{2}$ respectively, at right angles to the field directions. If $|\vec{B}_{1}| > |\vec{B}_{2}|$, which of the two protons will describe the circular path of smaller radius? Explain.
questions.answer:
(a) The force on the electron is $\vec{F}=q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}$, which is zero when $\vec{v}$ is parallel or antiparallel to $\vec{B}$ (i.e., $\theta=0^{\circ}$ or $180^{\circ}$), since $\sin\theta=0$; hence the electron passes through undeflected only when it moves along the direction of the field.
(b) The radius of the circular path is $r=\dfrac{mv}{qB}$, so $r\propto\dfrac{1}{B}$ for the same $m$, $v$, and $q$.
Since $|\vec{B}_{1}|>|\vec{B}_{2}|$, proton P describes the circular path of smaller radius.

questions.question: Two identical coils P and Q each of radius R are lying in perpendicular planes such that they have a common centre. Find the magnitude and direction of the magnetic field at the common centre when they carry currents equal to $I$ and $\sqrt{3} I$ respectively.
questions.answer:
Field due to each coil at the centre: $B_{1}=\dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{2R}$ and $B_{2}=\dfrac{\mu_{0}\sqrt{3}I}{2R}$, mutually perpendicular.
Resultant: $B=\sqrt{B_{1}^{2}+B_{2}^{2}}=\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{2R}\right)^{2}+3\left(\dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{2R}\right)^{2}}=\dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{R}$.
Direction: it makes an angle $\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{B_{2}}{B_{1}}\right)=\tan^{-1}(\sqrt{3})=60^{\circ}$ with $B_{1}$ (the field of coil P).

questions.question: Two coils P and Q of radius R and 2R respectively are lying in perpendicular planes having a common centre. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant magnetic field at the common centre, if they carry the currents $I$ and $2\sqrt{3} I$ respectively.
questions.answer:
Field due to coil P: $B_{1}=\dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{2R}$; field due to coil Q: $B_{2}=\dfrac{\mu_{0}(2\sqrt{3}I)}{2(2R)}=\dfrac{\mu_{0}\sqrt{3}I}{2R}$, mutually perpendicular.
Resultant: $B=\sqrt{B_{1}^{2}+B_{2}^{2}}=\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{2R}\right)^{2}+3\left(\dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{2R}\right)^{2}}=\dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{R}$.
It makes an angle $\theta=\tan^{-1}(\sqrt{3})=60^{\circ}$ with $B_{1}$ (the field of coil P).

questions.question: Two coils P and Q of radius R and 2R are lying in the same plane with their centres coinciding. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant magnetic field at the common centre if they respectively carry currents $3I$ and $2I$ in opposite directions.
questions.answer:
Field due to coil P: $B_{1}=\dfrac{\mu_{0}(3I)}{2R}=\dfrac{3\mu_{0}I}{2R}$; field due to coil Q: $B_{2}=\dfrac{\mu_{0}(2I)}{2(2R)}=\dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{2R}$.
Since the currents are opposite and the coils are coplanar, the fields oppose each other: $B=B_{1}-B_{2}=\dfrac{3\mu_{0}I}{2R}-\dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{2R}=\dfrac{\mu_{0}I}{R}$.
The resultant field is directed along the field of coil P (i.e., along the direction due to the current $3I$).

questions.question: Find the condition under which the charged particles moving with different speeds in the presence of electric and magnetic field vectors can be used to select charged particles of a particular speed.
questions.answer:
The electric force $q\vec{E}$ and magnetic force $q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}$ must be equal and opposite, with $\vec{E}$, $\vec{B}$ and $\vec{v}$ mutually perpendicular.
This gives the condition $qE=qvB$, i.e., $v=\dfrac{E}{B}$.
Only particles with this particular speed pass through undeflected, regardless of their charge or mass, so varying $E$ and $B$ selects a chosen speed — this is the principle of a velocity selector.

questions.question: An ammeter of resistance $0.80 \Omega$ can measure current upto $1.0$ A. (i) What must be the value of shunt resistance to enable the ammeter to measure current upto $5.0$ A? (ii) What is the combined resistance of the ammeter and the shunt?
questions.answer:
(i) For the shunt, the current through it and the ammeter must satisfy $I_{g}R_{g}=(I-I_{g})S$.
$1.0\times0.80=(5.0-1.0)S \Rightarrow S=\dfrac{0.80}{4.0}=0.2\ \Omega$.
(ii) Combined resistance: $R=\dfrac{R_{g}S}{R_{g}+S}=\dfrac{0.80\times0.2}{0.80+0.2}=0.16\ \Omega$.

questions.question: Deduce the expression for the magnetic dipole moment of an electron orbiting around the central nucleus.
questions.answer:
An electron of charge $e$ moving in a circular orbit of radius $r$ with speed $v$ constitutes a current $I=\dfrac{e}{T}=\dfrac{ev}{2\pi r}$, where $T=\dfrac{2\pi r}{v}$ is the time period.
This current loop has an equivalent magnetic moment $\mu_{l}=IA=\dfrac{ev}{2\pi r}\times\pi r^{2}=\dfrac{evr}{2}$.
The orbital angular momentum of the electron is $L=m_{e}vr$, so $vr=\dfrac{L}{m_{e}}$.
Substituting, $\mu_{l}=\dfrac{e}{2m_{e}}L$.
Since the electron is negatively charged, $\vec{\mu}_{l}$ is directed opposite to $\vec{L}$.

questions.question: A circular coil of $N$ turns and radius $R$ carries a current $I$. It is unwound and rewound to make another coil of radius $R/2$, current $I$ remaining the same. Calculate the ratio of the magnetic moments of the new coil and the original coil.
questions.answer:
Magnetic moment of a coil is $m = NI\pi R^2$.
The same wire (length $L = N \times 2\pi R$) is rewound with radius $R/2$, so the new number of turns is $N' = \dfrac{L}{2\pi (R/2)} = 2N$.
New magnetic moment: $m' = N'I\pi (R/2)^2 = 2NI\pi R^2/4 = \dfrac{1}{2}(NI\pi R^2)$.
So $\dfrac{m'}{m} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, i.e., the ratio is $1:2$.

questions.question: Two identical circular wires $P$ and $Q$ each of radius $R$ and carrying current ’ $I$’ are kept in perpendicular planes such that they have a common centre as shown in the figure. Find the magnitude and direction of the net magnetic field at the common centre of the two coils.
questions.answer:
Field at the centre due to each coil: $B_1 = B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$, and since the coils lie in perpendicular planes, $B_1$ and $B_2$ are mutually perpendicular.
Net field: $B = \sqrt{B_1^2 + B_2^2} = \sqrt{2}\,\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{\sqrt{2}R}$.
Direction: along the bisector of the angle between the axes of the two coils (at $45°$ to each plane).

questions.question: A particle of charge ’ $q$’ and mass ’ $m$’ is moving with velocity $\vec{V}$. It is subjected to a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ directed perpendicular to its velocity. Show that it describes a circular path. Write the expression for its radius.
questions.answer:
The magnetic force $\vec{F} = q\vec{V}\times\vec{B}$ is always perpendicular to $\vec{V}$, so it does no work and cannot change the speed; it only changes the direction of velocity.
Since $\vec{F}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{V}$ and constant in magnitude ($V$, $B$ constant), it acts as a centripetal force, making the particle move on a circular path.
Equating: $qVB = \dfrac{mV^2}{r}$, giving $r = \dfrac{mV}{qB}$.

questions.question: Two identical circular loops, $P$ and $Q$, each of radius $r$ and carrying currents $I$ and $2I$ respectively are lying in parallel planes such that they have a common axis. The direction of current in both the loops is clockwise as seen from $O$ which is equidistant from the both loops. Find the magnitude of the net magnetic field at point $O$.
questions.answer:
Field at O due to each loop (treated at the axial point equidistant from each): $B_P = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2r}$, $B_Q = \dfrac{\mu_0 (2I)}{2r}$.
Since both currents are clockwise as seen from O, but the loops lie on opposite sides of O, the two fields point in opposite directions along the axis.
Net field: $B = B_Q - B_P = \dfrac{\mu_0 (2I)}{2r} - \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2r} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2r}$, directed along the axis towards the loop carrying current $2I$.

questions.question: Write the expression for Lorentz magnetic force on a particle of charge $q$ moving with velocity $\vec{v}$ in a magnetic field $\vec{B}$. Show that no work is done by this force on the charged particle.
questions.answer:
Lorentz force: $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v}\times\vec{B})$.
Since $\vec{v}\times\vec{B}$ is always perpendicular to $\vec{v}$, the force $\vec{F}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{v}$ at every instant.
Work done in time $dt$: $dW = \vec{F}\cdot\vec{v}\,dt = 0$, since $\vec{F} \perp \vec{v}$.
Hence the magnetic force does no work on the charged particle.

questions.question: A steady current $(I_{1})$ flows through a long straight wire. Another wire carrying steady current $(I_{2})$ in the same direction is kept close and parallel to the first wire. Show with the help of a diagram how the magnetic field due to the current $I_{1}$ exerts a magnetic force on the second wire. Write the expression for this force.
questions.answer:
The current $I_1$ in the first wire produces a magnetic field $B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1}{2\pi d}$ at the location of the second wire, circling around wire 1 (into the page on one side, out on the other, by the right-hand rule).
This field exerts a force on the second wire carrying current $I_2$: $\vec{F} = I_2 \vec{l}\times\vec{B_1}$, and by $\vec{F} = I_2 l B_1$ (perpendicular to both $I_2$ and $B_1$), the force per unit length is $\dfrac{F}{l} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}$.
Since the currents are in the same direction, the force is attractive, pulling the wires toward each other.

questions.question: A charge $q$ moving along the X-axis with a velocity $\vec{v}$ is subjected to a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ acting along the Z-axis as it crosses the origin $O$. (i) Trace its trajectory. (ii) Does the charge gain kinetic energy as it enters the magnetic field? Justify your answer.
questions.answer:
(i) Since $\vec{v}$ (along X) and $\vec{B}$ (along Z) are perpendicular, the force $\vec{F} = q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}$ is centripetal and lies in the XY-plane, so the charge moves in a circular path in the XY-plane (in a plane perpendicular to $\vec{B}$).
(ii) No, the kinetic energy does not change. The magnetic force is always perpendicular to $\vec{v}$, so it does no work ($dW = \vec{F}\cdot\vec{v}\,dt = 0$), keeping the speed and hence KE constant.

questions.question: State Biot-Savart law. A current $I$ flows in a conductor placed perpendicular to the plane of the paper. Indicate the direction of the magnetic field due to a small element $d\vec{l}$ at point $P$ situated at a distance $\vec{r}$ from the element as shown in the figure.
questions.answer:
Biot-Savart law: the magnetic field due to a current element $I\,d\vec{l}$ at a point P, distance $\vec{r}$ away, is $d\vec{B} = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I\,d\vec{l}\times \hat{r}}{r^2}$.
The direction of $d\vec{B}$ at P is perpendicular to the plane containing $d\vec{l}$ and $\vec{r}$, given by the right-hand rule; for current flowing out of the plane of the paper towards the reader, $d\vec{B}$ at P circles the wire tangentially, e.g., into the page on one side and out of the page on the other, consistent with $d\vec{l}\times\hat{r}$.

questions.question: Define current sensitivity and voltage sensitivity of a galvanometer. Increasing the current sensitivity may not necessarily increase the voltage sensitivity of a galvanometer. Justify.
questions.answer:
Current sensitivity: deflection produced per unit current, $I_s = \dfrac{\theta}{I} = \dfrac{NAB}{k}$.
Voltage sensitivity: deflection produced per unit voltage, $V_s = \dfrac{\theta}{V} = \dfrac{NAB}{kR} = \dfrac{I_s}{R}$, where $R$ is the coil resistance.
If $N$ is increased to raise $I_s$, the length of wire (and hence resistance $R$) also increases proportionally, so $V_s = I_s/R$ may stay the same or even decrease.
Thus increasing current sensitivity does not necessarily increase voltage sensitivity.

questions.question: Using Ampere’s circuital law, derive an expression for the magnetic field along the axis of a toroidal solenoid.
questions.answer:
Consider an Amperian loop as a circle of radius $r$ along the axis of the toroid, concentric with it.
By symmetry, $\vec{B}$ is tangential and of the same magnitude at every point on this loop, so $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = B(2\pi r)$.
The loop encloses current $NI$ (where $N$ is the total number of turns), so by Ampere's law, $B(2\pi r) = \mu_0 NI$, giving $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 NI}{2\pi r}$ inside the core.
For loops outside the toroid (through the empty space inside the core or outside the toroid), the enclosed current is zero, so $B = 0$.

questions.question: Write the relation for the force acting on a charge carrier $q$ moving with a velocity $\vec{v}$ through a magnetic field $\vec{B}$ in vector notation. Using this relation, deduce the conditions under which this force will be (i) maximum (ii) minimum.
questions.answer:
The force on a charge $q$ moving with velocity $\vec{v}$ in a magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$, with magnitude $F = qvB\sin\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between $\vec{v}$ and $\vec{B}$.
(i) Maximum: when $\theta = 90^{\circ}$, i.e., $\vec{v}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{B}$, giving $F_{max} = qvB$.
(ii) Minimum (zero): when $\theta = 0^{\circ}$ or $180^{\circ}$, i.e., $\vec{v}$ is parallel or antiparallel to $\vec{B}$.

questions.question: A galvanometer has a resistance of 30 $\Omega$. It gives full scale deflection with a current of 2 mA. Calculate the value of the resistance needed to convert it into an ammeter of range 0-0.3 A.
questions.answer:
For a shunt $S$ in parallel with the galvanometer, $I_g G = (I - I_g)S$.
$S = \dfrac{I_g G}{I - I_g} = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-3} \times 30}{0.3 - 0.002}$
$S = \dfrac{0.06}{0.298} \approx 0.201\ \Omega$
This resistance must be connected in parallel with the galvanometer.

questions.question: Two long straight parallel conductors $A$ and $B$ carrying steady currents $I_{1}$ and $I_{2}$ in the same direction are separated by a distance $d$. Deduce the expressions for the force acting on length $L$ of conductor $B$ due to conductor $A$ and show it in figure. Write the expression for the force acting on length $L$ of conductor $A$ due to conductor $B$ and show that it follows Newton’s third law.
questions.answer:
The magnetic field due to conductor $A$ (carrying $I_1$) at conductor $B$, distance $d$ away, is $B_A = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1}{2\pi d}$, directed into the page (by right-hand rule), perpendicular to $B$.
Force on length $L$ of $B$: $F_{BA} = B_A I_2 L = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2 L}{2\pi d}$, directed toward $A$ (attractive, since currents are parallel).
Similarly, field due to $B$ at $A$ is $B_B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_2}{2\pi d}$, giving force on length $L$ of $A$: $F_{AB} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2 L}{2\pi d}$, directed toward $B$.
Since $F_{AB} = F_{BA}$ in magnitude but opposite in direction, Newton's third law is satisfied.

questions.question: Derive an expression for the magnetic field $\vec{B}$, due to a circular coil of $N$ turns, each of radius $r$ carrying current $I$, at a distance $x$ from the centre along its axis.
questions.answer:
Consider a circular coil of $N$ turns, radius $r$, carrying current $I$, and a point $P$ on its axis at distance $x$ from the centre.
By Biot-Savart law, field due to a current element $Idl$ is $dB = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I\,dl}{(r^2+x^2)}$, directed perpendicular to the line joining the element to $P$.
Resolving into components along and perpendicular to the axis, the perpendicular components cancel by symmetry, and axial components add:
$dB_x = dB \sin\phi = \dfrac{\mu_0 I\,dl}{4\pi(r^2+x^2)} \cdot \dfrac{r}{\sqrt{r^2+x^2}}$
Integrating over the loop ($\oint dl = 2\pi r$) for $N$ turns:
$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 N I r^2}{2(r^2+x^2)^{3/2}}$

questions.question: A circular coil of $30$ turns and radius $8$· $0$ cm carrying a current of $6$ A is suspended vertically in a uniform horizontal magnetic field of $1$· $0$ T. The field lines make an angle of $30^{^{\circ}}$ with the plane of the coil. Calculate the magnitude of the external torque that must be applied to prevent the coil from turning. What would happen if the circular coil is replaced by a planar coil of irregular shape that encloses the same area, keeping other parameters unchanged?
questions.answer:
$N = 30$, $r = 0.08$ m, $I = 6$ A, $B = 1.0$ T; angle between field and plane $= 30^{\circ}$, so angle $\theta$ between $\vec{B}$ and normal (magnetic moment) $= 60^{\circ}$.
$A = \pi r^2 = \pi (0.08)^2 = 2.01 \times 10^{-2}$ m$^2$
$\tau = NIAB\sin\theta = 30 \times 6 \times 2.01\times10^{-2} \times 1.0 \times \sin60^{\circ}$
$\tau \approx 3.13$ N m
External torque required $= 3.13$ N m (to balance this torque).
If replaced by an irregular planar coil of the same area, the torque remains unchanged, since torque depends only on the area enclosed, not on the shape of the loop.

questions.question: An alpha particle (mass $6$· $4 \times 10^{-27}$ kg and charge $3$· $2 \times 10^{-19}$ C) having $8$· $0$ MeV energy, enters a region of a uniform magnetic field of $0$· $5$ T.
