Option (C) is correct.
$f = R/(\mu-1) = 40/(1.5-1) = 80$ cm; image same size as object means magnification $-1$, so object is at $u = 2f = 160$ cm.

questions.question: A ray of monochromatic light travelling in air is incident on a glass slab and is partly reflected and partly refracted. Both the reflected and refracted lights will have: (A) same wavelength (B) same frequency (C) same intensity (D) same speed
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Frequency of light depends only on the source and remains unchanged on reflection and refraction.

questions.question: A ray of yellow light undergoes total internal reflection when it is incident at the interface of two media. This ray is successively replaced by the ray of blue, green and red lights. Which of the following statements is true if the angle of incidence is same in all cases? (A) Total internal reflection occurs for blue light only. (B) Total internal reflection occurs for red light only. (C) Total internal reflection occurs for both green and blue lights. (D) None of them will undergo total internal reflection.
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
Refractive index increases as violet > blue > green > yellow > red, so critical angle decreases in that order; since yellow just undergoes TIR at the given angle, blue and green (having smaller critical angles) also undergo TIR, while red (larger critical angle) does not.

questions.question: Assertion (A): When a convex lens made of glass is immersed in water, its converging power increases. Reason (R): The focal length of a lens depends only on the radii of curvature of its two faces. (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. (D) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
On immersing in water, the relative refractive index of glass decreases, so the focal length increases and power decreases (Assertion is false); also, by the lensmaker's formula $1/f = (\mu-1)(1/R_1 - 1/R_2)$, focal length depends on both the radii of curvature and the refractive index, not radii alone (Reason is false).

questions.question: The images formed by the objective lens and the eyepiece are respectively: (A) virtual, real (B) real, virtual (C) virtual, virtual (D) real, real
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
The objective forms a real, inverted image, which acts as the object for the eyepiece that forms a magnified virtual image.

questions.question: The magnification produced by the telescope does not depend upon the: (A) colour of light (B) focal length of objective lens (C) focal length of eyepiece (D) apertures of objective lens and eyepiece
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
Magnifying power in normal adjustment is $M = f_o/f_e$, which depends on the focal lengths (and colour of light through them) but not on the apertures, which only affect brightness and resolving power.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is not correct for this telescope? (A) The focal length of objective lens $(f_{o})$ is larger than the focal length of eyepiece $(f_{e})$. (B) Its magnifying power can be increased by increasing the focal length of objective lens $(f_{o})$. (C) The distance between two lenses is more than $(f_{o} + f_{e})$. (D) The magnifying power can be decreased by increasing the focal length of eyepiece.
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
For an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment, the separation between the objective and eyepiece equals $f_o + f_e$, not more than it.

questions.question: An astronomical telescope has objective lens and eyepiece of focal lengths 80 cm and 4 cm respectively. To view the image in normal adjustment, the lenses must be separated by a distance of: (A) 84 cm (B) 76 cm (C) 20 cm (D) 320 cm
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
In normal adjustment, separation between objective and eyepiece $L = f_o + f_e = 80 + 4 = 84$ cm.

questions.question: Consider the telescope described in question (iv) (a). Its magnifying power in normal adjustment will be: (A) 320 (B) 84 (C) 76 (D) 20
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
Magnifying power in normal adjustment $m = \frac{f_o}{f_e} = \frac{80}{4} = 20$.

questions.question: Case Study (Q30): A thin lens is a transparent optical medium bounded by two surfaces, at least one of which should be spherical. Applying the formula for image formation by a single spherical surface successively at the two surfaces of a lens, one can obtain the ’lens maker formula’ and then the ’lens formula’. A lens has two foci, called ’first focal point’ and ’second focal point’ of the lens, one on each side. (i) Consider the arrangement shown in figure. A black vertical arrow and a horizontal thick line with a ball are painted on a glass plate. It serves as the object. When the plate is illuminated, its real image is formed on the screen. Which of the following correctly represents the image formed on the screen? (A) Option A (image as shown) (B) Option B (image as shown) (C) Option C (image as shown) (D) Option D (image as shown)
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
A real image formed by a convex lens is inverted both vertically and laterally, so the arrow points downward and the ball's position is reversed relative to the object on the plate.

questions.question: (ii) Which of the following statements is incorrect? (A) For a convex mirror magnification is always negative. (B) For all virtual images formed by a mirror magnification is positive. (C) For a concave lens magnification is always positive. (D) For real and inverted images, magnification is always negative.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image, so its magnification is always positive, not negative.

questions.question: (iii) A convex lens of focal length $f$ is cut into two equal parts perpendicular to the principal axis. The focal length of each part will be: (A) $f$ (B) $2f$ (C) $\frac{f}{2}$ (D) $\frac{f}{4}$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Cutting the convex lens perpendicular to the principal axis gives two plano-convex lenses, each with half the original thickness/curvature contribution, so by the lens maker's formula each has focal length $2f$.

questions.question: (iii) OR: If an object in case (i) above is $20$ cm from the lens and the screen is $50$ cm away from the object, the focal length of the lens used is: (A) $10$ cm (B) $12$ cm (C) $16$ cm (D) $20$ cm
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Here $u = -20$ cm, $v = 50 - 20 = 30$ cm, so $\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{30} + \frac{1}{20} = \frac{1}{12}$, giving $f = 12$ cm.

questions.question: (iv) The distance of an object from first focal point of a biconvex lens is $X_{1}$ and distance of the image from second focal point is $X_{2}$. The focal length of the lens is: (A) $X_{1}X_{2}$ (B) $\sqrt{X_{1} + X_{2}}$ (C) $\sqrt{X_{1}X_{2}}$ (D) $\frac{\sqrt{X_{2}}}{X_{1}}$
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
By Newton's lens formula, $f = \sqrt{X_1 X_2}$.

questions.question: A beaker is filled with water (refractive index $\frac{4}{3}$) upto a height $H$. A coin is placed at its bottom. The depth of the coin, when viewed along the near normal direction, will be: (A) $\frac{H}{4}$ (B) $\frac{3H}{4}$ (C) $H$ (D) $\frac{4H}{3}$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Apparent depth $= \frac{\text{real depth}}{n} = \frac{H}{4/3} = \frac{3H}{4}$.

questions.question: The speed of light in two media ’1’ and ’2’ are $v_{1}$ and $v_{2} (> v_{1})$ respectively. For a ray of light to undergo total internal reflection at the interface of these two media, it must be incident from: $_{-1}[]$ (A) medium ’1’ and at an angle greater than $\sin\frac{v_{1}}{v_{2}} _{-1}[]$ (B) medium ’1’ and at an angle greater than $\cos\frac{v_{1}}{v_{2}} _{-1}[]$ (C) medium ’2’ and at an angle greater than $\sin\frac{v_{1}}{v_{2}} _{-1}[]$ (D) medium ’2’ and at an angle greater than $\cos\frac{v_{1}}{v_{2}}$
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Since $v_2 > v_1$, medium 1 is denser ($n_1 > n_2$), so TIR occurs for light travelling from medium 1 and incident at an angle greater than the critical angle $\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{v_1}{v_2}\right)$, using $\sin C = \frac{n_2}{n_1} = \frac{v_1}{v_2}$.

questions.question: A point source is placed at the bottom of a tank containing a transparent liquid (refractive index $n$) to a depth $H$. The area of the surface of the liquid through which light from the source can emerge out is: $2$ (A) $\frac{\pi H}{(n -1)} 2$ (B) $\frac{\pi H}{(n^{2}-1)} 2$ (C) $\frac{\pi H}{\sqrt{n}} 2$ (D) $\frac{\pi H}{(n^{2}+ 1)}$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Light emerges only within a circle of radius $R = H\tan C$, where $\sin C = \frac{1}{n}$; the area is $\pi R^2 = \pi H^2 \frac{\sin^2 C}{1-\sin^2 C} = \frac{\pi H^2}{n^2-1}$.

questions.question: A tub is filled with a transparent liquid to a height of 30.0 cm. The apparent depth of a coin lying at the bottom of the tub is found to be 16.0 cm. The speed of light in the liquid will be (A) $1.6 \times 10^{8}$ m s $-1$ (B) $2.0 \times 10^{8}$ m s $-1$ (C) $3.0 \times 10^{8}$ m s $-1$ (D) $2.5 \times 10^{8}$ m s $-1$
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Apparent depth $= \frac{\text{real depth}}{n}$, so $n = \frac{30.0}{16.0} = 1.875$, giving $v = \frac{c}{n} = \frac{3\times10^{8}}{1.875} = 1.6\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$.

questions.question: The focal length of a concave mirror in air is f. When the mirror is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $\frac{5}{3}$, its focal length will become (A) $\frac{5}{3}f$ (B) $\frac{3}{5}f$ (C) $\frac{2}{3}f$ (D) f
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
The focal length of a spherical mirror depends only on its radius of curvature ($f = R/2$), not on the refractive index of the surrounding medium, since the laws of reflection are independent of the medium.

questions.question: The plane face of a planoconvex lens is silvered. The refractive index of material and radius of curvature of the curved surface of the lens are n and R respectively. This lens will behave as a concave mirror of focal length (A) $\frac{R}{2}$ (B) $\frac{R}{2(n -1)}$ (C) nR (D) $\frac{R}{2(n -1)}$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
For a silvered plano-convex lens, $P = 2P_{lens} + P_{mirror}$, and since the plane mirror has zero power, $P = 2(n-1)/R$, giving equivalent focal length $\frac{R}{2(n-1)}$.

questions.question: The magnification produced by a spherical mirror is $-2.0$. The mirror used and the nature of the image formed will be: (A) Convex and virtual (B) Concave and real (C) Concave and virtual (D) Convex and real
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
A magnification of $-2.0$ means the image is real, inverted and enlarged, which occurs only for a concave mirror.

questions.question: A compound microscope has an objective and an eyepiece of focal lengths $f_{o}$ and $f_{e}$, respectively. To obtain a large magnification of a small object, the microscope should have: (A) $f_{o}$ and $f_{e}$ small, and $f_{e} > f_{o}$ (B) $f_{o}$ and $f_{e}$ small, and $f_{o} > f_{e}$ (C) $f_{o}$ and $f_{e}$ large, and $f_{e} > f_{o}$ (D) $f_{o}$ and $f_{e}$ large, and $f_{o} > f_{e}$
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Magnification of a compound microscope is $M \approx \frac{L}{f_{o}}\left(1+\frac{D}{f_{e}}\right)$, so both focal lengths must be small, with $f_{e} > f_{o}$ since the objective must have a shorter focal length than the eyepiece.

questions.question: A glass slab ($\mu = 1.5$) of thickness $6$ cm is placed over a paper. The shift in the letters printed on the paper will be: (A) $2$ cm (B) $1$ cm (C) $4$ cm (D) $3$ cm
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Shift $= t\left(1 -\frac{1}{\mu}\right) = 6\left(1 -\frac{1}{1.5}\right) = 2$ cm.

questions.question: A beam of light of wavelength $720$ nm in air enters water (refractive index $= \frac{4}{3}$). Its wavelength in water will be: (A) $540$ nm (B) $480$ nm (C) $420$ nm (D) $720$ nm
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
$\lambda_{water} = \frac{\lambda_{air}}{n} = \frac{720}{4/3} = 540$ nm.

questions.question: Assertion (A): In a reflecting telescope, the image does not have chromatic aberration. Reason (R): Chromatic aberration occurs only due to refraction of light through an optical medium. Select the correct answer from the codes given below: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. (D) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
A reflecting telescope uses a mirror, and since reflection does not depend on wavelength, no chromatic aberration occurs, while refraction through lenses causes different colours to focus at different points, correctly explaining the assertion.

questions.question: Assertion (A): A ray of light is incident normally on the face of a prism. The emergent ray will graze along the opposite face of the prism when the critical angle at glass-air interface is equal to the angle of the prism. Reason (R): The refractive index of a prism depends on angle of the prism. Select the correct answer: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. (D) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
Since the ray is incident normally on the first face, it travels undeviated to the second face where the angle of incidence equals the prism angle $A$; the ray just grazes the second face when $A = i_c$, so the assertion is true, but the refractive index is a property of the material and does not depend on the prism's angle, making the reason false.

questions.question: Case Study: When light travels from an optically denser medium to an optically rarer medium, at the interface it is partly reflected back into the same medium and partly refracted to the second medium. The angle of incidence corresponding to an angle of refraction $90^{^{\circ}}$ is called the critical angle ($i_{c}$) for the given pair of media. This angle is related to the refractive index of medium $1$ with respect to medium $2$. Refraction of light through a prism involves refraction at two plane interfaces. A relation for the refractive index of the material of the prism can be obtained in terms of the refracting angle of the prism and the angle of minimum deviation. For a thin prism, this relation reduces to a simple equation. Laws of refraction are also valid for refraction of light at a spherical interface. When an object is placed in front of a spherical surface separating two media, its image is formed. A relation between object and image distance, in terms of refractive indices of two media and the radius of curvature of the spherical surface can be obtained. Using this relation for two surfaces of a lens, ’lens maker formula’ is obtained. (i) A small bulb is placed at the bottom of a tank containing a transparent liquid (refractive index $n$) to a depth $H$. The radius of the circular area of the surface of liquid, through which light $[]$ from the bulb can emerge out, is $R$. Then $\frac{R}{H}$ is: (A) $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n^{2} -1}}$ (B) $\sqrt{n^{2} -1}$ (C) $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n^{2} + 1}}$ (D) $\sqrt{n^{2} + 1}$
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Light emerges only if it strikes the surface within the critical angle $i_c$, and $\tan i_c = R/H$; since $\sin i_c = 1/n$, $\tan i_c = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n^{2}-1}}$, giving $\frac{R}{H} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n^{2}-1}}$.

questions.question: (ii) (a) A parallel beam of light is incident on a face of a prism with refracting angle $60^{^{\circ}}$. The angle of minimum deviation is found to be $30^{^{\circ}}$. The refractive index of the material of the prism is close to: OR (b) The angle of minimum deviation for a ray of light incident on a thin prism, made of crown glass ($n = 1.52$) is $D_{m}$. If the prism was made of dense flint glass ($n = 1.62$) instead of crown glass, the angle of minimum deviation will: (A) (a) $1.3$ OR (b) decrease by $4\%$ (B) (a) $1.4$ OR (b) increase by $4\%$ (C) (a) $1.5$ OR (b) decrease by $19\%$ (D) (a) $1.6$ OR (b) increase by $19\%$
questions.answer:
(a) Option (B) is correct: $n = \dfrac{\sin\frac{A+D_m}{2}}{\sin\frac{A}{2}} = \dfrac{\sin 45^\circ}{\sin 30^\circ} \approx 1.4$.
OR
(b) Option (D) is correct: for a thin prism $D_m = (n-1)A$, so $D_m$ increases in the ratio $\frac{0.62}{0.52}$, an increase of about $19\%$.

questions.question: (iii) An object is placed in front of a convex spherical glass surface ($n = 1.5$ and radius of curvature $R$) at a distance of $4R$ from it. As the object is moved slowly close to the surface, the image formed is: (A) always real (B) always virtual (C) first real and then virtual (D) first virtual and then real
questions.answer: Option (C) is correct: using $\frac{n_2}{v}-\frac{n_1}{u}=\frac{n_2-n_1}{R}$, the image is real (finite $v>0$) while the object lies between $4R$ and $2R$, and becomes virtual once the object comes closer than $2R$.

questions.question: (iv) A double-convex lens, made of glass of refractive index $1.5$, has focal length $10$ cm. The radius of curvature of its each face, is: (A) $10$ cm (B) $15$ cm (C) $20$ cm (D) $40$ cm
questions.answer: Option (A) is correct: by $\frac{1}{f}=(n-1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)=(n-1)\frac{2}{R}$, $\frac{1}{10}=0.5\times\frac{2}{R}$ gives $R = 10$ cm.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Plane and convex mirrors cannot produce real images under any circumstance. Reason (R): A virtual image cannot serve as an object to produce a real image. (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. (D) Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.
questions.answer: Option (D) is correct: both plane and convex mirrors can form real images when a converging (virtual-object) beam falls on them, and a virtual image can act as a real object for the next surface to give a real image, so both statements are false.

questions.question: A double-convex lens, with each face having same radius of curvature $R$, is made of glass of refractive index $n$. Its power is: (A) $\frac{2(n -1)}{R}$ (B) $\frac{(2n -1)}{R}$ (C) $\frac{(n -1)}{2R}$ (D) $\frac{(2n -1)}{2R}$
questions.answer: Option (A) is correct: $P=\frac{1}{f}=(n-1)\left(\frac{1}{R}-\frac{1}{-R}\right)=\frac{2(n-1)}{R}$.

questions.question: A double-convex lens of power $P$, with each face having same radius of curvature, is cut into two equal parts perpendicular to its principal axis. The power of one part of the lens will be: (A) $2P$ (B) $P$ (C) $4P$ (D) $\frac{P}{2}$
questions.answer: Option (D) is correct: cutting perpendicular to the axis gives two plano-convex halves, each with $\frac{1}{f'}=(n-1)\left(\frac{1}{R}-0\right)=\frac{P}{2}$.

questions.question: The above two parts are kept in contact with each other as shown in the figure. The power of the combination will be: (A) $\frac{P}{2}$ (B) $P$ (C) $2P$ (D) $\frac{P}{4}$
questions.answer: Option (B) is correct: putting the two plano-convex halves (each of power $P/2$) back in contact reconstructs the original lens, so $P_{net}=\frac{P}{2}+\frac{P}{2}=P$.

questions.question: A double-convex lens of power $P$, with each face having same radius of curvature, is cut along its principal axis. The two parts are arranged as shown in the figure. The power of the combination will be: (A) Zero (B) $P$ (C) $2P$ (D) $\frac{P}{2}$
questions.answer: Option (C) is correct: cutting along the principal axis does not change either radius of curvature, so each half still has the full power $P$; placed in contact coaxially, $P_{net}=P+P=2P$.

questions.question: Two convex lenses of focal lengths $60$ cm and $20$ cm are held coaxially in contact with each other. The power of the combination is: (A) $6.6$ D (B) $15$ D (C) $\frac{1}{15}$ D (D) $\frac{1}{30}$ D
The refractive index of the material of a prism is $\sqrt{2}$. If the refracting angle of the prism is $60^{^{\circ}}$, find the: (1) Angle of minimum deviation, and (2) Angle of incidence.
questions.answer:
Using $n=\dfrac{\sin\frac{A+D_m}{2}}{\sin\frac{A}{2}}$: $\sqrt{2}\sin 30^\circ = \sin\frac{A+D_m}{2}$, so $\sin\frac{A+D_m}{2}=0.707=\sin 45^\circ$.
Thus $\frac{A+D_m}{2}=45^\circ \Rightarrow A+D_m=90^\circ \Rightarrow D_m = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$.
At minimum deviation, angle of incidence $i=\frac{A+D_m}{2}=45^\circ$.

questions.question: Assertion (A): The magnifying power of a compound microscope is negative. Reason (R): The final image formed is erect with respect to the object. (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. (D) Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
The negative magnifying power correctly indicates that the final image of a compound microscope is inverted with respect to the object, so the Reason (which claims the image is erect) is false even though the Assertion is true.

questions.question: When a ray of light propagates from a denser medium to a rarer medium, it bends away from the normal. When the incident angle is increased, the refracted ray deviates more from the normal. For a particular angle of incidence in the denser medium, the refracted ray just grazes the interface of the two surfaces. This angle of incidence is called the critical angle for the pair of media involved. For a ray incident at the critical angle, the angle of reflection is: (A) $0^{^{\circ}}$ (B) $< 90^{^{\circ}}$ (C) $> 90^{^{\circ}}$ (D) $90^{^{\circ}} []$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, which here is the critical angle, and the critical angle is always less than $90^{\circ}$.

questions.question: A ray of light of wavelength 600 nm is incident in water $n = \frac{4}{3}$ on the water-air interface at an angle less than the critical angle. The wavelength associated with the refracted ray is: (A) $400 nm$ (B) $450 nm$ (C) $600 nm$ (D) $800 nm$
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
Frequency stays unchanged on refraction, so $\lambda_{air} = n\,\lambda_{water} = \frac{4}{3}\times 600 = 800$ nm.

questions.question: (a) The interface AB between the two media A and B is shown in the figure. In the denser medium A, the incident ray PQ makes an angle of $30^{^{\circ}}$ with the horizontal. The refracted ray is parallel to the interface. The refractive index of medium B w.r.t. medium A is: OR (b) Two media A and B are separated by a plane boundary. The speed of light in medium A and B is $2 \times 10^{8} ms^{-1}$ and $2.5 \times 10^{8} ms^{-1}$ respectively. The critical angle for a ray of light going from medium A to medium B is: $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}^{-1} \frac{1}{9}$ (A) (a)(b) $\sin \frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}^{-1} \frac{4}{5}$ (B) (a)(b) $\sin \frac{4}{3}^{-1} \frac{3}{5}$ (C) (a)(b) $\sin \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}^{-1} \frac{2}{5}$ (D) (a)(b) $\sin$
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
(a) Since PQ makes $30^{\circ}$ with the horizontal interface, the angle of incidence with the normal is $60^{\circ}$; the refracted ray grazing the interface means the angle of refraction is $90^{\circ}$, so this is the critical angle and $n_{BA} = \frac{\sin 60^{\circ}}{\sin 90^{\circ}} = \frac{\sqrt3}{2}$.
OR (b) $\sin C = \frac{v_A}{v_B} = \frac{2\times10^{8}}{2.5\times10^{8}} = \frac{4}{5}$, so $C = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)$.

questions.question: The figure shows the path of a light ray through a triangular prism. In this phenomenon, the angle $\theta$ is given by: (A) $\sin^{-1}\sqrt{n^{2} -1} \sin^{-1}(n^{2} -1)$ (B) $_{-1}r$ (C) $\sin\frac{1}{n^{2}-1}$ (D) $\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{(n^{2}-1)}$
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
The ray strikes the second face at the critical angle for total internal reflection; using $\sin\theta = n\sin r$ and $\cos r = \sin(90^{\circ}-r) = \frac{1}{n}$ at that face gives $\sin\theta = \sqrt{n^{2}-1}$, so $\theta = \sin^{-1}\sqrt{n^{2}-1}$.

questions.question: Assertion (A): A convex lens, when immersed in a liquid, disappears. Reason (R): The refractive indices of material of the lens and the liquid are equal. (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. (D) Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Power of a lens depends on the difference between the refractive indices of the lens and surrounding medium, so when the liquid has the same refractive index as the lens, its power (and hence its ability to converge or diverge light) becomes zero and it becomes invisible.

questions.question: A thin converging lens of focal length $20$ cm and a thin diverging lens of focal length $15$ cm are placed coaxially in contact. The power of the combination is (A) $-\frac{5}{4}$ D (B) $-\frac{5}{3}$ D (C) $\frac{4}{3}$ D (D) $\frac{3}{5}$ D
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
$P = \frac{1}{f_1} - \frac{1}{f_2} = \frac{1}{0.20} - \frac{1}{0.15} = 5 - \frac{20}{3} = -\frac{5}{3}$ D.

questions.question: The radii of curvature of two surfaces of a convex lens are $R$ and $2R$. If the focal length of this lens is $(^{\frac{5}{3}})R$, the refractive index of the material of the lens is (A) $\frac{7}{5}$ (B) $\frac{8}{5}$ (C) $\frac{19}{15}$ (D) $\frac{3}{2}$
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Using $\frac{1}{f} = (n-1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)$ with $R_1=R,\ R_2=-2R$ and $f=\frac{5R}{3}$: $\frac{3}{5R} = (n-1)\frac{3}{2R}$, giving $n-1=\frac{2}{5}$, so $n=\frac{7}{5}$.

questions.question: The focal length of an equiconvex lens (A) increases when the lens is dipped in water. (B) increases when the wavelength of incident light decreases. (C) increases with decrease in radius of curvature of its surface. (D) decreases when the lens is cut into two identical parts along its principal axis.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Since $\frac{1}{f} = \left(\frac{n_{lens}}{n_{medium}}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)$, immersing the lens in water (a denser medium than air) reduces the relative refractive index, which increases the focal length.

questions.question: A thin convex lens $L$ of focal length $10$ cm and a concave mirror $M$ of focal length $15$ cm are placed coaxially $40$ cm apart as shown in figure. A beam of light coming parallel to the principal axis is incident on the lens. The final image will be formed at a distance of (A) $10$ cm, left of lens (B) $10$ cm, right of lens (C) $20$ cm, left of lens (D) $20$ cm, right of lens
questions.answer:
The parallel beam converges at the focus of the lens, $10$ cm from the lens, which is $30$ cm from the mirror — exactly the mirror's radius of curvature ($R=2f_M=30$ cm).
For a concave mirror an object at the centre of curvature forms its image back at the centre of curvature, so the reflected rays converge again $30$ cm from the mirror, i.e. at the same point $10$ cm from the lens (the focus of the lens itself).
Since this second image lies exactly at the lens's focal point, the rays emerging from the lens on the return path are parallel to the principal axis, so the final image is formed at infinity.

questions.question: A beam of light coming parallel to the principal axis of a convex lens $L_{1}$ of focal length $16$ cm is incident on it. Another convex lens $L_{2}$ of focal length $12$ cm is placed coaxially at a distance $40$ cm from $L_{1}$. The nature and distance of the final image from $L_{2}$ will be (A) real, $24$ cm (B) virtual, $12$ cm (C) real, $32$ cm (D) virtual, $18$ cm
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Parallel rays refracted by $L_1$ would converge $16$ cm from it, i.e. $40-16=24$ cm before $L_2$; since this point lies between the lenses, the diverging rays reaching $L_2$ come from a real object at $u=-24$ cm, so $\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{-24}=\frac{1}{12}$ gives $v=24$ cm, real.

questions.question: A prism is an optical medium bounded by three refracting plane surfaces. A ray of light suffers successive refractions on passing through its two surfaces and deviates by a certain angle from its original path. The refractive index of the material of the prism is given $[](/$ by $\mu = \sin\frac{A + \delta_{m}}{2}\sin \frac{A}{2}$. If the angle of incidence on the second surface is greater than an angle called critical angle, the ray will not be refracted from the second surface and is totally internally reflected. The critical angle for glass is $\theta_{1}$ and that for water is $\theta_{2}$. The critical angle for glass-water surface would be (given $_{a}\mu_{g} = 1.5$, $_{a}\mu_{w} = 1.33$): (A) less than $\theta_{2}$ (B) between $\theta_{1}$ and $\theta_{2}$ (C) greater than $\theta_{2}$ (D) less than $\theta_{1}$
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
$\sin\theta_c = \frac{{}_{a}\mu_{w}}{{}_{a}\mu_{g}} = \frac{1.33}{1.5} \approx 0.887$, giving $\theta_c \approx 62.5^{\circ}$, which is greater than $\theta_2 \approx 48.8^{\circ}$ (water-air critical angle).

questions.question:
When a ray of light of wavelength $\lambda$ and frequency $
u$ is refracted into a denser medium: (A) $\lambda$ and $
u$ both increase. (B) $\lambda$ increases but $
u$ is unchanged. (C) $\lambda$ decreases but $
u$ is unchanged. (D) $\lambda$ and $
u$ both decrease.
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
Frequency depends only on the source and stays unchanged on refraction, while speed decreases in the denser medium, so $\lambda = v/\nu$ decreases.

questions.question: The critical angle for a ray of light passing from glass to water is minimum for: (A) red colour (B) blue colour (C) yellow colour (D) violet colour
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
Since $\sin\theta_c = 1/\mu$ and violet light has the highest refractive index for glass, it has the smallest critical angle.

questions.question: Three beams of red, yellow and violet colours are passed through a prism, one by one under the same condition. When the prism is in the position of minimum deviation, the angles of refraction from the second surface are $r_{R}$, $r_{Y}$ and $r_{V}$ respectively. Then: (A) $r_{V} < r_{Y} < r_{R}$ (B) $r_{Y} < r_{R} < r_{V}$ (C) $r_{R} < r_{V} < r_{Y}$ (D) $r_{R} = r_{Y} = r_{V}$
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
At minimum deviation $r_1 = r_2 = A/2$ for every colour, and $A/2$ depends only on the prism's geometric angle, not on wavelength, so $r_R = r_Y = r_V$.

questions.question: A ray of light is incident normally on a prism ABC of refractive index $\sqrt{2}$, as shown in figure. After it strikes face AC, it will: (A) go straight undeviated (B) just graze along the face AC (C) refract and go out of the prism (D) undergo total internal reflection
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
For $\mu=\sqrt{2}$, the critical angle is $\theta_c=\sin^{-1}(1/\sqrt2)=45^{\circ}$; the ray strikes face AC at exactly $45^{\circ}$, so it grazes along AC instead of emerging or fully reflecting.

questions.question: The focal lengths of the objective and the eyepiece of a compound microscope are $1$ cm and $2$ cm respectively. If the tube length of the microscope is $10$ cm, the magnification obtained by the microscope for most suitable viewing by relaxed eye is: (A) $250$ (B) $200$ (C) $150$ (D) $125$
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
For relaxed-eye viewing, $M = \frac{L}{f_o}\times\frac{D}{f_e} = \frac{10}{1}\times\frac{25}{2} = 125$.

questions.question: A point object is kept $60$ cm in front of a spherical convex surface ($n = 1.5$, radius of curvature $40$ cm). The image formed is: (A) real, at a distance $1.8$ m from the surface. (B) virtual, at a distance $1.8$ m from the surface. (C) real, at a distance $3.6$ m from the surface. (D) virtual, at a distance $3.6$ m from the surface.
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
Using $\frac{n_2}{v}-\frac{n_1}{u}=\frac{n_2-n_1}{R}$ with $u=-60$ cm, $n_1=1$, $n_2=1.5$, $R=40$ cm: $\frac{1.5}{v}+\frac{1}{60}=\frac{0.5}{40}=\frac{1}{80}$, giving $v=-360$ cm, a virtual image $3.6$ m from the surface.

questions.question: Strontium titanate is a rare oxide — a natural mineral found in Siberia. It is used as a substitute for diamond because its refractive index and critical angle are $2.41$ and $24.5^{^{\circ}}$, respectively, which are approximately equal to the refractive index and critical angle of diamond. It has all the properties of diamond. Even an expert jeweller is unable to differentiate between diamond and strontium titanate. A ray of light is incident normally on one face of an equilateral triangular prism $ABC$ made of strontium titanate. Answer the following questions based on the above: Trace the path of the ray showing its passage through the prism.
questions.answer:
The ray enters face AB along the normal, so it passes through undeviated and travels straight to face AC.
At AC it strikes at $60^{\circ}$ (equal to the prism's apex angle), which exceeds the critical angle $24.5^{\circ}$, so it undergoes total internal reflection.
The reflected ray then strikes face BC exactly along the normal and emerges from BC without any bending.

questions.question: For the strontium titanate prism (refractive index $2.41$), find the velocity of light through the prism.
questions.answer: $v = \frac{c}{n} = \frac{3 \times 10^{8}}{2.41} \approx 1.245 \times 10^{8}$ m/s.

questions.question: For a concave mirror of focal length ’ $f$’, the minimum distance between the object and its real image is: (A) zero (B) $f$ (C) $2f$ (D) $4f$
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
For a real image, $u = v = 2f$ (object at centre of curvature), so the object and image coincide and the minimum distance between them is zero.

questions.question: The minimum distance between an object and its real image formed by a convex lens of focal length $f$ is: (A) $f$ (B) $2f$ (C) $3f$ (D) $4f$
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
The minimum separation occurs when $u = v = 2f$, giving object-image distance $= u+v = 4f$.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of media has the least value of critical angle? (A) Glass to air (B) Glass to water (C) Diamond to water (D) Diamond to air
questions.answer:
Option (D) is correct.
$\sin C = n_2/n_1$; diamond to air gives the smallest ratio ($1/2.42$), hence the smallest critical angle ($\approx 24.4^\circ$).

questions.question: A ray of monochromatic light propagating in air, is incident on the surface of water. Which of the following will be the same for the reflected and refracted rays? (A) Energy carried (B) Speed (C) Frequency (D) Wavelength
questions.answer:
Option (C) is correct.
Frequency depends only on the source and remains unchanged on reflection and refraction.

questions.question: A ray of light of wavelength $600$ nm propagates from air into a medium. If its wavelength in the medium becomes $400$ nm, the refractive index of the medium is (A) $1.4$ (B) $1.5$ (C) $1.6$ (D) $1.8$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
$\mu = \lambda_{air}/\lambda_{medium} = 600/400 = 1.5$.

questions.question: A ray of light travels a distance of $12.0$ m in a transparent sheet in $60$ ns. The refractive index of the sheet is (A) $1.33$ (B) $1.50$ (C) $1.65$ (D) $1.75$
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Speed $v = 12.0/(60\times10^{-9}) = 2\times10^{8}$ m/s, so $\mu = c/v = 3\times10^{8}/2\times10^{8} = 1.5$.

questions.question: Case Study: The lens maker’s formula is useful to design lenses of desired focal lengths using surfaces of suitable radii of curvature. The focal length also depends on the refractive index of the material of the lens and the surrounding medium. The refractive index depends on the wavelength of the light used. The power of a lens is related to its focal length. (a) How will the power of a lens be affected with an increase of wavelength of light?
questions.answer:
As wavelength increases, the refractive index $\mu$ of the material decreases (normal dispersion).
Since $\frac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)$, a decrease in $\mu$ increases $f$, so the power $P = 1/f$ decreases.

questions.question: (b) The radius of curvature of two surfaces of a convex lens is $R$ each. For what value of $\mu$ of its material will its focal length become equal to $R$?
questions.answer:
Using $\frac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2}\right)$ with $R_1 = R$, $R_2 = -R$: $\frac{1}{f} = (\mu-1)\frac{2}{R}$.
For $f = R$: $1 = 2(\mu - 1)$, so $\mu = 1.5$.

questions.question: An object AB is kept in front of a composite convex lens, as shown in figure. Will the lens produce one image? If not, explain.
questions.answer:
No, a single sharp image is not formed.
Since the two halves of the composite lens have different focal lengths (different refractive indices or curvatures), each half refracts light independently and forms its own image, so two images of the object are produced.

questions.question: A real image of an object formed by a convex lens is observed on a screen. If the screen is removed, will the image still be formed? Explain.
questions.answer:
Yes, the real image still forms at the same location in space, since the refracted rays actually converge there regardless of whether a screen is present.
Without the screen, the image simply cannot be seen there unless an eye or another screen is placed to intercept the converging (or subsequently diverging) rays.

questions.question: Two statements are given - one labelled Assertion (A) and the other labelled Reason (R). Select the correct answer to this question from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below: (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A). (B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A). (C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false. (D) Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false. Assertion (A): The angle of minimum deviation for a prism is lesser for red light than that for blue light. Reason (R): The refractive index of the material of a prism for blue light is greater than that for red light.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Since $\mu_{blue} > \mu_{red}$, and deviation increases with refractive index, the minimum deviation for red light is less than that for blue light, so R correctly explains A.

questions.question: An object approaches a converging lens with a uniform speed of $5$ m/s and stops at the focus. How will the image move with respect to the lens? Specify its nature.
questions.answer: As the object moves from a large distance towards the focus, the real, inverted image moves away from the lens on the other side, from near the focus towards infinity, with continuously increasing (non-uniform) speed.

questions.question: In a simple microscope, a convex lens of focal length $5$ cm is used. Calculate the magnifying power when the object is placed at the focus of the lens.
questions.answer: $M = \dfrac{D}{f} = \dfrac{25}{5} = 5$

questions.question: A ray of light on passing through an equilateral glass prism, suffers a minimum deviation equal to the angle of the prism. The value of refractive index of the material of the prism is ______.
questions.answer: $\sqrt{3}$ (since $\mu = \dfrac{\sin\left(\frac{A+D_m}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\frac{A}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{\sin 60^\circ}{\sin 30^\circ} = \sqrt{3}$)

questions.question: Larger aperture of objective lens in an astronomical telescope (A) increases the resolving power of telescope. (B) decreases the brightness of the image. (C) increases the size of the image. (D) decreases the length of the telescope.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Resolving power $\propto$ aperture of objective, so a larger aperture increases the resolving power of the telescope.

questions.question: A biconvex lens of glass having refractive index $1$· $47$ is immersed in a liquid. It becomes invisible and behaves as a plane glass plate. The refractive index of the liquid is (A) $1$· $47$ (B) $1$· $62$ (C) $1$· $33$ (D) $1$· $51$
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
The lens becomes invisible only when the refractive index of the liquid equals that of the lens material, i.e., $1.47$.

questions.question: For a glass prism, the angle of minimum deviation will be smallest for the light of (A) red colour. (B) blue colour. (C) yellow colour. (D) green colour.
questions.answer:
Option (A) is correct.
Since $\mu_{red}$ is the smallest among visible colours, and $D_m$ increases with $\mu$, red light has the smallest angle of minimum deviation.

questions.question: The resolving power of a telescope can be increased by increasing (A) wavelength of light. (B) diameter of objective. (C) length of the tube. (D) focal length of eyepiece.
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
Resolving power of a telescope $= \dfrac{a}{1.22\lambda}$, which increases with the diameter $a$ of the objective.

questions.question: The focal length of the objective of a compound microscope is (A) greater than the focal length of eyepiece. (B) lesser than the focal length of eyepiece. (C) equal to the focal length of eyepiece. (D) equal to the length of its tube.
questions.answer:
Option (B) is correct.
In a compound microscope, the objective has a small focal length to give high magnification, which is lesser than the focal length of the eyepiece.

questions.question: For a higher resolving power of a compound microscope, the wavelength of light used should be ______.
questions.answer: smaller (shorter), since resolving power $\propto \dfrac{1}{\lambda}$.

questions.question: A compound microscope is used because a realistic simple microscope does not have ______ magnification.
questions.answer: Large (sufficiently large) magnification without loss of image sharpness, since increasing magnification by reducing focal length brings the object too close to the eye to focus comfortably.

questions.question: The resolving power of a compound microscope can be ______ by using a medium (oil) of higher refractive index than air between the object and the objective lens.
questions.answer: Increased, since resolving power $= \frac{2\mu \sin\theta}{\lambda}$, and a higher refractive index $\mu$ raises the numerical aperture.

questions.question: The refractive index of the material of a converging lens is $1.5$. If air is replaced by a medium of refractive index $1.6$, then the lens will now behave as a ______ lens.
questions.answer: Diverging (concave) lens, because when the surrounding medium has a higher refractive index than the lens material, the effective relative refractive index becomes less than $1$, reversing the sign of $\frac{1}{f}$.

questions.question: The value of Brewster’s angle for air-glass interface is $\frac{\pi}{3}$; hence the refractive index of glass is ______.
questions.answer: $\mu = \tan i_p = \tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3}$

questions.question: An astronomical telescope may be a refracting type or a reflecting type. Which of the two produces image of better quality? Justify your answer.
questions.answer:
The reflecting type produces a better quality image.
This is because a mirror is free from chromatic aberration (no dispersion on reflection) and spherical aberration can be minimized using a parabolic mirror, and a mirror can be made with a much larger aperture, giving greater resolving power.

questions.question: A biconcave lens of power $P$ vertically splits into two identical plano concave parts. The power of each part will be (A) $2P$ (B) $P/2$ (C) $P$ (D) $P/\sqrt{2}$
questions.answer:
Option (B) $P/2$ is correct.
Each plano-concave half has only one curved surface (the other being flat), so by $\frac{1}{f} = (\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)$ its power is half that of the original biconcave lens.

questions.question: State the condition under which a large magnification can be achieved in an astronomical telescope. OR How does the angle of minimum deviation of a glass prism vary if the incident violet light is replaced by red light?
questions.answer: Large magnification is achieved when the focal length of the objective $f_o$ is large and the focal length of the eyepiece $f_e$ is small, since magnifying power $m = \frac{f_o}{f_e}$.

questions.question: Does the magnifying power of a microscope depend on the colour of the light used? Justify your answer.
questions.answer:
Yes, it depends slightly on colour.
The refractive index of the lens material, and hence the focal lengths of the objective and eyepiece, vary with wavelength, so the magnifying power $m = \frac{f_o}{f_e}\left(1+\frac{D}{f_e}\right)$ changes slightly with colour; also, resolving power is higher for shorter wavelengths (violet) than for longer ones (red).

questions.question: How does the angle of minimum deviation of a glass prism vary, if the incident violet light is replaced by red light? Give reason.
questions.answer:
The angle of minimum deviation decreases when violet light is replaced by red light.
This is because the refractive index of glass is higher for violet light than for red light ($\mu_v > \mu_r$), and deviation $\delta_m$ increases with $\mu$ as per $\mu = \frac{\sin\left(\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\frac{A}{2}\right)}$.

questions.question: The line AB in the ray diagram represents a lens. State whether the lens is convex or concave.
questions.answer:
The lens AB is convex if the refracted rays converge towards the principal axis (forming a real, converging beam), and it is concave if the refracted rays diverge away from the axis.
In the standard ray diagram where a ray incident parallel to the principal axis bends and passes through a point on the other side of the lens, the lens AB represents a convex (converging) lens.

questions.question: A concave lens of refractive index 1.5 is immersed in a medium of refractive index 1.65. What is the nature of the lens?
questions.answer:
The lens behaves as a converging (convex) lens.
This is because when a lens is placed in a medium denser than itself ($n_{medium} = 1.65 > n_{lens} = 1.5$), its nature reverses, so a concave lens acts as a converging lens.

questions.question: A convex lens is placed in contact with a plane mirror. A point object at a distance of 20 cm on the axis of this combination has its image coinciding with itself. What is the focal length of the lens?
questions.answer:
The focal length of the lens is $20$ cm.
For the image to coincide with the object, light must fall normally on the plane mirror after refraction through the lens, which happens only when the object is placed at the focus of the lens.

questions.question: A biconcave lens made of a transparent material of refractive index 1.25 is immersed in water of refractive index 1.33. Will the lens behave as a converging or a diverging lens? Give reason.
questions.answer:
The lens behaves as a converging (convex) lens.
Since the refractive index of the lens material ($1.25$) is less than that of the surrounding medium, water ($1.33$), the nature of the biconcave lens gets reversed and it converges light.

questions.question: Write the relationship between angle of incidence $i$, angle of prism $A$ and angle of minimum deviation for a triangular prism.
questions.answer:
$A + \delta_{m} = i_{1} + i_{2}$, and at minimum deviation $i_{1} = i_{2} = i$, so $i = \dfrac{A + \delta_{m}}{2}$.
Also, the angle of refraction at each face is $r = \dfrac{A}{2}$.

questions.question: A converging lens is kept coaxially in contact with a diverging lens — both the lenses being of equal focal lengths. What is the focal length of the combination?
questions.answer:
The focal length of the combination is infinite.
Using $\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{-f} = 0$, so $F = \infty$, meaning the combination behaves as a plane glass plate with zero power.

questions.question: For the same value of angle of incidence, the angles of refraction in three media A, B and C are $15^{^{\circ}}$, $25^{^{\circ}}$ and $35^{^{\circ}}$ respectively. In which medium would the velocity of light be minimum?
questions.answer:
The velocity of light is minimum in medium A.
Since $n = \dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r}$, the smallest angle of refraction ($15^{\circ}$) in medium A corresponds to the largest refractive index, and since $v = c/n$, the velocity is minimum there.

questions.question: Under what condition does a biconvex lens of glass having a certain refractive index act as a plane glass sheet when immersed in a liquid?
questions.answer: A biconvex glass lens acts as a plane glass sheet when the refractive index of the surrounding liquid is equal to the refractive index of the glass, since then $\left(\dfrac{n_{lens}}{n_{medium}} - 1\right) = 0$ and the lens formula gives $\dfrac{1}{f} = 0$, i.e., $f = \infty$.

questions.question: How does focal length of a lens change when red light incident on it is replaced by violet light? Give reason for your answer.
questions.answer:
The focal length decreases when red light is replaced by violet light.
Since $\dfrac{1}{f} = (n-1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$ and the refractive index for violet light is greater than that for red light, a larger $n$ gives a smaller $f$.

questions.question: A glass lens of refractive index 1.45 disappears when immersed in a liquid. What is the value of refractive index of the liquid?
questions.answer:
The refractive index of the liquid is $1.45$.
A lens disappears in a liquid when the refractive index of the liquid equals that of the lens material, since then the lens exerts no net refraction.

questions.question: State the conditions for the phenomenon of total internal reflection to occur.
questions.answer:
Two conditions must be satisfied:
(i) Light must travel from a denser medium to a rarer medium.
(ii) The angle of incidence in the denser medium must be greater than the critical angle $\theta_{c}$ for that pair of media.

questions.question: You are given following three lenses. Which two lenses will you use as an eyepiece and as an objective to construct an astronomical telescope?
questions.answer:
The lens with the larger focal length and larger aperture is used as the objective, and the lens with the smaller focal length is used as the eyepiece.
This is because the objective must collect more light and form a small angle image, while the eyepiece must magnify it through a large angle.

questions.question: Two thin lenses of power $+6D$ and $-2D$ are in contact. What is the focal length of the combination?
questions.answer:
The focal length of the combination is $25$ cm.
$P = P_1 + P_2 = 6 + (-2) = 4$ D, so $f = 1/P = 1/4$ m $= 25$ cm.

questions.question: A glass lens of refractive index $1.5$ is placed in a trough of liquid. What must be the refractive index of the liquid in order to make the lens disappear?
questions.answer:
The refractive index of the liquid must be $1.5$.
A lens disappears in a liquid when the liquid has the same refractive index as the lens, since then no refraction (bending) of light occurs at the surfaces.

questions.question: An object is held at the principal focus of a concave lens of focal length $F$. Where is the image formed?
questions.answer:
The image is formed at a distance $F/2$ from the lens, on the same side as the object.
Using $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$ with $u = -F$, $f = -F$: $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{2}{F}$, so $v = -F/2$, giving a virtual, erect, diminished image.

questions.question: A ray of light in air is incident at angle $\angle i$ on a face of an equilateral glass prism and is refracted through the prism. As $\angle i$ is varied, it is observed that the ray undergoes minimum deviation, when $\angle i$ is three-fourth of the angle of the prism. Calculate the speed of light in the prism.
questions.answer:
For the equilateral prism, $A = 60^\circ$, and $i = \frac{3}{4}A = 45^\circ$.
At minimum deviation, $\delta_m = 2i - A = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$.
$\mu = \dfrac{\sin\left(\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\frac{A}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{\sin 45^\circ}{\sin 30^\circ} = \sqrt{2}$
Speed in prism: $v = \dfrac{c}{\mu} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 2.12 \times 10^8$ m/s

questions.question: A $5$ cm long pencil is placed along the principal axis of a concave mirror of focal length $20$ cm such that its nearest end is at a distance of $25$ cm from the mirror. Calculate the length of the image of the pencil.
questions.answer:
For the near end, $u_1 = -25$ cm, $f = -20$ cm: $\dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = -\dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{25} = -\dfrac{1}{100}$, so $v_1 = -100$ cm.
For the far end, $u_2 = -30$ cm: $\dfrac{1}{v_2} = -\dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{30} = -\dfrac{1}{60}$, so $v_2 = -60$ cm.
Length of image $= |v_1 - v_2| = |-100 - (-60)| = 40$ cm

questions.question: A ray of light is incident on the face of a triangular prism of refracting angle $60^{^{\circ}}$ and it just suffers total internal reflection at the other face. Find the angle of incidence for the ray if the refractive index of the material of the prism is $\sqrt{2}$.
questions.answer:
Since the ray just suffers total internal reflection at the second face, the angle of incidence there equals the critical angle: $\sin C = \dfrac{1}{\mu} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, so $C = 45^\circ$.
Using $r_1 + r_2 = A$: $r_1 = 60^\circ - 45^\circ = 15^\circ$.
By Snell's law at the first face: $\sin i = \mu \sin r_1 = \sqrt{2} \times \sin 15^\circ = 0.366$
$i = \sin^{-1}(0.366) \approx 21.5^\circ$

questions.question: A ray of light is incident at an angle $2A$ on one of the faces of a glass prism of refracting angle $A$. After refraction from this face, the ray strikes the opposite face which is silvered. The reflected ray from this face retraces on its path. Trace the ray diagram and find the relation between the refractive index of material of prism and the angle of prism.
questions.answer:
For the ray to retrace its path after reflection at the silvered face, it must strike that face normally, so $r_2 = 0^\circ$.
From geometry, $r_1 + r_2 = A$, so $r_1 = A$.
Applying Snell's law at the first face: $\sin(2A) = \mu \sin r_1 = \mu \sin A$
$2\sin A \cos A = \mu \sin A \implies \mu = 2\cos A$

questions.question: Draw a labelled ray diagram of an astronomical telescope when final image is formed at infinity. Write the expression for its magnifying power.
questions.answer:
In an astronomical telescope with the final image at infinity, parallel rays from a distant object are focused by the objective lens at its focus $F_o$, which coincides with the focus $F_e$ of the eyepiece; the eyepiece then renders the rays parallel again, forming the final image at infinity.
Magnifying power: $M = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e}$

questions.question: A small bulb is placed at the bottom of a tank, containing a transparent liquid of refractive index $\sqrt{2}$, to a depth of 1 m. Calculate the area of the surface of the liquid through which light from the bulb emerges.
questions.answer:
Critical angle: $\sin C = \dfrac{1}{\mu} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, so $C = 45^\circ$.
Light emerges through a circle of radius $r = h\tan C = 1 \times \tan 45^\circ = 1$ m.
Area $= \pi r^2 = \pi \times 1^2 \approx 3.14$ m$^2$

questions.question: A concave mirror of radius of curvature 16 cm produces two-times enlarged real image of an object kept in front of it. Find the position of the object.
questions.answer:
For a real, magnified image formed by a concave mirror, $m = -\frac{v}{u} = -2$, so $v = 2u$.
Mirror formula: $\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}$, with $f = \frac{R}{2} = 8$ cm.
$\frac{1}{2u}+\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{8} \Rightarrow \frac{3}{2u}=\frac{1}{8} \Rightarrow u = 12$ cm.
The object must be placed $12$ cm in front of the mirror (between $F$ and $C$).

questions.question: A convex lens of refractive index 1·5 has a focal length of 20 cm in air. Find its nature and focal length when it is immersed in a transparent liquid of refractive index 1·25.
questions.answer:
Lens maker's formula: $\frac{1}{f}=\left(\frac{n_{lens}}{n_{medium}}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)$.
In air: $\frac{1}{20}=(1.5-1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right) \Rightarrow \left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)=\frac{1}{10}$ cm$^{-1}$.
In liquid: $\frac{1}{f'}=\left(\frac{1.5}{1.25}-1\right)\times\frac{1}{10}=0.2\times\frac{1}{10}=0.02$, so $f' = 50$ cm.
The lens remains convex (converging), with focal length $50$ cm in the liquid.

questions.question: A tank is filled with a liquid to a height of $12.5$ m. The apparent depth of a needle lying at the bottom of the tank is measured to be $9.0$ m. Calculate the speed of light in the liquid.
questions.answer:
Refractive index of liquid: $n = \frac{\text{real depth}}{\text{apparent depth}} = \frac{12.5}{9.0} = 1.39$.
Speed of light in liquid: $v = \frac{c}{n} = \frac{3\times10^{8}}{1.39} = 2.16\times10^{8}$ m/s.

questions.question: Two thin lenses of focal length $f_{1}$ and $f_{2}$ are placed in contact with each other coaxially. Prove that the focal length $f$ of the combination is given by $\frac{1}{f}= \frac{1}{f_{1}}+ \frac{1}{f_{2}}$.
questions.answer:
Let a point object O be placed on the axis. The first lens ($f_1$) forms an image $I_1$ of O, treated as a virtual object for the second lens.
For lens 1: $\frac{1}{v_1}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f_1}$
For lens 2 (thin lenses in contact, so same object distance $v_1$): $\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{v_1}=\frac{1}{f_2}$
Adding these two equations: $\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f_1}+\frac{1}{f_2}$
If the combination behaves as a single lens of focal length $f$ forming the same final image, $\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}$.
Comparing, $\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{f_1}+\frac{1}{f_2}$.

questions.question: A point source, in air, is placed at a distance of $6$ cm in front of a convex spherical surface ($n = 1.5$ and radius of curvature $= 24$ cm). Find the position and nature of the image formed.
questions.answer:
Using $\frac{n_2}{v}-\frac{n_1}{u}=\frac{n_2-n_1}{R}$, with $n_1=1$, $n_2=1.5$, $u=-6$ cm, $R=+24$ cm:
$\frac{1.5}{v}-\frac{1}{-6}=\frac{0.5}{24}$
$\frac{1.5}{v}=\frac{1}{48}-\frac{1}{6}=-\frac{7}{48}$
$v=-\frac{72}{7}\approx -10.3$ cm.
The image is virtual, formed $10.3$ cm from the surface on the same side as the object (in air).

questions.question: A ray of light MN is incident normally on the face corresponding with side AB of a prism with an isosceles right-angled triangular base ABC. Trace the path of the ray as it passes through the prism when the refractive index of the prism material is (i) $\sqrt{2}$, and (ii) $\sqrt{3}$.
questions.answer:
Since $MN$ is normal to $AB$, it enters without bending and strikes the hypotenuse $BC$ at an angle of incidence of $45°$.
(i) For $n=\sqrt{2}$: critical angle $C = \sin^{-1}(1/\sqrt{2}) = 45°$. As the angle of incidence equals $C$, the ray just grazes along $BC$, emerging at $90°$ to the normal.
(ii) For $n=\sqrt{3}$: $C = \sin^{-1}(1/\sqrt{3}) \approx 33.5°$, which is less than $45°$. So total internal reflection occurs at $BC$; the reflected ray then strikes $AC$ normally and emerges undeviated.

questions.question: A transparent solid cylindrical rod (refractive index $\sqrt{3}$) is kept in air. A ray of light incident on its face travels along the surface of the rod, as shown in figure. Calculate the angle $\theta$.
questions.answer:
Applying Snell's law at the flat face: $\sin\theta = \sqrt{3}\sin r$, where $r$ is the angle of refraction from the axis.
The refracted ray strikes the curved (lateral) surface at angle $(90°-r)$ to its normal.
Critical angle: $\sin C = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, so $C \approx 33.6°$.
The largest possible value of $r$ occurs at grazing incidence ($\theta=90°$), giving $r_{max}=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\approx 33.6°$, so the angle of incidence on the curved surface, $90°-r$, is always at least $56.4°$, which exceeds $C$.
Hence total internal reflection (light travelling along the surface) occurs for every angle $\theta$ from $0°$ to $90°$.

questions.question: A spherical convex surface of radius of curvature $R$ separates glass (refractive index $1.5$) from air. Light from a point source placed in air at distance $R/2$ from the surface falls on it. Find the position and nature of the image formed.
questions.answer:
Using $\frac{n_2}{v}-\frac{n_1}{u}=\frac{n_2-n_1}{R}$, with $n_1=1$ (air), $n_2=1.5$ (glass), $u=-R/2$:
$\frac{1.5}{v}-\frac{1}{-R/2}=\frac{0.5}{R}$
$\frac{1.5}{v}=\frac{0.5}{R}-\frac{2}{R}=-\frac{1.5}{R}$
$v=-R$.
The image is virtual, formed at a distance $R$ from the surface, on the same side as the object (in air).

questions.question: A double convex lens of glass has both faces of the same radius of curvature $17$ cm. Find its focal length if it is immersed in water. The refractive indices of glass and water are $1.5$ and $1.33$ respectively.
questions.answer:
Lens maker's formula: $\frac{1}{f}=\left(\frac{n_{glass}}{n_{water}}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)$, with $R_1=+17$ cm, $R_2=-17$ cm.
$\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}=\frac{2}{17}$ cm$^{-1}$
$\frac{n_{glass}}{n_{water}}-1=\frac{1.5}{1.33}-1=0.128$
$\frac{1}{f}=0.128\times\frac{2}{17}=0.0150$ cm$^{-1}$
$f \approx 66.5$ cm.

questions.question: Two concave lenses A and B, each of focal length 8.0 cm are arranged coaxially 16 cm apart as shown in figure. An object P is placed at a distance of 4.0 cm from A. Find the position and nature of the final image formed.
questions.answer:
For lens A ($f=-8$ cm, $u=-4$ cm): $\frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{f}+\frac{1}{u}=-\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{4}=-\frac{3}{8}$, so $v=-\frac{8}{3}$ cm.
This image $I_1$ (virtual, $\frac{8}{3}$ cm in front of A) acts as the object for lens B, at a distance $16+\frac{8}{3}=\frac{56}{3}$ cm from B.
For lens B ($f=-8$ cm, $u=-\frac{56}{3}$ cm): $\frac{1}{v}=-\frac{1}{8}-\frac{3}{56}=-\frac{5}{28}$, so $v=-5.6$ cm.
The final image is virtual and erect, formed $5.6$ cm from lens B (i.e., $10.4$ cm from A), between the two lenses.

questions.question: Two convex lenses A and B, each of focal length 10.0 cm, are mounted on an optical bench at 50.0 cm and 70.0 cm respectively. An object is mounted at 20.0 cm. Find the nature and position of the final image formed by the combination.
questions.answer:
For lens A: $u=-30$ cm, $f=10$ cm, so $\frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{f}+\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{10}-\frac{1}{30}=\frac{1}{15}$, giving $v=+15$ cm (image 65 cm from object, i.e. 5 cm before lens B).
For lens B: this image acts as object with $u=-5$ cm, $f=10$ cm, so $\frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{10}-\frac{1}{5}=-\frac{1}{10}$, giving $v=-10$ cm.
The final image is virtual, formed 10 cm to the left of lens B (i.e. at the 60 cm mark on the bench).

questions.question: A light beam converges at a point O. In the path of this beam, a concave lens of focal length 15 cm is placed at a distance of 10 cm before point O. The beam now converges at a point O’. Find the magnitude and the direction of shift OO’.
questions.answer:
The converging beam acts as a virtual object for the concave lens, so $u=+10$ cm, $f=-15$ cm.
Using $\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}$: $\frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{f}+\frac{1}{u}=-\frac{1}{15}+\frac{1}{10}=\frac{1}{30}$, so $v=+30$ cm.
The beam now converges 30 cm from the lens instead of 10 cm, so $OO' = 30-10 = 20$ cm, with $O'$ shifted away from the lens (beyond $O$).

questions.question: An equiconvex lens is made of glass of refractive index $1.55$. If the focal length of the lens is $15.0$ cm, calculate the radius of curvature of its surfaces.
questions.answer:
For an equiconvex lens, $R_1=R$, $R_2=-R$, so $\frac{1}{f}=(n-1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)=(n-1)\frac{2}{R}$.
$\frac{1}{15}=(1.55-1)\frac{2}{R}=\frac{1.1}{R}$
$R=1.1\times15=16.5$ cm.

questions.question: Find the focal length of plano-convex lens of refractive index $1.5$ and radius of curvature $10$ cm when it is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $1.25$.
questions.answer:
Using $\frac{1}{f}=\left(\frac{n_{lens}}{n_{medium}}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)$ with $R_1=10$ cm, $R_2=\infty$:
$\frac{1}{f}=\left(\frac{1.5}{1.25}-1\right)\frac{1}{10}=(0.2)(0.1)=0.02$ cm$^{-1}$
$f=50$ cm.

questions.question: The two surfaces of a biconvex lens are of radius of curvature ’ $R$’ each. Obtain the condition under which its focal length ’ $f$’ be equal to ’ $R$’. If one of the two surfaces of this lens is made plane, what will be the new focal length of the lens?
questions.answer:
For a biconvex lens, $R_1=R$, $R_2=-R$, so $\frac{1}{f}=(n-1)\frac{2}{R}$.
For $f=R$: $\frac{1}{R}=(n-1)\frac{2}{R}\Rightarrow n-1=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow n=1.5$.
If one surface is made plane ($R_2\to\infty$), $\frac{1}{f'}=(n-1)\frac{1}{R}=\frac{0.5}{R}$, giving $f'=2R$.

questions.question: (a) A point object is placed in air at a distance $R/3$ in front of a convex surface of radius of curvature $R$, separating air from a medium of refractive index $n (< 4)$. Find the nature and position of the image formed. OR (b) In Young’s double slit experimental set-up, the intensity of the central maximum is $I_{0}$. Calculate the intensity at a point where the path difference between two interfering waves is $\lambda/3$.
questions.answer:
(a) Using $\frac{n_2}{v}-\frac{n_1}{u}=\frac{n_2-n_1}{R}$ with $n_1=1$, $n_2=n$, $u=-\frac{R}{3}$:
$\frac{n}{v}+\frac{3}{R}=\frac{n-1}{R}\Rightarrow\frac{n}{v}=\frac{n-4}{R}\Rightarrow v=\frac{nR}{n-4}$
Since $n<4$, $v$ is negative, so the image is virtual, formed in the air (object) side at a distance $\frac{nR}{4-n}$ from the pole.
OR
(b) Phase difference $\phi=\frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\times\frac{\lambda}{3}=\frac{2\pi}{3}$.
$I=I_0\cos^2\left(\frac{\phi}{2}\right)=I_0\cos^2\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=I_0\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2=\frac{I_0}{4}$.

questions.question: A right angled isosceles glass prism $ABC$ is kept in contact with an equilateral triangular prism $DBC$ as shown in the figure. Both prisms are made of the same glass of refractive index $1$· $6$. Trace the path of the ray $MN$ incident normally on face $AB$ as it passes through the combination.
questions.answer:
Critical angle for the glass, $C=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{1.6}\right)\approx38.7°$.
Ray $MN$ enters face $AB$ normally and goes undeviated to strike the hypotenuse $AC$ at $45°$; since $45°>C$, total internal reflection occurs there, turning the ray by $90°$ towards face $BC$.
As $BC$ is a common interface between two prisms of the same refractive index, the ray passes straight through into prism $DBC$ without bending.
Inside $DBC$ it strikes the slant face at an angle less than $C$, so it refracts (bends away from the normal) and emerges from that face.

questions.question: A ray of light is incident on face $AB$ of a prism $ABC$ with angle of prism $A$ and emerges out from face $AC$. The prism is set in the position of minimum deviation with angle of deviation $\delta$. Find (i) the angle of incidence and (ii) the angle of refraction on face $AB$.
questions.answer:
At minimum deviation, $i_1=i_2=i$ and $r_1=r_2=\frac{A}{2}$.
Using $\delta=2i-A$: $i=\frac{A+\delta}{2}$
Angle of refraction on face $AB$: $r=\frac{A}{2}$.

questions.question: A tank is filled with a liquid of refractive index $\sqrt{2}$, up to a height of $30$ cm. A tiny bulb is glowing at the bottom of the tank. Calculate the diameter of an opaque disc floating symmetrically on the liquid surface that can cut off completely the light from the bulb that comes out of the liquid surface.
questions.answer:
For the light to be completely cut off, the disc must cover the cone of light that reaches the surface within the critical angle $C$, where $\sin C=\frac{1}{n}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\Rightarrow C=45°$.
Radius of the illuminated circle, $r=h\tan C=30\times\tan45°=30$ cm.
Diameter of the disc $=2r=60$ cm.

questions.question: (a) Using the mirror equation and the formula of magnification, deduce that "the virtual image produced by a convex mirror is always diminished in size and is located between the pole and the focus." OR (b) A convex lens of focal length $10$ cm, a concave lens of focal length $15$ cm and a third lens of unknown focal length are placed coaxially in contact. If the focal length of the combination is $+12$ cm, find the nature and focal length of the third lens, if all lenses are thin. Will the answer change if the lenses were thick?
questions.answer:
(a) For a convex mirror, $f$ is positive and a real object has $u$ negative.
From $\frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{f}-\frac{1}{u}$, since $-\frac{1}{u}>0$, we get $\frac{1}{v}>\frac{1}{f}$, so $0<v<f$, i.e. the image lies between the pole and focus.
Writing $v=\frac{fu}{u-f}=\frac{f|u|}{|u|+f}$ (positive, since $u<0,f>0$), which is always less than $f$.
Magnification $m=-\frac{v}{u}=\frac{f}{|u|+f}$, which is positive (erect, virtual) and less than $1$ (diminished) for all $|u|>0$.
OR
(b) $\frac{1}{f_{comb}}=\frac{1}{f_1}+\frac{1}{f_2}+\frac{1}{f_3}$
$\frac{1}{12}=\frac{1}{10}-\frac{1}{15}+\frac{1}{f_3}$
$\frac{1}{f_3}=\frac{1}{12}-\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{15}=\frac{5-6+4}{60}=\frac{1}{20}$
$f_3=+20$ cm, so the third lens is convex (converging).
If the lenses were thick, the simple additivity of powers would not hold since it ignores the separation between principal planes, so the answer would change.

questions.question: Monochromatic light of frequency $5.0\times10^{14}$ Hz passes from air into a medium of refractive index $1.5$. Find the wavelength of the light (i) reflected, and (ii) refracted at the interface of the two media.
questions.answer:
The reflected ray travels back in air, so its wavelength is unchanged.
$\lambda_{air} = c/\nu = (3\times10^8)/(5\times10^{14}) = 6\times10^{-7}$ m $= 600$ nm.
Refracted wavelength: $\lambda_{medium} = \lambda_{air}/n = 600/1.5 = 400$ nm.

questions.question: A plano-convex lens of focal length $16$ cm is made of a material of refractive index $1.4$. Calculate the radius of the curved surface of the lens.
questions.answer:
For a plano-convex lens, lens maker's formula gives $\frac{1}{f} = (n-1)\frac{1}{R}$, since the flat surface has $R_2=\infty$.
$R = (n-1)f = (1.4-1)\times16 = 6.4$ cm.

questions.question: An object is placed $30$ cm in front of a concave mirror of radius of curvature $40$ cm. Find the (i) position of the image formed and (ii) magnification of the image.
questions.answer:
Using the mirror formula $\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}$, with $f=R/2=-20$ cm and $u=-30$ cm:
$\frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{-20}-\frac{1}{-30} = -\frac{1}{60}$, so $v=-60$ cm.
(i) The image forms 60 cm in front of the mirror (real image).
(ii) $m = -v/u = -(-60)/(-30) = -2$; the image is real, inverted, and magnified twice.

questions.question: A ray of light passes through a triangular prism. Show graphically, how the angle of deviation varies with the angle of incidence? Hence define the angle of minimum deviation.
questions.answer:
As the angle of incidence $i$ increases from $0°$, the angle of deviation $\delta$ first decreases, reaches a minimum value $\delta_m$, and then increases again, giving a U-shaped curve.
The angle of minimum deviation is the particular deviation at which $i=e$ and $r_1=r_2=A/2$, with the ray inside the prism travelling parallel to its base.

questions.question: A ray of light is incident normally on a refracting face of a prism of prism angle $A$ and suffers a deviation of angle $\delta$. Prove that the refractive index $n$ of the material of the prism is given by $n = \frac{\sin(A + \delta)}{\sin A}$.
questions.answer:
Since the ray enters normally, $r_1=0$, so $r_2=A$ (as $r_1+r_2=A$).
Total deviation $\delta = i_1+e-A = e-A$ (since $i_1=0$), giving $e=A+\delta$.
Applying Snell's law at the emergent face: $n\sin r_2 = \sin e \Rightarrow n\sin A = \sin(A+\delta)$, so $n=\dfrac{\sin(A+\delta)}{\sin A}$.

questions.question: A convex lens (n = 1.52) has a focal length of 15.0 cm in air. Find its focal length when it is immersed in liquid of refractive index 1.65. What will be the nature of the lens?
questions.answer:
Lens maker's formula: $\frac{1}{f}=\left(\frac{n_{lens}}{n_{medium}}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)$.
In air: $\frac{1}{15}=(1.52-1)k \Rightarrow k=0.1282$ cm$^{-1}$.
In liquid: $\frac{1}{f'}=\left(\frac{1.52}{1.65}-1\right)k = (-0.0788)(0.1282)=-0.0101$, so $f' \approx -99$ cm.
Since $f'$ is negative, the lens now behaves as a diverging (concave) lens.

questions.question: The magnifying power of an astronomical telescope is $24$. In normal adjustment, distance between its two lenses is $150$ cm. Find the focal length of the objective lens.
questions.answer:
$M = f_o/f_e = 24$ and $L=f_o+f_e=150$ cm.
$f_o=24f_e \Rightarrow 25f_e=150 \Rightarrow f_e=6$ cm, so $f_o=144$ cm.

questions.question: Explain the following: (a) For a simple microscope, the angular size of the object equals the angular size of the image. Yet it offers magnification. (b) Both plane and convex mirrors produce virtual images of objects. Can they produce real images under some circumstances?
questions.answer:
(a) The magnifying power $M=D/f$ arises because the lens lets the object be placed closer than the near point $D$ (near the focal point), so it subtends a larger angle at the eye than it would at $D$ without the lens — even though the angular size of the image (measured at the lens) equals that of the object.
(b) For a real object, both mirrors always form virtual, erect images. However, if the incident rays are converging (a virtual object), both a plane mirror and a convex mirror can form a real image.

questions.question: A ray of light is incident normally on one face of an equilateral glass prism of refractive index $\mu$. When the prism is completely immersed in a transparent medium, it is observed that the emergent ray just grazes the adjacent face. Find the refractive index of the medium.
questions.answer:
Since incidence on the first face is normal, $r_1=0$, so $r_2=A=60°$.
The emergent ray grazing the surface means $e=90°$, i.e., $\sin e=1$.
Applying Snell's law at the second face (prism to medium): $\mu\sin r_2 = \mu_{medium}\sin e \Rightarrow \mu_{medium}=\mu\sin 60° = \frac{\sqrt3}{2}\mu$.

questions.question: An air bubble is trapped at point $B$ ($CB = 20$ cm) in a glass sphere of radius $40$ cm and refractive index $1.5$ as shown in figure. Find the nature and position of the image of the bubble as seen by an observer at point $P$.
questions.answer:
Using refraction at a spherical surface, with the pole at the surface nearer to $P$: object distance $u=-20$ cm, radius $R=-40$ cm, $n_1=1.5$ (glass, incidence side), $n_2=1$ (air).
$\frac{n_2}{v}-\frac{n_1}{u}=\frac{n_2-n_1}{R} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{v}+\frac{1.5}{20}=\frac{-0.5}{-40} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{v}=-0.0625$, so $v=-16$ cm.
The image is virtual, formed 16 cm from the curved surface on the same side as the bubble, i.e., it appears closer to the surface than the actual bubble position.

questions.question: In normal adjustment, for a refracting telescope, the distance between objective and eye piece lens is $1.00$ m. If the magnifying power of the telescope is $19$, find the focal length of the objective and the eyepiece lens.
questions.answer:
For a telescope in normal adjustment, $L = f_o + f_e = 100$ cm and $m = f_o/f_e = 19$.
So $f_o = 19f_e$, giving $19f_e + f_e = 100$, i.e. $20f_e = 100$.
$f_e = 5$ cm and $f_o = 19 \times 5 = 95$ cm.

questions.question: A telescope has an objective lens of focal length $150$ cm and an eyepiece of focal length $5$ cm. Calculate its magnifying power in normal adjustment and the distance of the image formed by the objective.
questions.answer:
Magnifying power in normal adjustment: $m = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e} = \dfrac{150}{5} = 30$.
Since the object is at infinity, the objective forms the image at its focus, so the distance of the image from the objective is $f_o = 150$ cm.

questions.question: The radius of curvature of a convex mirror is $30$ cm. It forms an image of an object which is half the size of the object. Find the separation between the object and the image.
questions.answer:
$R = 30$ cm, so $f = +15$ cm (convex mirror).
Since $m = 1/2$, using $m = -v/u$ gives $v = -u/2$; substituting in $\dfrac{1}{v}+\dfrac{1}{u}=\dfrac{1}{f}$: $-\dfrac{2}{u}+\dfrac{1}{u}=\dfrac{1}{15}$, so $u = -15$ cm and $v = 7.5$ cm.
The object is $15$ cm in front of the mirror and the (virtual) image is $7.5$ cm behind it.
Separation between object and image $= 15 + 7.5 = 22.5$ cm.

questions.question: A thin converging lens of focal length $10$ cm is placed coaxially in contact with a thin diverging lens of focal length $15$ cm. How will the combination behave? Justify your answer.
questions.answer:
For lenses in contact, $\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}+\dfrac{1}{f_2} = \dfrac{1}{10}-\dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{1}{30}$.
So $f = 30$ cm, which is positive.
The combination behaves as a converging (convex) lens of focal length $30$ cm.

questions.question: Why is a reflecting telescope preferred over a refracting telescope? Justify your answer giving two reasons.
questions.answer:
A reflecting telescope is preferred over a refracting telescope for two reasons:
It uses a mirror as the objective, which is free from chromatic aberration since reflection does not depend on wavelength.
A mirror can be made much larger and lighter (supported from behind) than a lens of the same aperture, giving a larger light-gathering power and better resolving power without sagging under its own weight.

questions.question: Briefly explain two applications of total internal reflection.
questions.answer:
Optical fibres: light entering the fibre undergoes repeated total internal reflection at the core-cladding boundary (since the core has higher refractive index) and travels along the fibre with negligible loss, used in communication and endoscopy.
Totally reflecting prisms: right-angled prisms used in binoculars and periscopes reflect light through $90^\circ$ or $180^\circ$ by total internal reflection, giving brighter, sharper images than silvered mirrors since there is no absorption loss.

questions.question: Define total internal reflection of light. Give two conditions for it.
questions.answer:
Total internal reflection is the phenomenon in which light travelling from a denser to a rarer medium is entirely reflected back into the denser medium at the interface, with no refracted ray.
Conditions: (1) Light must travel from an optically denser medium to a rarer medium.
(2) The angle of incidence in the denser medium must be greater than the critical angle $\theta_c$ for that pair of media, where $\sin\theta_c = 1/n$.

questions.question: A double-convex lens of power $4$ D is manufactured from a glass of refractive index $1.5$. What is the radius of curvature of each face of this lens if both faces have the same radius of curvature?
